items.name: Swedish reggae
items.lineage: Swedish reggae connects reggae’s rhythmic and song traditions with Sweden’s local music scenes, including Swedish-language roots-reggae writing. Its arrangements range from band-led song to studio production while sharing the interplay of bass, rhythm and vocal expression.
items.description: A grounded bass-and-drum pattern supports guitar or keyboard offbeats, with lead singing and backing voices shaping refrains. Flute and horn lines can add melodic counterpoint in expanded arrangements. The Swedish-language roots branch illustrates how this musical vocabulary supports local expression; its instrumentation is representative rather than a requirement for every artist in the wider scene.

items.name: Swiss reggae
items.lineage: Swiss reggae is a regional reggae field built through local bands, labels and performance communities. Musicians combine Jamaican-derived grooves and song structures with their own material, from roots-oriented arrangements to other contemporary reggae approaches.
items.description: Lead and backing singing sit over bass, drums and offbeat guitar. Piano and organ add chordal weight and rhythmic replies, while trombone and other horns supply melodic colour. The interaction of bass movement, drum accents and clipped accompaniment creates the groove. Swiss bands and local recording communities adapt this musical vocabulary through their own songs and arrangements.

items.name: Uk reggae
items.lineage: UK reggae grew through Britain’s Caribbean communities, local bands, recording studios and sound-system culture. Roots groups and producers such as Talisman and Dennis Bovell connect Jamaican musical foundations with British social experience and an enduring vocal-and-dub record tradition.
items.description: Bass and drums establish the groove, with clipped guitar and keyboard chords marking offbeats around the singer. Horn parts and backing voices enrich some arrangements. Lyrics encompass community life, social criticism and personal themes; instrumental dub versions rearrange the same musical materials through mixing. The interplay between band performance, studio production and sound-system listening is central to the British scene.
exemplars: Talisman — Don’t Play with Fyah, Dennison Joseph title-track branch

items.name: Trinidadian reggae
items.lineage: Trinidadian reggae brings reggae songwriting and performance into Trinidadian musical life and its diaspora. Artists combine the shared vocabulary of Jamaican-derived rhythm with local stories, personal expression and contemporary production.
items.description: Lead singing and vocal responses sit over bass, drums and offbeat guitar or keyboard accompaniment. A firm low end and rhythmic space give the words room, while instrumental replies connect phrases. Diaspora artists such as John Blood carry Trinidadian storytelling into band and studio reggae, linking regional identity with an international musical practice.
exemplars: John Blood — The Journey, track 3 ensemble branch

items.name: UK dub
items.lineage: UK dub developed through Britain’s reggae studios and sound systems, making the mixing desk and effects part of musical composition. It extends Jamaican versioning practices through local producers, musicians and dedicated bass-focused listening cultures.
items.description: Bass and drums remain central as voices and instruments enter, disappear and return in altered perspective. Echo, reverberation and selective emphasis reshape guitar, keyboard, horn and melodica phrases into shifting layers. Performances range from band-recorded foundations to electronically assembled productions; the decisive feature is the active recomposition of recorded material through space, repetition and contrast.
exemplars: Nat Birchall / Al Breadwinner — Tradition Disc In Dub

items.name: Virgin islands reggae
items.lineage: Virgin Islands reggae includes a strong roots-reggae tradition associated with St. Croix and local recording communities. Artists such as Vaughn Benjamin and the I Grade network connect reflective singing and roots production with the islands’ contemporary musical identity.
items.description: A resonant bass line and measured drum groove support the singer, while guitar and keyboards provide offbeat chords. Horn melodies can add responses and depth to the arrangement. The roots-oriented sound gives particular weight to vocal delivery, rhythmic patience and the relationship between the song and its accompanying groove.
exemplars: Vaughn Benjamin / Akae Beka — Exalt the Crown

items.name: Aarhus indie
items.lineage: Aarhus indie is the independent music scene associated with Aarhus, Denmark. Its bands and producers work across guitar music, electronic textures and song-based or instrumental composition, linked through a shared local creative community.
items.description: Electric guitars, synthesizers, keyboards and drums can combine in layered arrangements ranging from melodic song to atmospheric instrumental passages. Groups such as Gaardens illustrate the interaction of guitars and electronic colour. The regional label connects varied approaches through place and independent music-making, while individual artists shape their own balance of rhythm, texture and melody.

items.name: Aberdeen indie
items.lineage: Aberdeen indie comprises independent bands and artists associated with Aberdeen, Scotland. Guitar-led songwriting and electronic or keyboard colour meet within a local scene connected to wider Scottish indie music.
items.description: Lead singing and backing voices sit over guitar, bass and drums, while keyboards add harmonic and textural layers. Arrangements balance song melodies with rhythmic drive and contrasting instrumental sections. Bands such as The Little Kicks exemplify the combination of vocal songwriting, guitars and keys that contributes to the city’s indie sound.

Guitar, bass, drums, piano and electronic keyboards support arrangements that range from bright rhythmic pop to ballads. Graduates such as Sayaka Yamamoto also extend this repertory into solo, guitar-led work, connecting group performance with individual musical careers.

items.name: Swedish dancehall
items.lineage: Swedish dancehall developed through local engagement with Jamaican reggae and dancehall, alongside hip-hop and international sound-system culture. Artists such as Million Stylez carried the scene into Jamaican competitions and worldwide club circulation.
items.description: Rhythmic singing and deejay delivery ride bass-heavy grooves, with digital production and live reggae-band accompaniment both contributing to the scene.

items.name: Dub brasileiro
items.lineage: Dub brasileiro connects Jamaican mixing practices with Brazilian instrumental music and local rhythmic traditions. In projects such as Bixiga 70’s work with Victor Rice, ensemble recordings become material for spacious, bass-centred studio transformations.

items.name: Reggae mexicano
items.lineage: Reggae mexicano belongs to Mexico’s intertwined reggae, ska and live-band scenes. Groups such as Mexico City’s Girls Go Ska combine melodic singing with offbeat guitar, strong bass lines and saxophone arrangements.

items.name: Bedroom soul
items.lineage: Bedroom soul brings soul-influenced singing into intimate, small-scale songwriting and recording. Sparse guitar accompaniment and close vocal presentation sit alongside the personal, home-produced character of the music.

items.name: Blues latinoamericano
items.lineage: Blues latinoamericano grows from the adaptation of blues within Latin American musical communities. Local bands combine its vocal expression, guitar language and ensemble grooves with their own songwriting and regional scenes; Chile’s La Rata Bluesera is one example.

items.name: Dutch blues
items.lineage: Dutch blues grew through the Netherlands’ blues and rhythm-and-blues bands of the 1960s, including Cuby + Blizzards, and continues through clubs, festivals and national musician networks. Acoustic duos and amplified bands sustain different sides of the repertoire.

items.name: Finnish blues
items.lineage: Finnish blues has developed through performers, clubs, record releases and the Finnish Blues Society’s long-running support network. Acoustic singer-guitarists such as Jantso Jokelin continue a storytelling strand alongside amplified ensembles.
items.description: Bent harmonica phrases, fingerpicked accompaniment and sliding guitar notes shape the acoustic side of Finnish blues. Singing carries narrative verses, with instrumental replies and recurring blues patterns supporting flexible phrasing.

items.name: Funk mexicano
items.lineage: Mexican funk connects groove-based band music with local and wider Afro-Latin musical currents. Ensembles such as Som Bit combine original songwriting, African and Latin American rhythms, jazz elements and dance-oriented performance.

items.name: German blues

items.name: Japanese blues

items.description: Expressive vocals and bending or sliding guitar phrases work with recurring blues patterns and rhythmic accompaniment. Solo and small-group performances foreground phrasing, while electric bands extend the sound through amplification and stronger rhythmic drive.

items.name: Japanese R&B
items.lineage: Japanese R&B connects soul and rhythm-and-blues influences with local pop, hip-hop and independent music communities. Artists such as SIRUP move between singing and rap, while other projects explore hybrid band textures and alternative songwriting.
items.description: Vocal melodies, rhythmic phrasing and grooves shape the songs. Keyboards, bass, drums, guitars and electronic production provide flexible backing, from sparse accompaniment to layered arrangements with harmonies and contrasting textures.

items.name: Kenyan R&B
items.lineage: Kenyan R&B develops through singers, producers and collaborative networks, including Nairobi artists such as Karun and Jinku. Contemporary soul and electronic production support personal songwriting about relationships, identity and emotional change.
items.description: Expressive melodic singing moves over flexible grooves, guitar and bass lines, and studio-built textures. Layered voices and atmospheric accompaniment can create intimate or expansive settings around recurring hooks and narrative verses.

items.name: Latin funk
items.lineage: Latin funk brings funk grooves into dialogue with Latin American and Caribbean rhythmic practices. Bands such as Ex Romantika combine horn-led ensemble writing with dance-oriented rhythm sections and percussion.
items.description: Syncopated bass and guitar figures interlock with drums, congas and timbales. Horn riffs, electric-keyboard chords and vocal refrains reinforce recurring grooves, while ensemble breaks and instrumental passages create contrast.

items.name: MPB gospel
items.lineage: MPB gospel brings Brazilian popular songwriting into Christian devotional music. Performers such as Marcelo Dias e Fabiana connect personal reflection and everyday relationships with faith, alongside the wider Brazilian gospel recording circuit.
items.description: Melodic singing and acoustic-guitar accompaniment support intimate songs with clear refrains and reflective lyrics. Solo and duet voices can give the music a conversational quality, while gospel inflections intensify important phrases.

items.name: Retro soul
items.lineage: Retro soul revisits earlier soul, rhythm-and-blues and gospel traditions through contemporary bands and recordings. Revival groups such as The Congregation draw on the expressive singing and ensemble sound associated with Otis Redding, Aretha Franklin and Ike and Tina Turner.
items.description: Powerful lead vocals, horn figures and rhythmic guitar or keyboard accompaniment ride over bass and drums. Blues inflections, ensemble responses and a live-band feel connect polished song forms with rawer garage-soul textures.

items.name: R&B italiano

items.description: Melodic leads and layered backing voices sit over bass, drums, guitars and keyboards. Smooth vocal phrases can contrast with distorted guitar textures, while recurring hooks and changes in arrangement shape the songs.

items.name: Scandinavian R&B

items.name: Ugandan gospel
items.lineage: Ugandan gospel grows through church worship, devotional songwriting and local recording projects. Kampala initiatives such as Songs To Glory create praise music for congregations, combining personal testimony with messages of thanksgiving, healing and salvation.

items.name: South African gospel
items.lineage: South African gospel developed through church communities and the encounter between Christian hymnody and local singing traditions. Its multilingual choral traditions coexist with contemporary worship bands, soloists and Afrikaans devotional songwriting.
items.description: Rich vocal harmonies, repeated responses and rhythmic communal singing are prominent. Choirs may combine movement and percussion, while smaller worship arrangements use piano or guitar to support melodic leads and congregational refrains.

items.name: Swedish soul
items.lineage: Swedish soul connects American soul traditions with Swedish songwriting and collaborative music scenes. Artists such as Tingsek have developed a personal approach through recordings and international collaborations since the early 2000s.

items.name: R&B argentino

items.name: R&B brasileiro

items.description: Sung melodies ride syncopated bass and drum grooves, with guitar figures and horn riffs supplying rhythmic answers. Live-band arrangements, studio edits and remixes provide different settings for recurring hooks and instrumental passages.

items.name: Sertanejo gospel
items.lineage: Sertanejo gospel brings Brazilian country-song traditions into Christian praise and devotional music. Singing duos such as Cláudio & Márlon connect the melodic language of traditional sertanejo with contemporary gospel repertory.
items.description: Paired voices, acoustic-guitar accompaniment and memorable refrains carry themes of faith, blessing and religious commitment. Close vocal interplay and rhythmic strumming support both reflective songs and more outwardly celebratory praise.

items.name: Traditional soul
items.lineage: Traditional soul sustains the expressive singing and band-based songwriting of earlier soul and rhythm and blues. Contemporary performers such as Quentin Moore draw on Southern soul while placing its vocal and instrumental language in modern recordings.

exemplars: Quentin Moore — Kiss Your Lips (September 2025 single)

items.name: Samba gospel
items.lineage: Samba gospel combines Brazilian samba and pagode ensemble practice with Christian devotional repertory. Groups such as São Paulo’s Restaurados Pela Fé bring gospel messages into community-oriented singing and rhythmic group performance.
items.description: Lead and backing voices alternate with repeated refrains over interlocking percussion. Cavaquinho and acoustic guitar supply chordal rhythm, supported by bass, pandeiro and other percussion; some groups add drum kit.
exemplars: Grupo Restaurados Pela Fé — documented vocal ensemble and named instrument roles

items.name: Vintage gospel
items.lineage: Vintage gospel brings together historical recordings of Christian spirituals and gospel, including soloists, vocal quartets, choirs and guitar evangelists. Archival repertories preserve the diverse African American devotional practices heard in early commercial recordings.
items.description: Expressive leads, group harmonies and repeated responses carry sacred texts. Unaccompanied voices coexist with guitar-backed singing and other instrumental settings, with speech-like emphasis, sustained tones and ornamented phrases shaping the delivery.
exemplars: Blind Willie Harris — Where He Leads Me I Will Follow (c. February 1929)

items.name: South African R&B
items.lineage: South African R&B connects soul and rhythm-and-blues songwriting with local and transnational production networks. Projects such as Thaba explore connections with electronic music, dub and neighbouring southern African musical communities.
items.description: Sung melodies and layered textures combine with guitar, keyboards and rhythm-section grooves. Saxophone and percussion can add contrasting lines and rhythmic detail, while studio production creates space around reflective vocal phrases.
exemplars: Thaba — MMoloki (2025), Lollise Mbi vocal version

items.name: Zim gospel
items.lineage: Zimbabwean gospel develops through church ensembles, praise groups and contemporary devotional recording. Groups such as The Unveiled combine lead singers and arranged vocal sections with instrumental accompaniment.
items.description: Lead melodies and choral responses carry praise texts, with layered harmonies giving refrains collective force. Keyboards, guitars, bass and drums support contemporary band arrangements, ranging from reflective worship to more emphatic praise.
exemplars: The Unveiled — Hallelujah Hossana (official December 2024 video)

items.name: Acoustic chill
items.lineage: Acoustic chill brings acoustic songwriting and instrumental textures into relaxed contemporary listening. Collaborations such as paulfcook and With Sun connect singer-songwriter intimacy with understated studio production.
items.description: Unhurried melodic phrases and gentle guitar accompaniment create a reflective atmosphere. Sparse keyboard or reed-instrument lines can add colour without crowding the voice, with restrained dynamics and open space between gestures.
exemplars: paulfcook x With Sun — I Can't Look Up (2025)

items.name: Acoustic cover
items.lineage: Acoustic covers reinterpret existing songs through acoustic performance. Solo musicians and small ensembles adapt familiar vocal melodies and harmonic progressions, circulating their versions through live performance and independent recordings.
items.description: A singing voice and acoustic guitar often carry the arrangement, with strumming or picked figures supporting the melody. Reduced accompaniment brings attention to lyrics, phrasing and changes in dynamics while preserving recognisable features of the song.
exemplars: Ryan Keller — Tenerife Sea (Ed Sheeran Cover), 2014 single

items.name: Acoustic guitar cover
items.lineage: Acoustic guitar covers translate songs and instrumental themes into guitar-led arrangements. Classical-guitar performers and other acoustic players adapt repertory from popular music, films and television for solo or small-ensemble performance.
items.description: Picked strings carry melody, bass movement and chordal accompaniment, often combining these functions within one instrument. Resonance, articulation and changes in register give familiar material a distinct acoustic shape.
exemplars: Gene Akimoff — Game of Thrones Titles Theme Cover, Classical Guitar Favorites (2017)

items.name: Adelaide indie
items.lineage: Adelaide indie comprises independent bands and songwriters working through the city’s local recording and performance networks. Groups such as Console Warriors develop alternative and indie-rock songs within this South Australian scene.
items.description: Guitar, bass and drums support sung melodies and recurring hooks in a common band format. Rhythmic interplay, contrasting guitar textures and changes in intensity give compact songs room for both melodic and more forceful passages.
exemplars: Console Warriors — The Jitterblood Mini EP (2013), release-credited ensemble

items.name: Adventista
items.lineage: Adventist music forms part of the worldwide Seventh-day Adventist community’s worship and musical life. Congregational singing, choirs and smaller groups connect sacred texts with local musical cultures and church education.
items.description: Clear vocal presentation and attention to devotional words are central. Unaccompanied and instrumentally supported singing coexist, with piano accompaniment offering one familiar setting for choral harmony and shared melodic lines.
exemplars: Badalona Adventist singers — Padre Nuestro in Catalan at Barcelona Plaça Espanya station, November 2024

items.name: Alabama indie
items.lineage: Alabama indie connects independent bands and songwriters across the state’s local scenes. Birmingham groups such as LoveRat bring rock songwriting into dialogue with roots-oriented influences through self-directed recording and performance.
items.description: Sung hooks and narrative verses work with guitars, bass, drums and keyboards. Band arrangements use recurring grooves, vocal interplay and contrasts between more restrained passages and forceful choruses.

items.name: Afrikaans
items.lineage: Afrikaans music encompasses songwriting and performance across the language’s diverse communities. Platforms such as ATKV-Crescendo support its varied voices, while artists move among acoustic song, popular music, rock and other styles.
items.description: Lyrics and vocal expression link otherwise varied musical approaches. Intimate voice-and-guitar songs, harmonised group singing and amplified bands offer different settings for storytelling, reflection and memorable refrains.

items.name: Adoracion
items.lineage: Adoración centres on Spanish-language Christian worship and devotional song. Church communities and music ministries develop repertories for shared praise, combining translated hymns with contemporary songwriting.
items.description: Melodic leads and backing voices carry repeated refrains and praise texts. Acoustic and electric guitars, percussion or other band accompaniment support congregational singing, with dynamics shaped around the words and recurring responses.
exemplars: Sovereign Grace Music — Todo lo que Creó el Rey (2025 single)

items.name: Aggro chileno
items.lineage: Aggro chileno emerged through Chile’s alternative-metal scene during the 1990s. Groups such as Rékiem combined heavy international influences with local band networks, and events such as Aggrofest helped bring the scene together.
items.description: Distorted guitar riffs, electric bass and forceful drums support intense vocals. Heavy rhythmic passages can contrast with melody and atmosphere, linking metal weight with the alternative and nu-metal language associated with the scene.

items.name: Afrobeat fusion
items.lineage: Afrobeat fusion connects Afrobeat-oriented ensemble grooves with other musical approaches, including rock, electronic production and instrumental fusion. Groups such as Elephant Hump develop hybrid textures within this open-ended field.
items.description: Interlocking rhythm-section figures support repeating melodies and instrumental exchanges. Guitar, bass, drums and percussion can combine with horns, flute and electronic layers, using repetition, timbral contrast and changing ensemble density.

items.name: Accordion
items.lineage: Accordion music encompasses solo and ensemble repertories built around the instrument’s bellows-driven reeds. Dance traditions and song accompaniment coexist with composed concert pieces; duos such as Accordéon Mélancolique develop original works for paired instruments.
items.description: Bellows shape phrasing and dynamics while melody, bass and chords can sound together. Register combinations alter the reed colour, and arrangements range from chordal accompaniment to interwoven independent lines.

items.name: Accordion band
items.lineage: Accordion bands develop arranged ensemble repertories through community groups and concert organisations. Piano-key and button instruments can play differentiated parts, with bass and keyboard players extending the ensemble’s range.
items.description: Reed sections distribute melodic, harmonic and accompaniment lines, using bellows articulation and register contrasts to balance the texture. Repertory can move among popular songs, film themes, dance music and concert arrangements; some bands add winds or vocal groups.
exemplars: Bradford Accordion Band — arranged mixed-accordion ensemble practice

items.name: Acoustic OPM
items.lineage: Acoustic OPM brings Philippine popular songs into acoustic performance settings. Solo singers and smaller groups develop intimate or rhythmically direct versions, drawing on local songwriting and the wider Original Pilipino Music repertory.
items.description: Voice and guitar lead many arrangements, while bass and cajon can provide a compact rhythmic foundation. Strummed or picked accompaniment leaves space for lyrics and melodic phrasing, with some groups retaining the energy of a larger band.

items.name: Adoración pentecostal
items.lineage: Adoración pentecostal develops through Spanish-speaking Pentecostal churches and their praise repertories. Hymns and contemporary songs express resurrection, salvation and shared faith through congregational and recorded worship.
items.description: Lead voices and supporting singers carry recurring devotional phrases over piano, guitars and rhythm-section accompaniment. Changes in dynamics and vocal intensity give room to both reflective hymn singing and more emphatic praise.

items.name: Afro psych
items.lineage: Afro psych connects African popular music with psychedelic rock, funk and experimental studio approaches. Lagos was an important centre during the 1970s, with artists such as the Lijadu Sisters and releases on Afrodisia contributing to a wider network of hybrid sounds.
items.description: Insistent bass grooves and percussion meet fuzz guitar, keyboards, horns or synthesizers. Repeated vocal phrases and instrumental passages can expand into exploratory textures, with changes in timbre and density shaping the music.
exemplars: Lijadu Sisters — Bayi L’ense (1977), Africa Seven Afro Psych

items.name: Afro-Cuban percussion
items.lineage: Afro-Cuban percussion connects distinct rhythmic traditions with dance bands, teaching and contemporary performance. Congas, bongos and timbales form an important ensemble practice, with musicians such as Victor Rendón teaching their complementary functions.
items.description: Interlocking hand and stick patterns divide rhythmic tasks among instruments. Open tones, muted strokes, slaps and metallic accents create contrasting attacks; clave-related organisation and shifts between accompaniment and solo phrases shape many arrangements.
exemplars: Victor Rendón — The Art Of Playing Timbales (2022), conga/bongo examples

items.name: Afrobeat brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian Afrobeat brings the ensemble language of Afrobeat into dialogue with Afro-Brazilian rhythmic traditions. Rio de Janeiro groups such as Abayomy Orquestra connect this practice with ijexá, coco, afoxé and maracatu, alongside jazz and Yoruba-language song.
items.description: Interlocking guitar and bass figures, drums and percussion support layered vocal responses and horn arrangements. Keyboards enrich the texture, while repeated rhythmic patterns leave room for instrumental exchanges and changes in ensemble density.

items.name: AI
items.lineage: AI music uses computational systems to generate musical material from learned patterns. Systems such as MuseNet and Magenta contributed to experiments in generated composition and performance, including piano releases by Aleksandr Sigalov.
items.description: The field spans contrasting styles and instrument combinations. In its solo-piano branch, generated melodic figures and arpeggios unfold over harmonic patterns; the resulting material can be presented through a piano timbre or developed into a performed arrangement.
exemplars: Aleksandr Sigalov — OpenAI’s MuseNet Artificial Intelligence Piano Performances

items.name: Åländsk musik
items.lineage: Åländsk musik encompasses musical activity associated with the Åland Islands, including local bands and a varied concert and festival culture. LAMORI, founded in 2009, represents a modern gothic-rock and metal strand within that regional scene.
items.description: Styles range across the region’s performers and events. The gothic-rock branch combines sung melody with electric guitar, bass, drums and keyboard textures, balancing weighty riffs with atmospheric passages.

items.name: Alaska indie
items.lineage: Alaska’s independent music scene links local communities with touring and collaborative networks beyond the state. Anchorage bands such as Termination Dust connect guitar-based songwriting with DIY recording, drawing on indie rock, emo and pop approaches.
items.description: Layered guitars and drums can support overlapping sung parts, with contrasting vocal textures giving songs a conversational quality. Arrangements range from quieter passages to more forceful sections, and some groups extend the palette with electronic instruments.

items.name: Albanian alternative
items.lineage: Albanian alternative music includes bands working beyond mainstream pop conventions, with Tirana serving as one centre of activity. Into Thin Air connects this scene with post-rock and progressive-rock approaches through guitar, bass and drums.
items.description: Instrumental passages develop through recurring guitar figures, bass movement and changing drum patterns. Vocals appear in some work, while extended textures and shifts in intensity allow the instrumental ensemble to carry the musical development.
exemplars: Into Thin Air — Fibonacci Sequence EP, instrumental band-core selection

items.name: Albany NY indie
items.lineage: Albany’s independent rock scene includes bands working across indie rock, emo, punk and related styles. Groups such as Scotchka connect guitar-led songwriting with the city’s recording and live-music community.
items.description: Lead and rhythm guitars work over bass and drums, supporting expressive vocals and recurring song sections. Melodic passages can give way to heavier attacks, with changes in intensity reinforcing lyrical tension.

items.name: Albuquerque indie
items.lineage: Albuquerque indie encompasses local independent bands and recording activity. The Ordinary Things represents a guitar-centred strand whose songwriting combines everyday observations with a wider instrumental palette.
items.description: Layered vocals meet guitar riffs, bass movement and drums. Synthesizers and brass can extend the texture, while contrasts between softer singing and sharper instrumental attacks shape the arrangements.

items.name: Bangla gojol
items.lineage: Bangla gojol is a Bengali-language Islamic devotional song practice, including praise repertory circulated through performers, religious communities and specialist publishers. Vocal-only nasheed releases form one strand of this field.
items.description: The sung devotional text leads the musical presentation. Unaccompanied performances foreground melodic phrasing and the singer’s articulation, with repeated phrases supporting reflection and participation.
exemplars: KMY — Ogo Maula (lyrics), Bangla Gojol (Hamd), vocal-only branch

items.name: Bangladeshi indie
items.lineage: Bangladeshi indie includes independently produced song and band music, with artists combining local-language expression and varied rock influences. Dhaka’s Blunderware draws together Bengali song, folk, blues and alternative approaches.
items.description: Acoustic renditions place the sung line over a repeating guitar figure or strummed accompaniment. The wider band practice expands these ideas through rock arrangements, while lyrical repetition and melodic contours give the songs their shape.
exemplars: Rushnaf Wadud / Blunderware — Afim Chaash, acoustic live branch

items.name: Baoulé
items.lineage: Baoulé music in Côte d’Ivoire is closely connected with dance, storytelling, community celebrations and religious ceremonies. Vocal traditions coexist with drumming, horns, flutes, xylophones and harp playing, documented in community recordings collected by Donald Thurow.
items.description: Singers and choruses interact through repeated phrases and rhythmic responses. Some vocal performances imitate instrumental music, while dance repertories combine voices with contrasting percussion and melodic instruments.
exemplars: The Baoulé of the Ivory Coast — track212, Vocal, with Chorus (1956)

items.name: Alpenpanorama
items.lineage: Alpenpanorama brings together Alpine folk and popular-folk repertories associated with regional and family music-making. Allgäu ensembles such as Familienmusik Paulsteiner combine singing with changing instrumental groups for local performances and recordings.
items.description: Paired singing, accordion and guitar provide one familiar texture. Other arrangements draw on hammered dulcimer, harp, bowed strings and brass, with the balance of voices, melody and accompaniment changing across the repertory.
exemplars: Familienmusik Paulsteiner — Alpenpanorama (2017); documented duet, accordion and guitar core

items.name: Alternative ccm
items.lineage: Alternative CCM connects contemporary Christian music audiences with alternative rock. Bands such as San Diego’s Switchfoot developed a following across both markets, bringing spiritually engaged songwriting into guitar-led rock performance.
items.description: Anthemic vocals rise over guitar, bass and drums, with keyboards adding texture. Melodic hooks and changes between restrained passages and stronger ensemble sections give the songs their shape.
exemplars: Switchfoot — documented alternative Christian rock band roles

items.name: Ambeat
items.lineage: Ambeat combines ambient music with beat-oriented production. Japanese trumpeter and producer konb uses the term for music connecting synthesizer atmosphere, a defined rhythmic pulse and instrumental melody.
items.description: Floating synthesizer textures sit over tightly organised beats. Trumpet phrases add a human melodic contour, balancing sustained electronic layers with clear rhythmic attacks.

items.name: American early music
items.lineage: American early music includes colonial-era repertory and its historically informed revival. Early song composers such as Francis Hopkinson drew on European models while contributing to musical life in the American colonies.
items.description: Voice and keyboard accompaniment form one strand of the repertory. In eighteenth-century songs, a written melody and bass could leave harmonic detail to the accompanist, with graceful phrasing, passing notes and short instrumental passages shaping the performance.
exemplars: Francis Hopkinson — My Days Have Been So Wondrous Free, AMRC0015 track1 soprano/harpsichord version

items.name: American oi
items.lineage: American Oi! developed within US street-punk scenes influenced by British Oi! and related punk traditions. Long Island’s Templars, founded in 1990, connect this lineage with 1970s punk, early British rock and metal influences.
items.description: Direct vocal delivery and electric-guitar riffs drive concise songs over a forceful drum pulse. Bass and additional guitar parts fill out many band arrangements, while economical early lineups also form part of the scene’s history.
exemplars: The Templars — original documented Carl/Phil duo branch

items.lineage: Ancient Mediterranean music is explored through surviving notation, historical evidence and reconstructed instruments. items.name: Andean flute
items.lineage: Andean flute music includes distinct Indigenous and regional wind traditions, with the quena playing an important role in Andean communities. Archival recordings document Aymara quena performance in Bolivia, including music associated with San Lorenzo.
items.description: Breath-shaped melodic lines and articulated attacks carry the flute part, sometimes with drum accompaniment. Register, phrasing and the relationship between melody and rhythmic support vary with the local repertory and performance setting.
exemplars: Aymara quena player — San Lorenzo Quena Music, Folkways anthology track34

items.name: Animal singing
items.lineage: Animal singing uses recorded animal vocalisations as musical material. Novelty projects such as Jingle Cats organise these sounds into recognisable songs through recording and electronic arrangement.
items.description: Edited animal calls carry melodies, with timing and pitch shaping their musical role. The distinctive attacks and changing textures of the calls remain audible within the arrangement.
exemplars: Jingle Cats — digitally arranged recorded cat meows

items.name: Anime cv
items.lineage: Anime character songs connect fictional characters with the performers who voice them. Japanese anime music labels release these songs under character names and character-voice credits, including both solo characters and combinations of cast members.
items.description: Singing brings a character’s personality into melodic songs, extending the dramatic world beyond spoken dialogue. Solo and shared vocal presentations give individual characters and their relationships a musical presence.
exemplars: Gareki (CV: Hiroshi Kamiya) — Karneval Character SongVol5, Reach for the sky (LACM14105)

items.name: Anime game
items.lineage: Anime and game music circulates through soundtracks, song releases and arrangements for listening outside the original screen setting. Japanese game publishers also develop concert and piano collections, with Final Fantasy providing a prominent example.
items.description: Recognisable themes move between dramatic cues, songs and instrumental arrangements. In the piano branch, melodic lines and harmonic accompaniment bring music associated with characters and locations into a solo performance.

items.name: Anime latino
items.lineage: Latin American anime music grew around Spanish-language television themes and the performers who brought them to regional audiences. Singers such as Adrián Barba continue this repertory through new recordings, collaborations and fan-convention performances across Latin America.
items.description: Familiar sung melodies connect television memories with contemporary pop and rock arrangements. Electric-guitar reinterpretations add rhythmic drive while audiences recognise and sing along with the Spanish lyrics.

items.name: Apostolic worship
items.lineage: Apostolic worship music is cultivated in Pentecostal church communities through congregational songs, choirs and instrumental practice. Teachers such as Richard W. Smith sustain practical church musicianship rooted in gospel and contemporary worship traditions.

items.name: Arab alternative
items.lineage: Arab alternative music brings regional and diasporic histories into independent musical expression. Palestinian-rooted projects such as DUNUMS connect memories of home, political experience and collaborative experimentation across places.

items.name: Canadian latin
items.lineage: Latin American diasporic music in Canada carries regional traditions into local performing and recording communities. Toronto’s OKAN draws on Cuban roots while working across Latin and jazz settings.
items.description: Singing, piano, bass and percussion support rhythmic arrangements that may add violin, brass, woodwinds or guitar. Interlocking accompaniment and melodic improvisation connect dance, song and jazz-oriented performance.
exemplars: OKAN — Espiral, piano-and-vocal core of Pie de Foto

items.name: Canadian soundtrack
items.lineage: Canadian screen music brings composers and songwriters into film, television and audiovisual production. The field includes original dramatic scores, songs and experimental approaches to image and sound.
items.description: Music follows the pacing, atmosphere and dramatic needs of the screen work. Acoustic instruments and electronic textures can be combined: flute colors and synthesizer drones form one exploratory approach alongside broader scoring practices.
exemplars: Ice Locus — Breath of the Loci Soundtrack

items.name: Canberra indie
items.lineage: Canberra’s independent music develops through local artists and performance spaces such as Smith’s Alternative. Singer-songwriters including Kim Yang connect folk-oriented writing with collaborative live-band arrangements.
items.description: Expressive singing and personal lyrics sit among keyboards, bass and drums, with acoustic colors such as cello and flute in some ensembles. Close storytelling can expand into layered band passages and supporting vocal lines.
exemplars: Kim Yang — Live at Smith’s Alternative

items.name: Cancion infantil mexicana
items.lineage: Mexican children’s music connects familiar rounds and play songs with contemporary recording and performance. Groups such as Tripas de Gato revisit this repertoire through jazz arrangements.
items.description: Recognizable melodies and playful lyrics remain central while accompaniment ranges from simple song settings to ensemble arrangements. Jazz-oriented interpretations use singing, guitar, saxophone, bass and drums to renew songs associated with childhood games.
exemplars: Tripas de gato — Jazzeando las rondas

items.name: Cancoes infantis
items.lineage: Portuguese-language children’s songs connect play, learning and family listening. In Brazil, Palavra Cantada has developed a contemporary repertoire through the songwriting and performances of Sandra Peres and Paulo Tatit.
items.description: Singing, rhythmic games and accessible melodies encourage participation. Keyboards and acoustic or electric guitars can join bass, drums and percussion in colorful band arrangements, with contrasting textures supporting the words and play.

items.name: Cantautora argentina
items.lineage: Argentina’s women singer-songwriters develop personal repertoires across folk, roots and independent music. Artists such as Delfi Moore place their own words and melodies at the center of intimate acoustic songs and fuller band arrangements.
items.description: Voice and guitar can carry close storytelling, gentle melodic phrases and conversational expression. Keyboards, accordion, electric guitar or drums broaden some arrangements, while sparse songs leave space around the lyric.
exemplars: Delfi Moore — Descansá Chiquita, from Amiga

items.name: Canzone siciliane
items.lineage: Sicilian song carries stories, lullabies, serenades and social commentary between rural and urban communities. The revival associated with Clara Salvo, Rosa Balistreri and the cantastorie links inherited repertoire with the island’s twentieth-century protest movements.
items.description: Text-led singing and expressive melodic delivery bring narrative and social themes forward. Guitar accompaniment and supporting voices can frame solo verses, shared refrains and quieter lullaby settings.

items.name: Kurdish pop
items.lineage: Kurdish pop connects Kurdish-language song and inherited melodies with contemporary songwriting and concert production. Singers such as Rewşan bring collected repertoire and new compositions to audiences across Kurdish communities and the diaspora.
items.description: Expressive lead singing carries memorable melodic lines, while arrangements can draw on bowed strings and contemporary ensemble accompaniment. Traditional song material and personal songwriting meet in varied modern settings.
exemplars: Rewşan — documented singer/violinist core, authored reduced arrangement

items.name: La pop
items.lineage: Los Angeles pop grows through independent artists, production studios and live performance networks. Singer-producers such as Shoffy combine songwriting and multi-instrumental recording practice within the city’s pop and electronic scenes.
items.description: Melodic vocals meet guitar, piano and synthesizer textures. Acoustic and electronic approaches can mix with R&B and dance influences, supporting both intimate songs and more layered productions.

items.name: Latvian pop
items.lineage: Latvian pop encompasses contemporary songwriters and performing artists working across melodic popular styles. Riga’s Elizabete Balčus represents an adventurous art-pop branch joining songwriting with electro-acoustic experimentation.
items.description: Vocal melodies can be framed by electronic production and acoustic colors. Flute, strings or brass may appear alongside rhythmic or atmospheric textures, with arrangements ranging from direct songs to dreamlike, exploratory sound.
exemplars: Elizabete Balčus — CONARIUM (2016), voice/flute core of Latvian art pop

items.name: Lithuanian pop
items.lineage: Lithuanian pop and rock include singer-songwriters whose work circulates through recordings, broadcast sessions and live performance. Alina Orlova’s piano-led songs represent a literary and intimate branch of this contemporary field.
items.description: Expressive singing and keyboard accompaniment can expand into arrangements with acoustic and electric guitars, bass, drums and percussion. Songs balance close vocal storytelling with the color and momentum of a band.
exemplars: Alina Orlova — LRT Opus Live (2013), credited vocal/piano/guitar/bass/drum core

items.name: Luxembourgian pop
items.lineage: Luxembourg’s pop scene includes locally based songwriters and performers drawing on international pop, soul and R&B. Josh Island’s work connects personal songwriting with collaborative band and studio production.
items.description: Lead and supporting vocals shape melodic songs over acoustic or electric guitars, bass and drums. Keyboards and programmed elements can extend the arrangements, while soul-inflected phrasing adds warmth and emphasis.
exemplars: Josh Island — Beautiful World (2021), credited vocal/guitar/bass/drum core

items.name: Macau pop
items.lineage: Macao pop develops through local bands, songwriters, festivals and broadcasting. Groups such as Lavy have helped build the city’s live scene through original songs influenced by American pop-rock and other styles.
items.description: Lead vocals, guitar and bass provide one melodic band foundation. Catchy hooks and varied contemporary arrangements connect local songwriting with international pop-rock sounds.

items.name: Malawian pop
items.lineage: Malawian pop joins local musical traditions with contemporary songwriting, soul and electronic production. Artists such as Faith Mussa connect community and family-band experience with international collaboration and solo performance.
items.description: Layered guitars and sung melodies meet propulsive rhythms, vocal harmonies and electronics. Loop-based performance and traditional instruments can bring older timbres into modern arrangements, with songs in Chichewa and English among the repertoire.
exemplars: Faith Mussa — festival-documented solo voice/guitar core

items.name: Maltese pop
items.lineage: Maltese pop grows through local bands and singer-songwriters drawing on international popular styles. The Busker’s early work connects melodic songwriting with folk and classic-pop influences.
items.description: Voices and guitars combine with bass and drums, while saxophone, keyboards and percussion can add color. Compact song forms and band interplay carry melodies from acoustic-leaning arrangements into fuller rhythmic settings.
exemplars: The Busker — FOUR-era historical five-member roster (2014), selected guitar/bass/sax/drum core

items.name: Math pop
items.lineage: Math pop brings the intricate instrumental interplay of math rock into a melodic, approachable song world. Projects such as Sincerely connect progressive guitar music with tuneful writing and a strong sense of groove.
items.description: Interlocking guitar figures, active bass lines and tightly coordinated drums support recurring melodic ideas. Instrumental arrangements can foreground the conversation between parts, while the wider field also includes vocal songs.

items.name: Bogor Indie
items.lineage: Bogor’s independent music scene grows through local bands and labels such as Hujan! Rekords. Texpack represents a guitar-driven branch influenced by 1990s alternative rock, dream pop and shoegaze.
items.description: Singing and layered electric guitars sit above bass and drums. Fuzzy guitar textures and melodic lines alternate with direct band passages, joining song-focused writing to a hazier alternative-rock sound.

items.name: Cape breton indie
items.lineage: Cape Breton’s independent scene includes songwriters and bands working across folk, rock and pop. Artists such as Alicia Penney bring local experience and personal stories into original songs.
items.description: Expressive lead vocals and supporting harmonies sit alongside guitars, bass and drums. Keyboards and percussion can broaden the accompaniment, balancing intimate lyrics with a fuller band sound.

items.name: Cape town indie
items.lineage: Cape Town indie encompasses local independent songwriting and alternative bands. The Simon van Gend Band represents an introspective folk-rock branch rooted in the city’s live and recorded music.
items.description: Acoustic guitar and lead singing carry conversational, reflective songs above bass and drums. Rhythmic accompaniment and melodic phrasing give the intimate writing a lively band setting.

items.name: Cardiff indie
items.lineage: Cardiff’s independent bands connect alternative rock with art-rock, post-punk and experimental approaches. Groups such as Enabling Behaviour combine local collaboration with original recording and performance.
items.description: Vocals and electric guitars work against bass and drum patterns, moving between direct songs and noisier or more spacious textures. Contrasting voices and guitar layers can enrich the arrangements.

items.name: Cascadia psych
items.lineage: Cascadia psych connects psychedelic music in the Pacific Northwest with exploratory performance and recording. Portland projects such as Plankton Wat and Eternal Tapestry draw on the region’s landscapes and countercultural traditions.
items.description: Guitars move between melodic lines, feedback and ambient textures, with bass, keyboards and synthesizers adding depth. Improvisation and deliberate composition meet in layered passages that can range from quiet drift to forceful psychedelic peaks.

items.name: CDMX indie
items.lineage: Mexico City’s independent scene includes self-producing guitar bands and home-recorded pop projects. Useless Youth connects local collaboration with indie-rock, bedroom-pop and twee-pop songwriting.
items.description: Sung melodies and layered guitars ride over bass and drums. Light, direct song structures and intimate production can coexist with a full band sound and shared vocal lines.

items.name: CDO indie
items.lineage: Cagayan de Oro’s independent music includes original songwriting across acoustic pop and alternative rock. Local acts such as Northern Sparks connect personal songcraft with home and independent production.
items.description: Sung melodies and guitar accompaniment carry verse-and-chorus songs, with acoustic textures offering one intimate approach. Memorable refrains and direct lyrical expression connect the local scene to wider Philippine indie and pop.

items.name: Cello
items.lineage: Cello-centered music reaches across composed repertoire, chamber performance and contemporary improvisation. Musicians such as Oliver Barrett explore the instrument as a complete solo sound world as well as a familiar ensemble voice.
items.description: Bowed strings can sustain lyrical lines, drones and shifting textures; plucked attacks offer contrasting articulation. Solo performance can move between melodic phrasing and freer exploration of resonance, register and timbre.

items.name: Cello ensemble
items.lineage: Cello ensembles develop the expressive range of several cellos performing together. The Berlin Philharmonic’s twelve-cellist ensemble grew from a 1972 production of Julius Klengel’s Hymnus and expanded into a wide-ranging concert tradition.
items.description: A shared instrumental color supports layered melodies, harmonies and bass lines across a broad register. Repertoire can include classical works, contemporary composition, jazz and tango arrangements, contrasting blended sonorities with individual lines.
exemplars: The 12 Cellists of the Berliner Philharmoniker — Klengel Hymnus formation

items.name: Celtic harp
items.lineage: Celtic harp music joins traditional repertoire with contemporary arrangements and original compositions. Players such as Philip Boulding bring lever-harp sound into solo performance and ensembles, drawing on Celtic and wider musical influences.
items.description: Plucked melodies and resonant accompaniment can range from flowing tunes to reflective airs and seasonal repertoire. The harp’s ringing strings support clear melodic lines and gently layered harmony.

items.name: České chvály
items.lineage: Czech praise music brings Christian prayer and devotional texts into contemporary song. Ensembles such as Nenadarmo combine Czech-language repertoire with influences from wider Christian songwriting.
items.description: Lead and shared singing carry reflective or celebratory texts over acoustic guitar, bowed strings and keyboards. Bass, drums and percussion can support a fuller band arrangement, with harmonies reinforcing the communal character of the songs.

items.name: Chakra
items.lineage: Chakra music belongs to contemporary meditation and devotional listening practices that organize sound around the chakra system. Artists such as Sonic Yogi use sustained singing-bowl recordings within this listening tradition.
items.description: Resonant bowls create extended tones, overlapping overtones and slowly changing textures. Spacious pacing and repetition support contemplative listening.
exemplars: Sonic Yogi — Singing Bowl Love (2017), Sacral Chakra branch

items.name: Chamamé brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian chamamé is rooted in the musical exchanges of the Pantanal and Mato Grosso do Sul with neighboring South American traditions. Musicians such as Marcelus Anderson develop this regional repertoire through accordion-led performance.
items.description: Accordion melodies and guitar accompaniment combine rhythmic movement with lyrical phrasing. Instrumental duos offer an intimate expression of the region’s dance and song repertoire.
exemplars: Marcelus Anderson and Marcela Mar — Sanfona Pantaneira duo

items.name: Chamber psych
items.lineage: Chamber psych brings psychedelic atmosphere into intimate alternative songwriting. Contemporary artists such as navel grazr connect the label with dark indie rock, post-punk and goth-pop influences.
items.description: Sung melodies, guitars, synthesizers and drums build layered song arrangements. The interplay of electric textures and vocal phrasing emphasizes atmosphere alongside the rhythmic band foundation.

items.name: Channel Islands indie
items.lineage: Independent music from the Channel Islands includes guitar bands working across garage rock, post-punk and electronic influences. Jersey-formed acts such as The Gaa Gaas connect island origins with the wider British independent circuit.
items.description: Vocals and electric guitars sit over bass and drums, with keyboards adding further texture. Songs can combine direct rhythmic drive with noisier, experimental or synthesizer-led colors.
exemplars: The Gaa Gaas — Close Your Eyes (2016/2019)

items.name: Chanson humoristique
items.lineage: Chanson humoristique places comedy and playful observation within French-language songwriting. Performers such as Evelyne Gallet combine the songwriter tradition with an expressive stage presence.
items.description: The voice carries the text and its comic timing, supported by melodic accompaniment. Guitar-led singing provides an intimate setting for lyrical character, wit and interaction with the audience.

items.name: Chanson paillarde
items.lineage: Chanson paillarde carries a tradition of bawdy, comic and provocative song into communal and staged performance. Contemporary groups such as Les Cop(i)nes revisit older repertoire and create new responses to it.
items.description: Playful texts, rhyme and alliteration are central to the style. Unaccompanied ensemble singing can bring harmonies and lively melodic exchanges to its irreverent storytelling.
exemplars: Les Cop(i)nes — unaccompanied three-voice bawdy-song repertoire

items.name: Chanson québécoise
items.lineage: Québec chanson spans a living repertoire of French-language songs and their reinterpretation. Ensembles such as Tea for 20’s revisit familiar songs by writers including Muriel Millard through traditional and jazz-influenced performance.
items.description: The sung text and melody remain central while accompaniment ranges from intimate settings to colorful bands. Swinging arrangements can combine guitar, piano, bass, drums, brass, reeds and percussive spoons.
exemplars: Tea for 20’s — Dans nos vieilles maisons (2021)

items.name: Chanson virale
items.lineage: Viral chanson connects French-language songwriting with circulation through online video and social platforms. Songs such as Patrick Watson’s Je te laisserai des mots have reached large new audiences through this form of rediscovery.
items.description: The field embraces varied song arrangements and periods. Intimate singing, piano and bowed strings form one expressive branch, placing lyrical melody and atmosphere at the center of the listening experience.
exemplars: Patrick Watson — Je te laisserai des mots (2010)

items.name: Chant basque
items.lineage: Basque singing encompasses oral repertoire, unaccompanied traditions and newer songs in euskara. From the 1960s, singer-songwriters expanded the repertoire, while contemporary groups continue to explore polyphony and new arrangements.
items.description: Solo and shared voices carry melodic lines and layered harmonies. A cappella singing remains an important practice alongside performances enriched by acoustic or electronic instruments.
exemplars: Lurodei — Maylis Raynal and Manon Irigoyen vocal-polyphony branch

items.name: Chant religieux
items.lineage: French religious song joins Christian devotional texts with accessible melodies for prayer and shared singing. Songwriters such as Jean-Claude Gianadda have helped circulate this repertoire through recordings and gatherings.
items.description: A lead voice and guitar can support intimate prayer-song, while familiar refrains encourage participation. Clear melodic phrasing foregrounds the text and its devotional purpose.
exemplars: Jean-Claude Gianadda — French Christian prayer-song guitar practice

items.name: Chapman Stick
items.lineage: Chapman Stick music centers on the fretted tapping instrument developed by Emmett Chapman. Players such as Michael Kollwitz use its independent bass and melody ranges in original pieces and arrangements across several styles.
items.description: Both hands tap the strings directly against the frets, allowing bass lines, chords and melodies to unfold together. The resulting articulated texture can support a complete solo arrangement as well as ensemble playing.
exemplars: Michael Kollwitz — The Chapman Stick Meets The Beatles

items.name: Charango
items.lineage: The charango developed within Andean musical life and spread through Bolivia, Peru and neighboring regions. Its solo and ensemble traditions also inspire contemporary concert and screen-music arrangements.
items.description: The small plucked instrument combines a compact ringing tone with agile melodic and rhythmic playing. Strummed accompaniment and clear individual notes give it a distinctive voice in dance music and solo pieces.
exemplars: Greg Nicolett — Solidarity, Solo Charango Version (2014)

items.name: Charlotte NC indie
items.lineage: Charlotte’s independent music includes guitar-based songwriting and electronic experimentation. Acts such as Julian Calendar bring post-punk and new-wave influences together with sampled rhythm and adventurous pop arrangements.
items.description: Vocals, guitars, bass and synthesizers can combine with drum loops and programmed beats. Contrasting textures range from driving electronic rhythms to softer song settings and string-colored arrangements.

items.name: Charlottesville indie
items.lineage: Charlottesville’s independent rock scene includes bands drawing on alternative, garage and proto-punk traditions. Acts such as Breakers connect local recording and performance with original guitar-led songwriting.
items.description: Sung melodies and interlocking guitars sit over electric bass and drums. Direct rhythmic backing supports the songs while guitar texture supplies much of their edge and color.
exemplars: Breakers — In Search of an Exit (2017)

items.name: Chattanooga indie
items.lineage: Chattanooga’s independent guitar scene includes shoegaze, grunge and alternative rock. Bands such as LACING connect local performances and rehearsal-space recording with the circulation of demos and independent releases.
items.description: Vocals and layered electric guitars ride over bass and drums. Fuzzy textures and sustained guitar color can contrast with direct band rhythms and clearer passages.

items.name: Chennai indie
items.lineage: Chennai’s independent rock scene includes guitar bands such as Skrat, formed in 2006. Local gigs and independent recording platforms connect original songwriting with garage-rock and alternative influences.
items.description: Sung lines, electric guitars and bass combine with rhythmic percussion in compact band arrangements. Contrasting vocal parts and guitar-led hooks give this branch a direct song-centered sound.
exemplars: Skrat — Tin Can Man, IndiEarth Out There Season1 (2013), vocal/guitar/bass core

items.name: Chicago indie
items.lineage: Chicago’s independent music spans guitar songwriting, alternative folk and experimental pop. Bands such as Minor Moon connect folk-rock and country influences with more expansive ensemble arrangements.
items.description: Voices, electric guitars, bass, drums and keyboards form one recurring song texture. Steel guitar, tuned percussion and horn arrangements can broaden the palette, while intimate passages retain a strong melodic focus.
exemplars: Minor Moon — An Opening (2019), four-member song core

items.name: Chihuahua indie
items.lineage: Chihuahua’s independent songwriting includes the bedroom-folk beginnings of Dromedarios Mágicos. Diego Puerta’s intimate guitar-led songs developed from the mid-2010s toward a wider range of collaborative and band settings.
items.description: Close vocal delivery and acoustic-guitar accompaniment support direct melodic songs. The intimate solo texture sits alongside fuller arrangements within the wider independent scene.
exemplars: Dromedarios Mágicos — Diego Puerta’s early acoustic guitar and vocal core

items.name: Children's story
items.lineage: Children’s recorded stories draw on oral storytelling, character voices and imaginative spoken narratives. Storytellers such as Howard Finster carry personal yarns and playful sound imitation into recordings for young listeners.
items.description: A narrator shapes characters and events through speech rhythm, inflection, pacing and pauses. Stories may stand alone or appear beside songs and musical interludes in a larger programme.
exemplars: Howard Finster — Man of Many Voices (1984), spoken-storytelling core

items.name: Chilean indie
items.lineage: Chile’s independent guitar music includes post-punk, shoegaze and alternative-rock currents. Santiago bands such as TØLVA connect local songwriting with atmospheric guitar textures and an introspective urban sensibility.
items.description: Vocals, delayed electric guitars, solid bass lines and precise drums shape one recurring band sound. Melancholy melodies and sustained textures coexist with direct rock rhythms.

items.name: Chill beats
items.lineage: Chill beats connects instrumental hip-hop beatmaking with relaxed listening and jazz-colored samples. Producers such as Mujo circulate compact beat tapes through independent online platforms.
items.description: Chopped phrases, looped melodies and programmed rhythmic fragments create a repeating pocket. Sample texture and small variations in the groove carry much of the music’s movement.
exemplars: Mujo情 — Yutori (2024), instrumental sampler beat core

items.name: Chill groove
items.lineage: Chill groove brings melodic smooth jazz into contact with lounge, soul and relaxed listening music. Ensembles such as Threestyle move between these overlapping traditions in recordings and live performance.
items.description: Flowing saxophone lines and guitar phrases sit over bass grooves, with keyboards and rhythmic percussion enriching fuller arrangements. The emphasis is on melody, smooth transitions and an easy rhythmic feel.
exemplars: Threestyle — A Little Longer (2016), tenor-sax/guitar/bass core

items.name: Chill guitar
items.lineage: Chill guitar places guitar-led melody within mellow listening and lo-fi production. Independent catalogs such as Melody to Beats connect guitarists across different locations with contemporary instrumental and soundtrack work.
items.description: Clear guitar phrases can combine with soft keyboard layers, bass and sampled drums. Background vocal textures sometimes enrich an otherwise instrument-led arrangement.
exemplars: Melody to Beats — Chill Guitar Instrumentals (2021), guitar/voice core

items.name: Chillsynth
items.lineage: Chillsynth joins retro electronic production with atmospheric listening and synth-based soundscapes. Independent projects such as Cyberspace O’Blivion place it alongside chillwave, synthwave and space music.
items.description: Layered synthesizer tones and spacious sustained textures create a reflective electronic setting. Melodic movement and changes in timbre can carry a piece without a foreground singer.
exemplars: Cyberspace O'Blivion — Rogue Planet (2023), analog-synth core

items.name: Chinese audiophile
items.lineage: Chinese audiophile repertoire brings Chinese-language songs and familiar melodies into carefully produced listening recordings. Labels such as Harmony connect Mandarin repertoire with jazz-influenced arrangements and an emphasis on recorded detail.
items.description: An exposed vocal line may sit over acoustic guitar and piano, with space for instrumental phrasing and subtle dynamic changes. The field emphasizes recorded clarity and presentation rather than a single mandatory ensemble.
exemplars: Jacintha — Love Flows Like A River (Harmony Records), Mandarin vocal/guitar/piano core

items.name: Chinese experimental
items.lineage: Chinese experimental music includes sound art and composition crossing acoustic instruments, electronics and recorded environments. Artists such as Li Yilei connect migration, memory and everyday surroundings with exploratory listening.
items.description: Synthesizer textures, strings, vocal samples and field recordings can form fragmented soundscapes. Changes in timbre, space and duration can organize a piece as strongly as melody or a regular beat.
exemplars: Li Yilei — 之 / OF (2021), synth/violin/guqin core

items.name: Chinese new year
items.lineage: Chinese New Year music accompanies Spring Festival celebrations across Chinese communities. Familiar festive repertoire appears in public performances, recordings and arrangements ranging from larger ensembles to solo piano.
items.description: Bright melodies and celebratory rhythmic gestures mark the seasonal setting. Piano transcriptions offer an instrumental route through the repertoire, while songs and ensemble versions serve other festive occasions.
exemplars: Lang Lang — Happy Chinese New Year (2014), piano arrangement branch

items.name: Chinese worship
items.lineage: Chinese worship music connects Chinese-language Christian congregations through original songs, ministry recordings and live worship. Stream of Praise has developed this repertoire for Chinese churches internationally since the 1990s.
items.description: Sung praise and congregational participation lie alongside instrumental devotional arrangements. Piano can carry hymn and worship-song melodies with chordal support, while worship bands provide fuller settings.
exemplars: Stream of Praise — With All My Love, Piano Series 2 (2008), instrumental piano core

items.name: Chip hop
items.lineage: Chip hop brings video-game music and chip-derived sounds into hip-hop production. Artists such as Mode 7 connect game-music sampling with rap and beat-making.
items.description: Rapped verses and looped beats meet melodic fragments and recognizable textures from game soundtracks. Chopped samples and layered sequences provide a production route alongside synthesized chip sounds.

items.name: Christchurch indie
items.lineage: Christchurch indie draws on the independent bands and recording activity of the New Zealand city. Groups such as PATIENTS connect local songwriting with alternative and indie rock.
items.description: Electric guitars, bass and drums support sung melodies and contrasting vocal parts. Guitar-led arrangements range from direct hooks to rougher, more atmospheric rock textures.

items.name: Christelijk
items.lineage: Christelijk encompasses Dutch Christian music associated with worship, devotion and church life. Projects such as Psalmen voor Nu bring Psalm texts into contemporary Dutch-language song.
items.description: Clear sung melodies and chordal accompaniment support devotional texts and communal participation. Voice and acoustic guitar offer an intimate setting alongside fuller church and recording ensembles.
exemplars: Psalmen voor Nu — Licht, kom tevoorschijn (2013), published guitar-score realization

items.name: Christian a cappella
items.lineage: Christian a cappella uses unaccompanied voices for Christian song and worship. Congregations, quartets and vocal groups maintain harmony traditions through live singing, recordings and teaching.
items.description: Interlocking vocal parts carry melody, harmony and rhythmic support without instrumental accompaniment. Four-part arrangements are a prominent teaching and performance practice, with larger groups extending the same vocal texture.
exemplars: Acappella Ministries — Praise & Harmony training-disc quartet

items.name: Christian indie
items.lineage: Christian indie connects independent songwriting and alternative music with Christian texts and devotional themes. Artists such as Thief to King work across acoustic song, worship and band-based recording.
items.description: Sung melodies sit over guitars, bass and drums, with piano and organ adding harmonic color. Intimate acoustic passages and fuller band textures give the repertoire a range of dynamics.
exemplars: Thief to King — Your Decrees Are Very Sure (Psalm 93), Hail the King (2025)

items.name: Christian lo-fi
items.lineage: Christian lo-fi brings devotional music and hymn repertoire into intimate, deliberately modest recording practices. Home performances and simple recordings can preserve the immediacy of personal or congregational music-making.
items.description: Soft keyboard melodies and restrained arrangements support reflective listening. Audible room character and limited recording fidelity can become part of the presentation, alongside contemporary beat-based approaches to devotional repertoire.
exemplars: Tyler James Cook — My Wonderful Lord, The Lo-Fi Hymnal (2020)

items.name: Christian music
items.lineage: Christian music encompasses songs and instrumental works shaped by Christian belief, worship and devotional life. Historical hymn texts continue to receive new melodies and arrangements from contemporary songwriters such as Rachel Wilhelm.
items.description: Voice-centered settings range from intimate acoustic accompaniment to larger groups. Guitar, piano and sustained strings can frame hymn melodies with gentle rhythmic motion and layered harmony.
exemplars: Rachel Wilhelm — O Love With Heights Unknown (2016)

items.name: Christian uplift
items.lineage: Christian uplift gathers faith-centered repertoire associated with encouragement, consolation and hope. Hymn interpretations and contemporary devotional songwriting connect inherited texts with personal musical expression.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies and supportive accompaniment foreground the words. Fingerpicked nylon-string guitar provides an intimate folk-influenced setting, while other arrangements build a fuller sense of communal affirmation.
exemplars: Wilder Adkins — Nothing But the Blood, Oak & Apple (2011)

items.name: Christmas instrumental
items.lineage: Christmas instrumental music recasts seasonal songs, carols and associated screen repertoire without sung text. Solo arrangements and ensemble performances bring familiar melodies into settings ranging from home listening to concerts.
items.description: Instrumental melody carries the tune while accompaniment supplies harmony and rhythmic character. Solo piano can combine both roles, drawing on jazz voicings, classical phrasing and familiar seasonal themes.
exemplars: Steve T Hunter — Christmas Solo Piano (2020)

items.name: Cincinnati indie
items.lineage: Cincinnati indie grows from the city’s independent bands, songwriters and live music activity. Groups such as Old City combine local songwriting with alternative and indie-rock performance.
items.description: Guitar, bass and drums frame vocal hooks and introspective lyrics. Contrasting voices and shifts between restrained passages and a fuller band sound give the music its dynamic shape.

items.name: Clap and tap
items.lineage: Clap and tap is a South African choral practice connecting group singing with rhythmic hand percussion. Student and community ensembles maintain the practice through shared performance and cultural participation.
items.description: Blended vocal harmony combines with coordinated clapping and hand tapping. The voices carry the melodic texture while the hand rhythm gives the ensemble a clear collective pulse.
exemplars: Nelson Mandela University — Clap and Tap Student Society

items.description: Murcia indie combines melodic songwriting with local independent-band culture. Clean electric guitars, bass and drums support lead and backing voices in its indie-pop branch, balancing direct song forms with ensemble interplay.

items.name: Música alagoana
items.lineage: Music of Alagoas, spanning regional popular traditions, contemporary songwriting and instrumental composition.
items.description: Música alagoana is a broad regional field shaped by musicians from Alagoas. Popular songs and local traditions coexist with new instrumental compositions and improvisation, including intimate solo performances.

items.name: Música Amapaense
items.lineage: Music of Amapá, connecting regional song, poetry and varied contemporary performance practices.
items.description: Música Amapaense brings local cultural expression into songs and instrumental music. Its poetic acoustic branch combines singing, spoken verse and guitar accompaniment, emphasizing language, lyrical imagery and close interaction among performers.

items.name: Música Andorra
items.lineage: Andorra’s musical field, encompassing song, instrumental music and contemporary acoustic-electronic work.
items.description: Música Andorra gathers varied practices associated with Andorran musicians. Alongside songs and instrumental performance, ambient and contemporary chamber approaches combine acoustic strings, voices and electronic sound design.
exemplars: Landry Riba — The Meaning of Now, complete eight-track album2024

items.name: Musica Costarricense
items.lineage: Costa Rican music, including popular songs, regional traditions and concert interpretations of national repertoire.
items.description: Música Costarricense encompasses diverse musical life in Costa Rica. Familiar songs circulate through singing, ensemble performance and instrumental arrangements, while composers and performers bring national repertoire into new settings.
exemplars: José Daniel Zúñiga — Caña dulce, Manuel Matarrita piano-solo adaptation

items.name: Musica Feirense
items.lineage: Music of Feira de Santana, including independent rock and contemporary local songwriting.
items.description: Música Feirense reflects the varied musical life of Feira de Santana. Its independent-rock branch uses voices, electric guitar, bass and drums, with riff-centered stoner-rock textures among its contemporary approaches.
exemplars: Novelta — Quintais Abertos EP (2015), complete quartet

items.name: Musica Infantil
items.lineage: Spanish-language children’s music, bringing stories, play and learning into accessible songs.
items.description: Música Infantil combines memorable melodies, playful narratives and direct vocal delivery. Arrangements range from simple accompaniment to colorful pop bands, with keyboards, guitars, bass, drums and programmed sounds supporting imaginative child-oriented songs.

items.name: Musica Infantil Catala
items.lineage: Catalan children’s songs, transmitted through singing, play, teaching and instrumental arrangements.
items.description: Música Infantil Català connects traditional and newly composed songs with childhood play and learning. Familiar tunes support participation and language, while educational arrangements bring the repertoire into instrumental study.
exemplars: Enric Capdevila — El racó del piano1, El gegant del pi pedagogical piano setting (B.3686)

items.name: Musica Lombarda
items.lineage: Lombard regional music, including dialect song and contemporary folk-oriented composition.
items.description: Música Lombarda connects regional language and cultural memory with new songs. Its Brescian dialect branch brings social observation, irony and poetry into vocal arrangements with plucked strings and keyboards.

items.name: Musica Londrinense
items.lineage: Music of Londrina, including independent bands and contemporary heavy music.
items.description: Música Londrinense reflects a diverse local musical field. Its metal branch combines voices, electric guitars and bass with forceful rhythmic accompaniment, including programmed drums in independently produced recordings.

items.name: Música mallorquina
items.lineage: Mallorcan music, encompassing island traditions and contemporary popular and independent scenes.
items.description: Música mallorquina includes varied musical practices rooted in Mallorca. Contemporary rock bands add amplified guitars, bass, drums and vocals to the island’s musical life, with psychedelic and stoner-rock approaches among those branches.

items.name: Música maranhense
items.lineage: Music of Maranhão, connecting regional songwriting, MPB, samba and Afro-Maranhão influences.

items.name: Música maringaense
items.lineage: Music of Maringá, including independent rock, songwriting and varied ensemble arrangements.
items.description: Música maringaense reflects the contemporary musical life of Maringá. Its independent-rock branch combines voices and electric guitars with bass and drums, sometimes expanding through keyboards, acoustic guitar, accordion and brass.
exemplars: errorama — Todas as coisas que eu acho que sei (2016)

items.name: Música menorquina
items.lineage: Menorcan music, including island songwriting and acoustic interpretations of local experience.
items.description: Música menorquina encompasses varied music associated with Menorca. Its singer-songwriter branch brings personal lyrics and Catalan-language expression into intimate guitar accompaniment, sometimes layering backing voices around the lead melody.

items.name: Música occitana
items.lineage: Occitan music, sustaining a living language through traditional repertoire and contemporary reinterpretation.
items.description: Música occitana includes song, dance and new composition across Occitan-speaking communities. Contemporary amplified approaches place traditional melodies and lyrics alongside electric guitar and drums, connecting inherited repertoire with rock performance.
