items.name: Brazilian CCM
items.lineage: Brazilian contemporary Christian music includes a substantial Catholic recording and performance community. Artists, ministries and devotional media connect newly composed songs with communal worship and personal reflection.
items.description: Melodic singing and clear refrains often meet acoustic guitar or keyboard accompaniment, with fuller bands in other settings. Intimate delivery, shared responses and accessible harmonies support contemporary devotional expression.

items.name: Britcore
items.lineage: Britcore emerged as a hard-edged branch of British hip-hop, associated with groups such as Hijack, Hardnoise and the Demon Boyz. Rapid rap, forceful breakbeats and turntable technique connect its sound with the UK’s wider sound-system and breakbeat cultures.
items.description: Urgent rhythmic speech meets chopped drum breaks, layered samples and scratch accents. Dense rhythmic attacks and quick verbal exchanges create momentum without requiring a fixed number of rappers or a single production setup.

items.name: Drikkelek
items.lineage: Drikkelek songs belong to contemporary Nordic participatory party-game repertoire. They circulate through local celebrations, recordings and social gatherings, overlapping student-party music while serving a distinct game-oriented function.
items.description: Spoken instructions alternate with memorable sung refrains over repeated electronic accompaniment. Clear verbal cues, communal responses and recurring rhythmic sections organize participation.

items.name: Dunedin indie
items.lineage: Dunedin indie connects the New Zealand city’s independent musicians, labels and venues across generations. The Flying Nun-era Dunedin Sound remains an important inheritance alongside newer guitar, electronic and experimental communities.
items.description: Distinctive vocal melodies and guitar interplay meet bass, drums and varied keyboard textures. Lo-fi intimacy, sharp rhythmic contrasts and exploratory arrangements coexist rather than defining one fixed local sound.

items.name: Dutch moombahton
items.lineage: Dutch moombahton develops within Netherlands club and producer networks that connect Dutch house, reggaeton, bubbling and related dance styles. Producers and MCs bring this local repertoire into international festival and online circulation.
items.description: Syncopated electronic drums, rounded bass and repeated synth or sample hooks support a slower, bouncing dance pulse. Vocal fragments, MC calls and transitions between contrasting rhythmic sections give arrangements their momentum.

items.name: Dweilorkest
items.lineage: Dweilorkesten are Dutch festive wind-and-percussion bands heard at carnival, sporting events and other public celebrations. Local associations sustain a participatory performance tradition with flexible instrumentation and familiar popular repertoire.
items.description: Trumpets, saxophones and trombones exchange punchy melodic phrases over a low brass foundation and percussion. Clear rhythmic accents, communal energy and compact arrangements project into lively public spaces.

items.name: Early avant garde
items.lineage: Early avant-garde music challenged inherited assumptions about composition, sound and performance during the early twentieth century. Chance procedures, Dada experiments, unconventional instruments and new approaches to pitch and form opened paths for later experimental music.
items.description: Independent vocal lines, unusual sound sources and unexpected combinations of gesture and silence can replace familiar harmonic development. Some works organize sound through instructions or chance, while others explore instrumental color and discontinuous musical structures.

items.name: Eastern Bloc groove
items.lineage: Eastern Bloc groove draws together jazz, funk, soul, disco and beat recordings from the former socialist countries of Eastern Europe. Collectors, reissue labels and contemporary musicians connect these varied national recording histories through their rhythmic and instrumental affinities.
items.description: Syncopated bass and drums support electric keyboards and melodic wind lines, with ensemble interplay ranging from concise dance arrangements to exploratory jazz passages. Warm electric textures and repeated grooves connect diverse local repertoires.

items.name: Edo old school
items.lineage: Edo old school centers the recorded popular-music heritage of Benin City and surrounding Edo communities in Nigeria. Highlife, funk and local musical materials met in the work of artists such as Victor Uwaifo, Osayomore Joseph and Akaba Man.
items.description: Repeated bass figures, rhythmic guitar and driving percussion support expressive voices and bright melodic lines. Synthesizers, organs, flute and horns add contrasting colors to arrangements that range from lean grooves to psychedelic textures.

items.name: Egyptian alternative
items.lineage: Egyptian alternative connects independent musicians and experimental communities working across contemporary Egyptian song, rock and electronics. Cairo’s exploratory networks bring inherited melodic materials into dialogue with new production and ensemble practices.
items.description: Voices, guitars, synthesizers and acoustic rhythm sections can combine layered textures, irregular contrasts and improvisatory interplay. Instrument choices and approaches vary widely, from intimate songs to dense electronic and acoustic ensembles.

items.name: Egyptian traditional
items.lineage: Egyptian traditional music encompasses urban art-song, regional folk, devotional and instrumental traditions. Cairo’s takht heritage is one influential strand within a wider landscape that also includes Upper Egyptian, Nubian and Coptic repertoires.
items.description: Ornamented voices and melodic instruments explore modal phrases over recurring rhythmic cycles. Oud and qanun provide plucked detail while hand percussion marks and varies the rhythmic frame; flutes, bowed strings and other ensembles expand the palette in different traditions.

items.name: Eletrônica underground brasileira
items.lineage: Brazilian underground electronic music develops through independent clubs, labels, producers and resident-DJ networks. House, techno, disco and experimental approaches intersect in a community distinct from, but connected to, the larger commercial dance economy.
items.description: Repeated electronic drums and bass patterns support synthesizer movement, sampled textures and gradual transitions. Individual producers vary the balance of rhythmic weight, melodic detail and abstraction across dance-floor and listening contexts.

items.name: EPA dunk
items.lineage: EPA-dunk is associated with Swedish A-tractor youth culture and communal party listening. Producers and singers connect accessible popular-song hooks with bass-heavy electronic arrangements and a repertoire that also circulates beyond the vehicle scene.
items.description: Prominent vocals, repeated refrains and firmly marked electronic beats create an immediate participatory sound. Synthesizer figures and low-end weight reinforce the songs’ rhythmic drive and memorable melodic phrases.

items.name: Epic Collage
items.lineage: Epic collage names a network of experimental electronic music that emerged around surreal combinations of pop fragments, dramatic effects and cinematic textures. Artists connect club-derived materials with abstract narratives and unexpected sonic juxtapositions.
items.description: Abrupt edits, layered samples and contrasting atmospheres form discontinuous musical scenes. Familiar vocal or instrumental fragments may be stretched, interrupted or placed against unrelated sounds, with rhythm serving both dance movement and narrative disruption.

items.name: Epunk
items.lineage: Epunk connects contemporary internet-based punk communities, independent releases and DIY performance. Participants draw on garage punk, power pop and related guitar music while developing local and online networks around shared recordings.
items.description: Direct singing, distorted guitar, bass and drums support concise riffs and forceful song structures. Rough textures and immediate delivery coexist with melodic hooks; electronic production varies rather than defining the category’s name.

items.name: Er ge (Chinese children’s repertoire)
items.lineage: Er ge encompasses Chinese-language children’s songs and associated childhood listening repertoire. Familiar melodies circulate through family, educational and recorded settings, alongside instrumental adaptations and spoken stories.
items.description: Clear sung phrases, recurring rhythms and accessible accompaniment support recognition, memory and participation. Keyboard-led versions offer one common setting, while ensemble, instrumental and narrated formats broaden the listening field.

items.name: Erotica
items.lineage: Erotica is an adult-themed listening field spanning literary readings, songs and atmospheric instrumental material. Publishers and performers connect intimate narrative with a wider repertoire organized around mood and subject rather than a single musical lineage.
items.description: Spoken delivery emphasizes pacing, character and verbal detail in its literary branch. Other recordings use sung melody or instrumental atmosphere, with texture and performance shaped by the work’s intended listening context.

items.name: Escape Room
items.lineage: Escape room is a named discovery community connecting experimental pop, hip-hop and R&B. Its artists blur established genre expectations through independent production, socially engaged expression and unconventional approaches to popular-song material.
items.description: Voices move between direct hooks and rhythmically detailed phrasing over electronic beats, samples and changing synth textures. Arrangement contrasts and distinctive production gestures carry personality without requiring a single shared sound-design technique.

items.name: Ethiopian Traditional
items.lineage: Ethiopian traditional music encompasses inherited repertoires across the country’s diverse communities. Family transmission, poetic performance, regional celebrations and devotional institutions sustain distinct musical languages rather than one national style.
items.description: In lyric-centered traditions, expressive singing and plucked lyre accompaniment carry love poetry, social observation and proverbs. Repeated figures and flexible vocal phrasing coexist with other regional instrumental and choral practices.

items.name: Ethnomusicology
items.lineage: Ethnomusicology connects the study of music in cultural context with documentary recordings, archives and sustained research relationships. Curated listening collections bring distinct local traditions to wider audiences while retaining their separate histories and practices.
items.description: Musical form, voice, rhythm and instrumental color vary across the field’s many communities. Solo instrumental traditions offer one path into attentive listening, alongside ensemble, vocal, ritual and everyday music documented in other settings.

items.name: Euphoric Hardstyle
items.lineage: Euphoric hardstyle is the melodic and emotionally expansive branch of hardstyle, sustained by producers, labels and festival communities. It overlaps rawer approaches while placing particular emphasis on memorable leads, harmonic lift and dramatic releases of tension.
items.description: Heavy electronic kicks and a steady dance pulse support layered synthesizer melodies and broad chordal textures. Breakdowns, rising transitions and returning hooks create contrasts between spacious anticipation and forceful rhythmic impact.

items.name: Eventyr
items.lineage: Eventyr connects Scandinavian fairy-tale traditions with literary collections, oral storytelling and recorded narration. Familiar plots and characters circulate across languages and generations rather than belonging to a single narrator or modern edition.
items.description: Spoken pacing, changes of character and expressive pauses shape imagined scenes. A clear narrative voice can carry the entire tale, with phrasing and emphasis guiding attention through recurring motifs and dramatic turns.

items.name: Experimental Club
items.lineage: Experimental club music brings exploratory sound and rhythm design into dance-floor culture. Independent producers and labels connect unusual timbres and structures with club programming, sometimes preserving steady mixing and sometimes interrupting it.
items.description: Synthetic tones, manipulated samples and shifting rhythmic layers create contrasting textures. Repetition can establish a pulse while edits, changing densities and unexpected transitions reshape the listener’s sense of movement.

items.name: Experimental Psych
items.lineage: Experimental psych extends psychedelic rock through exploratory textures, extended performance and unconventional forms. Heavy riffs, improvisatory interaction and altered instrumental colors connect older psychedelic practices with contemporary independent scenes.
items.description: Fuzzed guitar, bass and drums support voices and evolving rhythmic passages. Repeated figures may expand through shifting dynamics, noise and textural changes, moving between concentrated song gestures and open-ended exploration.

items.name: Fantasy
items.lineage: Fantasy music evokes imagined worlds, journeys and characters through instrumental or vocal composition. Standalone concept pieces coexist with music for games, film and other narrative media, crossing acoustic, orchestral and electronic approaches.
items.description: Contrasting themes, changes of register and shifts in harmony suggest places, movement and dramatic events. Piano-led compositions provide one intimate setting, while larger ensembles and electronic textures can create broader imagined spaces.

items.name: Focus Beats
items.lineage: Focus beats connects instrumental beat-making with listening for work, study and everyday concentration. Radio curators and independent producers draw on beat tapes, instrumental hip-hop and related electronic music, creating a functional listening field that crosses individual production styles.
items.description: Repeated rhythmic figures and understated melodic layers maintain continuity while small changes in texture keep the music moving. Sampled fragments and electronic tones can sit within an instrumental arrangement, with occasional vocal fragments rather than a required lead singer.

items.name: Folclore Navarra
items.lineage: Navarre folk music brings together regional song, dance and instrumental traditions in Basque and Spanish. Contemporary groups such as Mielotxin connect locally transmitted repertoire with new compositions and arrangements, maintaining a dialogue between rural traditions and present-day concert life.
items.description: Voices, accordion and traditional flutes combine with rhythmic accompaniment in flexible ensembles. Dance accents, recurring melodic patterns and clear song phrases shape the music, while acoustic strings and percussion support changing textures.

items.name: Future Bounce
items.lineage: Future bounce developed within future-house production and festival culture, with Mike Williams, Brooks and Mesto among its prominent practitioners. It shares house rhythm and electronic production with the wider field while emphasizing buoyant melodic figures and sharply shaped releases of energy.
items.description: Electronic drums and bass support bright, repeating synthesizer figures. Contrasting breakdowns, rising transitions and rhythmically articulated hooks give the music its springy dance-floor character.

items.name: German Hyperpop
items.lineage: German-language hyperpop connects internet-led pop culture with rave, rap and emotionally direct songwriting. Artists including Baby B3ns, Domiziana and Abor & Tynna move between electronic pop, club energy and influences from emo and guitar music. The field extends beyond national borders through its language and online communities.
items.description: Prominent voices, synthetic hooks and electronic drums form a vivid pop texture. Pitch processing, exaggerated timbres and abrupt contrasts can heighten intimacy or intensity, while song melodies remain central through changing production styles.

items.name: Guidance
items.lineage: Guidance recordings connect practical instruction, personal advice and self-help writing with spoken listening. Audiobooks and instructional programmes cover subjects ranging from language and creative skills to everyday decisions and personal development.
items.description: A clear speaking voice organizes explanations, examples and suggestions. Pacing, emphasis and pauses help listeners follow ideas, with the narration able to carry the programme without musical accompaniment.

items.name: Guitarra Argentina
items.lineage: Argentine guitar repertoire brings together concert composition, tango, milonga and folk-derived instrumental practice. Soloists, duos and larger ensembles connect regional dance rhythms with the guitar’s melodic and harmonic resources. Eduardo Falú and Héctor Ayala are among the composers represented in its concert repertoire.
items.description: Fingerpicked nylon strings combine melody, bass and inner voices within a compact texture. Rhythmic accents and changes in register shape dances, lyrical passages and extended compositions, with articulation balancing clear individual notes and resonant chords.

items.name: Gym hardstyle
items.lineage: Gym hardstyle connects hard-dance production with online fitness and Zyzz-associated listening communities. Producers and curators such as Tevvez and Ru-Style draw on melodic hardstyle and harder dance crossovers, bringing festival energy into workout-oriented music circulation.
items.description: Forceful electronic kicks and repeating synthesizer hooks establish a driving pulse. Expansive melodic passages and escalating transitions contrast with dense rhythmic returns, emphasizing intensity without requiring a particular workout or physiological effect.

items.name: Hakkapop
items.lineage: Hakkapop brings Hakka-language songwriting and cultural expression into contemporary popular music. Artists such as Lo Sirong draw on literary texts and mountain-song traditions while engaging with folk, blues and other international influences. The scene overlaps Taiwanese popular music without requiring a single style or ethnic background from every performer.
items.description: Expressive lead singing carries the words over acoustic or amplified accompaniment. Guitar-led arrangements may include mandolin, banjo and harmonica, allowing lyrical phrases and rhythmic instrumental responses to meet in an intimate texture.

items.name: Halloween
items.lineage: Halloween music gathers seasonal songs, theatrical effects and concert repertoire around playful fright and supernatural imagery. Community celebrations and curated listening bring novelty recordings, organ classics, soundtrack material and other styles into a shared seasonal setting.
items.description: Dark contrasts, dramatic pauses and memorable gestures help create suspense or comic surprise. Resonant pipe organ offers one instrumental setting, while voices, bands and electronic effects appear elsewhere in the repertoire.

items.name: Hammond organ
items.lineage: Hammond organ music spans jazz, gospel, rock and experimental performance. Tonewheel sound, drawbar registration and rotating-speaker color connect solo exploration with ensembles, from organ trios to amplified bands and sustained drone-based work.
items.description: Keyboard figures move between melodic lines, chords and repeating patterns, with bass and upper registers available to a single player. Changing registration and rotary movement reshape the tone, supporting both clear rhythmic attack and sustained textures.

items.name: Handpan
items.lineage: Handpan music centers on hand-played tuned steel shells, developing from the Hang and related contemporary instruments. Solo improvisation, composition and ensemble collaboration circulate through maker communities, recordings and live performance.
items.description: Resonant pitched strikes combine melody and rhythm across a small set of tuned fields. Alternating hands, repeated figures and contrasting touches let ringing tones overlap while quieter taps maintain motion.

items.name: Hardgroove
items.lineage: Hardgroove developed within techno through funk-driven rhythm, percussion and layered loop production, with Ben Sims central to its named scene and label. Its connections to DJ culture emphasize movement and interaction between rhythmic layers rather than a single fixed tempo or sample source.
items.description: Interlocking percussion and repeated sampled figures ride a firm electronic pulse. Gradual changes in density, accent and loop combination keep the groove active, combining mechanical precision with syncopated rhythmic movement.

items.name: Haryanvi ragni
items.lineage: Ravi Kumar and Group — complete five-person Haryanvi Ragini practice documented by producer Anahad. Ravi Kumar sings lead; Ram Meher Singh and Naveen Kumar both play harmonium and sing chorus; Rajesh Kumar plays Nagada; Mausam plays Dholak. Four sound families and three positively documented singers retain all five people, including two harmonium players, without adding another role from other groups these musicians join. The producer interview and two issued performance pages establish a complete storytelling ensemble rather than an arbitrary vocal highlight or incomplete studio-credit reconstruction. Indian bardic placement follows the explicit story-centered song practice. Hand-pumped harmonium uses all original physical action, reed-voicing and use controls with an isolated local free_reed_technique override for keyboard/bellows gesture; it does not inherit mouth-harmonica first-position/overblow technique. Hand pumping and lower-register reed voicing are authored acoustic construction options, not measured source reed banks. Two documented harmonium players share this sound-family card. items.name: Heligónka
items.lineage: Heligónka music centers on a diatonic button accordion associated with Slovak and Czech folk performance. Solo players and accompanying musicians carry dance melodies and songs through a practice shaped by changing pitches with bellows direction and strong left-hand support.
items.description: Melody, bass and chord patterns interact within one instrument. Push-and-pull phrasing gives repeated figures rhythmic lift, while the characteristic low accompaniment supports clear dance accents and song contours.

items.name: Hindi worship
items.lineage: Hindi worship connects Christian congregational singing and original devotional songwriting across Hindi-speaking communities. Youth ensembles, churches and recording musicians share repertoire that overlaps wider contemporary worship while retaining its language and local religious networks.
items.description: Lead singing and supporting harmonies carry devotional words over chordal accompaniment. Keyboard-led arrangements leave space for repeated phrases, group participation and gradual changes in vocal intensity.

items.name: Hinos CCB
items.lineage: Hinos CCB is the hymn repertoire of Congregação Cristã no Brasil, sustained through its hymnbook, congregational services and organized musical instruction. Singers, organists and instrumental musicians share a denominational body of melodies that also circulates in home study and recordings.
items.description: Clear hymn phrases and supporting harmonies guide collective singing. Organ accompaniment can sustain the melody and chordal movement, while larger instrumental settings and solo arrangements offer other ways of presenting the same repertoire.

items.name: Histoire pour enfants
items.lineage: Histoire pour enfants brings French-language children’s stories into spoken recordings and listening programmes. Traditional tales, translated stories and newer writing circulate through individual narrators and multi-reader collections.
items.description: Expressive pacing, clear diction and changes of character carry the story. Pauses and vocal emphasis mark suspense, surprise and recurring motifs, with a single narrator able to sustain the imagined scene.

items.name: Hörspiel
items.lineage: Hörspiel developed as a German-language field of radio drama and acoustic dramatic art, encompassing literary dialogue, original scripts and experimental sound. Broadcast institutions and independent recording projects support both voiced dramatic readings and productions combining speech with music or sound design.
items.description: Characters emerge through contrasting voices, dialogue rhythm and the placement of silence. Edited exchanges and narration can create a complete dramatic scene, while other productions add acoustic environments, effects and musical structures.

items.name: Hokkaido indie
items.lineage: Hokkaido indie connects independent rock and pop musicians through local performance, recording and self-release practices. Home-produced projects and bands share a regional setting within the wider Japanese independent music field, with places such as Asahikawa supporting their own creative networks.
items.description: Voices and electric guitars carry melodies and riffs over bass and drums. Direct song structures, rough-edged textures and flexible recording approaches range from compact home productions to fuller band arrangements.

items.name: Honky-tonk piano
items.lineage: Honky-tonk piano connects lively keyboard playing with country, blues, ragtime and early popular dance music. Its influence extends through R&B, rockabilly, rock-and-roll and jazz, crossing the boundaries of the vocal-country style that shares its name.
items.description: Strong left-hand patterns support rhythmic chords and melodic flourishes. An upright’s bright, slightly detuned color can add a bustling edge, while repeated bass figures and flexible accents encourage variation and improvisation.

items.name: Houston indie
items.lineage: Houston indie connects independent rock and pop artists through local venues, studios and self-directed releases. Guitar-based groups such as Only Beast are part of a city scene that coexists with Houston’s better-known hip-hop traditions and broader Texas music networks.
items.description: Voices, electric guitar, bass and drums create a direct band texture. Melodic hooks, forceful riffs and contrasting dynamics move between garage-rock urgency and more spacious alternative-rock passages.

items.name: Hüzünlü şarkılar
items.lineage: Hüzünlü şarkılar gathers Turkish sad-song repertoire across pop, alternative rock and other styles. Melancholy lyrics and emotional identification connect the field’s listeners even when arrangements differ in tempo, instrumentation or intensity.
items.description: Expressive voices foreground longing, loss and reflection. Guitar-band arrangements can combine recurring melodic phrases with firm rhythmic support, showing how sorrowful words may coexist with energetic instrumental motion.

items.name: Igbo traditional
items.lineage: Igbo traditional music encompasses inherited community song, dance and instrumental practices in southeastern Nigeria. Travelling ensembles and local ceremonial settings preserve distinct roles for tuned skin drums, slit drums and voices, with practices varying between communities and occasions.
items.description: Interlocking drum parts combine rhythmic pattern and pitched contour. Skin-headed drums and wooden ekwe can answer one another in a dance ensemble, using contrasting attacks and registers to create melodic as well as percussive movement.

items.name: Igbo worship
items.lineage: Igbo worship is a Christian devotional repertoire carried through the Igbo language in churches, choirs and recordings. Praise and thanksgiving songs connect local expression with choral and congregational practices, overlapping wider Nigerian Christian music while retaining their language-centered identity.
items.description: Voices carry the devotional text through repeated phrases and supporting harmonies. Unaccompanied choral arrangements offer one clear setting, while other practices use instrumental support and larger congregational participation.

items.name: Indiana indie
items.lineage: Indiana indie connects independent songwriting communities across Bloomington, Indianapolis and other parts of the state. Artists and labels such as Amy O and Winspear link local recording and performance networks with broader American indie pop and rock.
items.description: Voices and guitars meet bass, drums and keyboard colors in flexible song arrangements. Melodic immediacy, changing textures and contrasts between intimate delivery and fuller ensemble passages shape the sound; programming and overdubs provide additional options.

items.name: Indie arequipeño
items.lineage: Arequipa indie connects independent music-making in the southern Peruvian city with wider national rock and pop networks. Guitar-based songwriting and electronic exploration coexist, with artists such as Paisaje 3 drawing on trip-hop, loops and synthesized textures.
items.description: Voices, guitars and bass interact with electronic sequences and samples. Repetition and layered timbres create atmosphere, while melodic figures and changing densities preserve a sense of song within the production.

items.name: Indie Cantabria
items.lineage: Cantabria indie brings together regional independent rock and pop practice within the broader Spanish scene. Groups such as Lunatic Catz build their music around songs, local performance and flexible guitar-band arrangements.
items.description: Lead singing, layered guitars and keyboards sit over bass and drums. Chordal support and melodic responses alternate with dynamic contrasts, moving between compact song sections and fuller ensemble textures.

items.name: Indie Córdoba
items.lineage: Córdoba indie refers to independent music from Córdoba, Argentina, within the country’s wider rock and pop landscape. Regional artists range from melodic pop and folk-influenced songwriting to grunge and alternative-rock bands.
items.description: Voices and electric guitars lead bass-and-drum arrangements, with repeated riffs, melodic hooks and shifts in intensity shaping the songs. Distorted and cleaner textures coexist across the scene.

items.name: Indie hidalguense
items.lineage: Hidalgo indie connects independent rock and pop practice in the Mexican state, including artists working in Pachuca. Dream pop, shoegaze and alternative-rock influences meet within a regional branch of the broader Mexican independent field.
items.description: Singing and electric guitars create layered melodic textures over bass and drums. Chordal repetition and changing dynamics support intimate passages as well as denser, more enveloping arrangements.

items.name: Indie poblano
items.lineage: Puebla indie is the regional independent-song field within Puebla’s broader musical life. Guitar-based pop and rock artists participate in local performance and recording networks while sharing influences with the wider Mexican independent scene.
items.description: Lead melodies and layered guitars sit over bass and drums. Rhythmic chord patterns, melodic responses and recurring hooks give songs a clear shape, with shifts in arrangement balancing intimacy and ensemble energy.

items.name: Indie queretano
items.lineage: Querétaro indie connects regional independent rock and pop practice with the wider Mexican scene. Guitar songwriting and psychedelic or electronic colors coexist in locally produced recordings and collaborative projects.
items.description: Voices, guitar, bass and drums combine with sustained synthesizer layers. Repeating song figures and contrasts in texture allow melodic phrases to emerge from a fuller, atmospheric band sound.

items.name: Indie Trujillano
items.lineage: Trujillo indie names independent rock and pop practice in the northern Peruvian city. Bands such as Mafús connect melodic songwriting, pop-punk energy and local performance with the broader Peruvian independent field.
items.description: Singing and electric guitars carry hooks and chord patterns over bass and drums. Rhythmic attack and changes in density give the songs momentum while leaving room for clear vocal melodies.

items.name: Indie veneto
items.lineage: Veneto indie connects independent artists across the northeastern Italian region. Alternative rock, melodic pop, post-rock and other approaches circulate through overlapping local networks, with artists including Post Nebbia, Talk to Her and C+C=Maxigross.
items.description: Voices, guitars, bass and drums provide one central ensemble, often expanded with keyboard colors. Melodic clarity, rhythmic drive and contrasting textures move between direct songs and more exploratory arrangements.

items.name: Indonesian bamboo
items.lineage: Indonesian bamboo music brings together distinct regional traditions that use bamboo as a sounding material. Struck tubes, shaken instruments and other local forms retain their own histories and social settings; Upper Jelai senggayung belongs to a fruit-harvest ritual practice rather than a single national ensemble standard.
items.description: Contrasting pitched attacks and resonances organize melodic and rhythmic patterns. In senggayung, paired tubes are struck together and selectively muted, combining different registers within memorized ensemble compositions.

items.name: Indonesian experimental
items.lineage: Indonesian experimental music connects acoustic traditions, electronic processes and environmental sound with contemporary exploratory practice. Artists such as Catu Daya bring gamelan-related resources into improvisatory and spatial sound work without replacing the distinct structures of traditional ensembles.
items.description: Bowed tones, resonant gongs, electronic textures and assembled field recordings interact in changing layers. Sustained sound and differences in attack, density and decay create movement beyond conventional song or dance structures.

items.name: Indonesian neo-psychedelia
items.lineage: Indonesian neo-psychedelia reimagines Indonesian folk and popular-music heritage through contemporary psychedelic production. Revival and diaspora projects such as Nusantara Beat connect archival listening and family histories with new songs, groove-oriented bands and electronic textures.
items.description: Voices, electric guitars, bass, keyboards and drums create a layered psychedelic sound. Samples and traditional instrumental colors can add contrasting resonance and rhythmic detail, linking current song forms with inherited melodic resources.

items.name: Indy Indie
items.lineage: Indy indie refers to Indianapolis independent rock and pop communities. Bands, local venues and benefit programmes connect musicians through shared performance spaces, while recordings circulate within Indiana’s wider independent-music networks.
items.description: Voices, guitars, bass and drums form direct, flexible song arrangements. Interacting vocal lines, repeated riffs and dynamic shifts move between melodic accessibility and alternative-rock weight.

items.name: Iranian experimental
items.lineage: Iranian experimental music connects composers, sound artists and exploratory bands across acoustic, electronic and mixed-media work. Platforms such as Zabte Sote link individual projects with a wider creative community, overlapping electronic composition without being limited to one technology.
items.description: Synthetic and acoustic resources can be reshaped through unusual timbres, structures and listening perspectives. In fully electronic work, contrasting synthesis methods create changing layers, spectral detail and shifting relationships between pitch, noise and rhythm.

items.name: Irish ballad
items.lineage: Irish ballads carry narrative songs through oral tradition, broadside circulation and modern folk performance. Stories of historical events, journeys, relationships and political experience move between solo singers, duets and accompanied groups, often sharing repertory with neighboring song traditions.
items.description: The voice guides attention through successive verses and recurring melodic phrases. Clear storytelling, changes in emphasis and interaction between singers can sustain the narrative with or without instrumental accompaniment.

items.name: Japanese instrumental
items.lineage: Japanese instrumental music is a broad wordless listening field crossing piano, guitar, traditional instruments and ensemble composition. Jazz interpretations, concert pieces and popular melodies circulate alongside newly written instrumental repertoire.
items.description: Melody and texture take the foreground without a required lead singer. A piano trio can combine chordal variation, plucked bass and brushed drums, while other branches use different acoustic or electronic ensembles.

items.name: Japanese prog
items.lineage: Japanese progressive rock encompasses composition-focused bands, experimental ensembles and free-rock collaborations. Artists including KENSO, Ars Nova, Ruins and Koenjihyakkei draw on differing progressive traditions rather than a single national sound.
items.description: Extended structures, changing rhythmic relationships and contrasting instrumental colors move beyond compact song forms. Guitar, bass and drums can develop material through improvisation, while other ensembles add keyboards, voices and more elaborate written arrangements.

items.name: Jesus movement
items.lineage: The Jesus Movement connected late-1960s and 1970s Christian revival communities with contemporary songs, bands and new recording networks. Groups such as Love Song and artists including Keith Green helped link personal devotional songwriting, communal worship and the emerging contemporary Christian music field.
items.description: Direct melodies and accessible harmonies support expressive singing and group participation. Piano or guitar can carry intimate devotional songs, while fuller rock arrangements bring the same repertoire into concerts and communal gatherings.

items.name: Jirai kei
items.lineage: Jirai kei connects a Japanese fashion and fan aesthetic with popular music, online covers and idol performance. Vocaloid producers, human singers and idol acts share parts of this discovery network, with visual presentation and audience identification linking otherwise varied musical approaches.
items.description: Catchy sung melodies, electronic rhythm and vivid instrumental colors support an emotionally heightened pop presentation. Synthesized or human voices can carry the songs, with covers and rearrangements offering different relationships between music and character.

items.name: Jumptek
items.lineage: Jumptek connects Jump and Tek or tekstyle repertoire through Belgian and Dutch hard-dance communities and their wider circulation. Producers, club programmes and DJs bring related rhythmic styles together, overlapping jumpstyle without being confined to its dance demonstrations.
items.description: Firm electronic kicks and sharply articulated synth figures establish a forceful pulse. Repetition, accent changes and contrasting sections emphasize rhythmic impact and movement within compact hard-dance arrangements.

items.name: Junior songfestival
items.lineage: Junior Songfestival is the Dutch national junior-song competition and its audition, finalist and performance repertoire. Broadcasters and young performers develop songs through a pathway that connects local songwriting with the wider televised European junior-pop setting.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies and recurring hooks are central, whether presented with piano accompaniment or fuller electronic and band production. Arrangement changes can move a song from intimate audition delivery to a larger stage presentation.

items.name: Kalmar indie
items.lineage: Kalmar indie connects independent music across the southeastern Swedish region, including the Västervik area. Its varied artists encompass pop, rock and roots-oriented songwriting, sharing regional connections without a single required style.
items.description: Voices and acoustic strings can form a warm song-centered texture with bass, drums and steel-guitar responses. Other branches favor electric bands or electronic production, while melodic songwriting links different approaches.

items.name: Kannada bhava geethe
items.lineage: Kannada bhava geethe sets modern Kannada literary poetry to composed melodies. Singers and composers foreground a poem’s emotional expression and language, drawing on varied musical resources without simply reproducing film song or classical concert forms.
items.description: A clear melodic voice carries the text with intimate accompaniment. Flute, harmonium and tabla can provide melodic responses, sustained support and rhythmic shape while leaving the poem in the foreground.

items.name: KC indie
items.lineage: KC indie is the independent-music network of the Kansas City metropolitan area across Kansas and Missouri. Loud guitar groups, melodic pop bands and other independent artists share local venues, studios and audiences within a scene broader than any one ensemble.
items.description: Singing, guitar, bass and drums offer a direct band foundation. Riffs, hooks and contrasting dynamics move between abrasive rock textures and more melodic passages, with arrangements varying across the community.

items.name: Kent indie
items.lineage: Kent indie connects independent musicians, venues and labels across the county, including the Deal and Kingsdown circuit. Acoustic songwriters and electric bands share local networks within the wider British independent scene.
items.description: Narrative singing and acoustic guitar offer an intimate branch of the repertoire, while other groups build songs around fuller bands. Melodic accompaniment and flexible dynamics leave room for words and individual vocal character.

items.name: Korean superband
items.lineage: Korean superband is the collaborative musician community formed around JTBC’s Superband competition. Instrumentalists, singers and songwriters develop groups across styles rather than following a single rock-band formula.
items.description: Contrasting instrumental colors and vocal melodies meet in newly arranged songs. Piano-supported singing offers one accessible texture, while guitars, strings and rhythm sections expand the ensemble in other performances.

items.name: Korean worship
items.lineage: Korean worship brings Christian praise songs into Korean-language church life and music ministries. Contemporary songwriters and congregations share repertoire that also circulates through recordings, choirs and instrumental arrangements.
items.description: Sung prayer and recurring melodic phrases invite participation. Piano can sustain the harmony beneath a lead or group of voices, with restrained accompaniment leaving space for words and collective expression.

items.name: Lagu Sasak
items.lineage: Lagu Sasak encompasses Sasak-language songs from Lombok, linking contemporary pop bands with local-language musical traditions. Musicians use familiar language and stories in arrangements that cross pop, regional entertainment and other styles.
items.description: Voices lead melodic songs over guitar, bass, keyboards and drums in contemporary band settings. Clear hooks and rhythmic accompaniment support the text, while other branches use different local instrumental combinations.

items.name: Lampung Indie
items.lineage: Lampung indie connects local bands, organizers and creative communities within Indonesia’s independent music scene. Pop, folk and rock approaches circulate through regional performances and independently issued recordings.
items.description: Singing and guitar can sit over bass and drums in a light, melodic band texture. Acoustic colors and contrasting instrumental responses support direct songs without prescribing one arrangement for the whole scene.

items.name: Latin Christian
items.lineage: Latin Christian music links Spanish-language Christian artists, churches and ministries across national borders. Worship, gospel, pop, rock and rap coexist within a broad devotional and recording network.
items.description: Voices carry prayers, testimony and praise through familiar song forms. Piano-supported singing provides a reflective setting, while bands, choirs and electronic production give other parts of the repertoire more rhythmic or expansive textures.

items.name: Louisville Underground
items.lineage: Louisville underground developed through connected punk, hardcore and experimental-rock communities, with shared musicians, labels, venues and independent publications. Groups such as Slint, Rodan and Shipping News helped sustain a network that crosses stylistic boundaries.
items.description: Interlocking guitars, bass and drums support vocals through riffs, abrupt contrasts and changing densities. Repetition and tension can matter as much as conventional hooks, with instrumental passages opening space for ensemble interaction.

items.name: Maithili
items.lineage: Maithili music draws on the language and literary traditions of Mithila, spanning devotional poetry, folk song and contemporary repertoire. Vidyapati’s Krishna poetry has also circulated through neighboring devotional singing traditions.
items.description: An expressive voice can carry poetic texts over khol accompaniment in a devotional setting. Melodic phrasing and responsive drum patterns support the words, while other parts of the repertoire use different ensembles and secular themes.

items.name: Malayalam worship
items.lineage: Malayalam worship connects Christian devotional songs with Malayalam-speaking congregations and music ministries. Church repertoire, devotional film songs and contemporary compositions circulate through choral, a cappella and accompanied arrangements.
items.description: Lead singing and supporting voices can weave melody with harmonic and rhythmic accompaniment. Clear text and shared phrases support devotional expression, whether performed by an unaccompanied vocal group or a larger ensemble.

items.name: Meme music
items.lineage: Meme music forms a changing repertoire through online quotation, remixing and humorous recontextualization. Older pop songs, game and film themes, novelty recordings and instrumental tunes can acquire new meanings through repeated reuse.
items.description: Recognizable hooks and abrupt associations help listeners identify a reference. Piano arrangements expose familiar melodies and harmony, while other versions use voices, electronic sounds, edits or intentionally exaggerated performance.

items.name: Middle-earth music
items.lineage: Middle-earth music gathers songs, screen scores and concert works associated with Tolkien’s imagined world. Film adaptations and independent interpretations connect vocal songwriting with large-scale instrumental and symphonic traditions.
items.description: Memorable themes, expansive phrases and contrasting textures evoke places and characters. Voice with piano can present a song intimately, while orchestral, choral and other instrumental settings offer different scales of storytelling.

items.name: Mluvené slovo
items.lineage: Mluvené slovo is the Czech spoken-word publishing field, encompassing literary narration and other recorded voice forms. It includes adult fiction as well as children’s stories, dramatic readings and related spoken repertoire.
items.description: A clear speaking voice shapes narrative through pacing, emphasis and changes of character. Unaccompanied reading focuses attention on language, while other productions may involve multiple voices or supporting sound.

items.name: Mongolian alternative
items.lineage: Mongolian alternative connects contemporary independent and alternative musicians, including Ulaanbaatar’s guitar-oriented scene. Bands and songwriters combine local community ties with varied rock and pop approaches.
items.description: Vocals, guitars, bass and drums create direct songs with melodic hooks and contrasting dynamics. Raw amplified textures can sit beside more intimate passages, without requiring traditional overtone singing or one common instrumental style.

items.name: Chill-Out Trance
items.lineage: Chill-out trance connects trance repertoire with relaxed listening, including reinterpretations of vocal-trance songs. Remixers and labels such as Seven24’s network, RNM and Suanda link melodic dance music with atmospheric listening arrangements.
items.description: Sustained synth harmony and restrained electronic rhythm leave space around melodic material. Layers develop gradually, with softened attacks and spacious production offering an alternative to the pressure of a dance-floor arrangement.

items.name: Indonesian indigenous traditional
items.lineage: Indonesian indigenous traditions encompass many distinct local musical cultures, including communal vocal poetry, instrumental ensembles and dance repertoires. Language, social occasions and inherited performance practices connect music with particular communities.
items.description: A solo voice and responding chorus can shape extended poetic verses, as in Kenyah communal singing. Layered voices and parallel melodic movement offer one texture within a much wider range of regional practices.

items.name: Japanese beats
items.lineage: Japanese beats connects beatmakers, DJs and independent labels through sample-based production and record culture. Networks such as Jazzy Sport bring hip-hop into contact with jazz, soul, house and experimental electronic approaches.
items.description: Layered samples, shaped drum patterns and recurring melodic fragments create compact rhythmic pieces. Texture, timing and variation give instrumental beats their character, while other releases add rap, singing or longer mixed programmes.

items.name: Japanese traditional
items.lineage: Japanese traditional music gathers distinct historical lineages, including court music, theater, vocal repertoire and instrumental schools. Transmission through teachers and communities preserves contrasting instruments, techniques and aesthetic approaches.
items.description: Shakuhachi offers a breath-shaped solo branch, with flexible pitch shading, sustained tones and pauses. Koto, voices and larger ensembles produce other textures across the broader traditional repertoire.

items.name: Japanese VTuber
items.lineage: Japanese VTuber music grows from avatar-mediated streaming performers and their production communities. Virtual idols and independent talents sing original songs and covers, collaborating with songwriters and producers across popular styles.
items.description: Expressive singing, memorable hooks and vivid electronic accompaniment support performances that link music with an on-screen character. Synthesizers and programmed rhythm offer one common pop texture, alongside acoustic and band arrangements.

items.name: Kazakh indie
items.lineage: Kazakh indie connects independent songwriters and bands within Kazakhstan’s contemporary music scene. Kazakh-language songs circulate through intimate performances, recorded releases and collaborations that cross folk, rock and electronic approaches.
items.description: Voice and guitar can place words and melody in the foreground. Restrained accompaniment and shifting dynamics support personal expression, while other arrangements expand into fuller band or electronic textures.

items.name: Lagu Madura
items.lineage: Lagu Madura encompasses Madurese-language song, including community play-songs and later popular or concert interpretations. Regional language and repertoire link varied arrangements without requiring a single ensemble.
items.description: Shared melodies and memorable text support individual or communal singing. Choral settings can distribute phrases across several parts, using imitation, layered harmony and vocal slides to develop familiar material.

items.name: Lagu Timur
items.lineage: Lagu Timur connects contemporary song repertoires across Eastern Indonesia, including Nusa Tenggara, Papua and Maluku. Musicians draw on regional identity and local musical resources while participating in wider Indonesian popular music.
items.description: Singing can blend acoustic guitar and keyboards with programmed sound, percussion and strings. Melodic hooks and layered accompaniment connect contemporary song structures with varied regional colors.

items.name: Latincore
items.lineage: Latincore connects Latin American punk, hardcore and melodic-core communities through touring, independent releases and shared audiences. Argentine, Chilean, Mexican and other scenes overlap within a transnational network of guitar-driven music.
items.description: Emphatic singing and group responses ride over distorted guitars, bass and drums. Driving riffs and melodic passages create contrast, with rhythmic intensity supporting both direct hooks and longer developments.

items.name: Latintronica
items.lineage: Latintronica connects Latin American roots repertoires with electronic production across national borders. Cumbia reworking, Andean materials, folk reinterpretation and ambient approaches circulate through overlapping producer and festival networks.
items.description: Layered samples and electronic rhythms reshape acoustic colors and familiar melodic fragments. Repetition, texture and gradual changes can support dancing or more atmospheric listening, without requiring every piece to follow one regional rhythm.

items.name: Liechtenstein
items.lineage: Liechtenstein’s musical life includes historical composition, contemporary popular groups and national ensembles. Institutions and repertoire traditions connect these contrasting practices, with Josef Gabriel Rheinberger an important figure in its composed-music heritage.
items.description: Romantic organ music offers one branch, combining sustained harmony, contrapuntal lines and broad changes in registration. Other parts of the national repertoire use voices, bands or chamber ensembles and follow different musical forms.
exemplars: Josef Gabriel Rheinberger — complete Organ Sonata No.15, op.168; Carus50.168/00

items.lineage: Lustrum songs are associated with anniversaries of Dutch student organizations. Commissioned or collectively adopted songs connect association identity, celebration and wider popular-music circulation.
items.description: Lead and group singing carry memorable refrains over energetic popular accompaniment. Piano, bass-synth figures and electronic drums can form a compact foundation, with other arrangements adding brass, strings or sampled effects.

items.name: Malaysian Traditional
items.lineage: Malaysian traditional music encompasses distinct regional and community repertoires, including the oral traditions of Sarawak. Songs and instrumental practices pass between generations while also reaching contemporary stages and new arrangements.
items.description: Voice with sape offers an intimate story-bearing texture, joining melodic singing with plucked resonance. Other Malaysian traditions use different ensembles, languages and ceremonial or social settings.

items.name: Marathi Remix
items.lineage: Marathi remix connects Marathi-language songs with electronic reworking and dance-floor circulation. Producers reinterpret familiar repertoire through house, techno, trance and other club approaches, extending regional songs into new listening settings.
items.description: Repeated samples, electronic percussion and contrasting sections emphasize recognizable hooks and rhythmic movement. Layering and edits can transform a song’s texture while preserving a melodic or vocal reference.

items.name: Montana roots
items.lineage: Montana roots connects regional folk, country, bluegrass and acoustic-song communities. Songwriters and ensembles circulate through local performances and recordings, drawing on shared roots traditions while developing individual approaches.
items.description: Voice and acoustic guitar can foreground stories and melodic phrasing. Strummed harmony and flexible dynamics provide an intimate foundation, while other groups expand the texture with strings, bass and drums.

items.name: Moroccan traditional
items.lineage: Moroccan traditional music encompasses distinct Amazigh, Arab, Gnawa, Andalusi and Moroccan Jewish repertoires. Community transmission and social or ceremonial settings sustain diverse vocal and instrumental lineages.
items.description: An unaccompanied narrative romance offers one intimate vocal branch, with melodic turns supporting the unfolding text. Other traditions use percussion, strings, wind instruments or larger ensembles with their own forms and occasions.

items.name: Motivation
items.lineage: Motivation connects spoken recordings and readings directed toward encouragement, self-development and practical reflection. Historical self-help writing, contemporary talks and personal testimony offer contrasting approaches to this purpose-based listening field.
items.description: A speaking voice uses pacing and emphasis to organize ideas and address the listener. Reflective narration can be calm and conversational, while other presentations use greater rhetorical intensity or supporting music.

items.name: Multidisciplinary
items.lineage: Multidisciplinary music connects artists whose work crosses composition, visual art, design, performance and other practices. Methods and ideas move between media, producing varied forms rather than one common instrumental style.
items.description: Piano composition can explore space, repetition and changing resonance, while other artists use voices, electronics or sculptural sound. The relationship between musical material and another creative practice shapes each work’s character.

items.name: Música blumenauense
items.lineage: Música blumenauense connects Blumenau’s musicians, venues and independent cultural organizations. Authorial music ranges from rock to MPB and acoustic pop, with regional collaboration supporting varied approaches.
items.description: Voices and guitars can combine with bass, cello and percussion in a melodic song texture. Acoustic and electric colors alternate between support and response, while other local groups develop different ensembles and styles.

items.name: Musica calabrese
items.lineage: Musica calabrese encompasses Calabrian regional repertoire, including dialect storytelling, sentimental song and dance music. Folk revivals and contemporary performers renew songs associated with local history and social life.
items.description: Voice and guitar can bring narrative and language to the foreground through flexible phrasing and direct accompaniment. Dance-oriented branches use stronger repeated rhythms, while reflective songs leave more space around the text.

items.name: Música capixaba
items.lineage: Música capixaba is the cross-style music community of Espírito Santo, connecting popular music, regional scenes and experimental practice. Universities, labels and cultural organizations provide settings for collaboration across these approaches.
items.description: An experimental ensemble can combine processed voices, guitars, bass and electronic sources with live sound manipulation. Sustained textures and changing layers create interaction between performers, while other capixaba branches favor direct song or dance forms.

items.name: Música caririense
items.lineage: Música caririense connects the musical communities of Ceará’s Cariri region, including songwriting, percussion, rock and experimental work. Local artists and independent labels bring these approaches into shared circulation.
items.description: Looped guitar improvisation offers one exploratory branch, using delay and resonance to build changing layers. A foot-played jingle pulse can accompany the guitar, while other regional groups use different acoustic and electric ensembles.

items.name: Música cearense
items.lineage: Música cearense connects Ceará’s cross-style musical community, from acoustic song and popular repertoire to forró and experimental groups. Regional artists, labels and performances link local repertoires with broader Brazilian musical currents.
items.description: Singing with steel-string guitar can present songs directly, using ringing chords and small melodic inflections. Fuller bands and other instrumental combinations expand the range of textures across the regional field.

items.name: Música chiapaneca
items.lineage: Música chiapaneca encompasses the regional repertoires and musical communities of Chiapas. Marimba ensembles, Indigenous-language songs, strings, winds and percussion contribute distinct traditions within this wider field.
items.description: A marimba-led instrumental ensemble can combine interlocking wooden-keyboard lines with bass, bright glockenspiel color and percussion. Song and dance melodies circulate through contrasting arrangements, alongside other regional vocal and instrumental practices.

items.name: Música colombiana instrumental
items.lineage: Música colombiana instrumental gathers instrumental repertoires across Colombia, including piano, string ensembles, harp-associated traditions and orchestral arrangements. Composers and performers reinterpret regional forms alongside concert music.
items.description: Piano can carry melody, harmonic movement and contrasting phrases in a compact instrumental setting. Other ensembles distribute these roles among plucked strings, winds or larger groups, reflecting varied regional and compositional traditions.

items.name: Música moçambicana
items.lineage: Música moçambicana connects Mozambique’s traditional, popular and contemporary musical communities, including artists working across borders. Marrabenta, sung repertoire, electronic collaborations and rap contribute to a broad national and diaspora field.
items.description: Voices and plucked accompaniment can interact with electronic textures in contemporary song arrangements. Shared melodic phrases and changing layers support the text, while dance bands and other regional ensembles offer different rhythmic foundations.

items.name: Música paranaense
items.lineage: Música paranaense connects Paraná’s varied musical communities, including songwriters, bands and concert performers. Local institutions and artists sustain regional networks within broader Brazilian musical life.
items.description: Voice and acoustic guitar provide an intimate setting for lyrical songs. Melodic accompaniment and flexible phrasing place words in the foreground, while other regional performers work with larger bands or instrumental ensembles.

items.name: Musica per bambini
items.lineage: Musica per bambini connects Italian children’s musical publishing and performance, including songs, lullabies, choral repertoire and narrated musical stories. Educational and cultural institutions bring these forms to different ages and listening settings.
items.description: Spoken narration with piano can shape a story through pacing, musical responses and changes in mood. Other works use singing, repeated refrains or group participation, offering contrasting ways to connect words and music.

items.name: Música piauiense
items.lineage: Música piauiense connects Piauí’s musicians and cultural networks across rock, popular song and rhythmic Brazilian traditions. Artists combine local community ties with influences including samba-rock, funk, baião, soul and reggae.
items.description: A singing voice can lead a guitar, bass and drum ensemble through rhythmic songs. Clean guitar patterns, a firm bass foundation and varied drum articulation support melodic phrases and changes in groove.

items.name: Mùsica piemontèisa
items.lineage: Mùsica piemontèisa encompasses Piedmontese regional-language song and community repertoire, including narratives, rhymes and dance-related traditions. Publications, recordings and performers sustain these materials through revival and contemporary interpretation.
items.description: Voice with guitar can present words directly through melodic accompaniment and changing emphasis. Solo recitals coexist with choral and instrumental settings, reflecting the range of regional repertoire.

items.name: Música pitiusa
items.lineage: Música Pitiusa connects the repertoires of Ibiza and Formentera, including traditional dance music, song and later revival or popular approaches. Island communities and cultural organizations sustain distinct practices within the wider Catalan-speaking musical world.
items.description: In ball pagès, a one-handed flute and drum interact with large castanets to support dance. Repeated melodic fragments and rhythmic elaboration shape the performance, while other island repertoires use voices or different instrumental combinations.

items.name: Música puntana
items.lineage: Música puntana connects the repertoire and musical communities of San Luis, including traditions shared with the wider Cuyo region. Regional songs, poetry and contemporary concert arrangements sustain a varied provincial field.
items.description: Voices and guitars can combine with bass, piano and percussion in a melodic song ensemble. Instrumental responses and shared vocal phrases support regional texts, while other settings favor more intimate accompaniment.

items.name: Música rapa nui
items.lineage: Música Rapa Nui encompasses the island’s inherited and contemporary musical expressions. Artists connect local language and identity with folk, rock, blues and other influences, working across acoustic and amplified settings.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices can ride over electric guitars, bass, drums and percussion. Melodic hooks and rhythmic accompaniment carry contemporary songs, alongside other island practices with different textures and occasions.

items.name: Música sudcaliforniana
items.lineage: Música sudcaliforniana connects Baja California Sur’s regional repertoire, including corridos, campirano and contemporary popular music. Local narratives and community performance link acoustic groups with broader Mexican song traditions.
items.description: A singer with guitar and requinto can be supported by the rounded bass pulse of a tuba. Plucked melodic responses and clear text shape an intimate regional-song texture, with other ensembles offering different arrangements.

items.name: Música tabasqueña
items.lineage: Música tabasqueña gathers Tabasco’s regional repertoire, including the tamborilero traditions maintained through community performance and cultural transmission. Indigenous and mestizo practices meet in ceremonial, social and dance settings.
items.description: Cane flute carries melodies over contrasting small and large drums. Repeating patterns and changes of accent support danza, son and zapateo, with ensemble size and additional instruments varying between contexts.

items.name: Música tradicional cubana
items.lineage: Música tradicional cubana encompasses interrelated Cuban song and dance repertoires, including bolero, son, habanera, guajira and guaracha. Troubadours, trios, larger popular ensembles and other performers sustain contrasting approaches within this broad field.
items.description: Harmonizing voices, guitar, tres and percussion can form a compact traditional-song texture. Plucked responses and repeated rhythmic figures support melody and text, while larger groups add other instrumental colors.

items.name: Musical advocacy
items.lineage: Musical advocacy connects repertoire organized around public causes, collective action and charitable support. Multi-artist projects and community performances bring songs across pop, rock, choral and other traditions into new social contexts.
items.description: Shared singing and memorable refrains can emphasize participation and solidarity. Piano-supported voices offer a direct setting, while larger bands and ensembles expand the musical scale of a performance.

items.name: Músicas espíritas
items.lineage: Músicas espíritas connects Brazilian Spiritist artists, study groups and devotional performance. Songs circulate through concerts, recordings and religious education, engaging with reflection and Spiritist interpretations of spiritual life.
items.description: Voices and acoustic guitar can create an intimate devotional texture. Melodic phrases and responsive accompaniment support the words, with duets, solo singing and fuller arrangements providing different settings.

items.name: Musiqi-ye Zanān
items.lineage: Musiqi-ye zanān gathers Iranian and Persian women’s voices across traditional, popular and contemporary music. Singers connect poetic repertoire, personal expression and varied performance communities without sharing one required style or political position.
items.description: An unaccompanied voice can bring the contour and language of a poem into focus. Other settings add acoustic or electronic accompaniment, while vocal phrasing remains central across contrasting approaches.

items.name: Musique alsacienne
items.lineage: Musique alsacienne connects Alsace’s regional dances, dialect songs and ensemble traditions. Musicians and arrangers transmit repertoire shaped by French and German musical exchange, including polkas, marches and Rhinländer.
items.description: Accordion can carry dance melodies and harmonic support through articulated bellows phrases. Solo and duo arrangements coexist with wind ensembles and sung repertoire, creating different textures around familiar regional forms.

items.name: Musique centrafricaine
items.lineage: Musique centrafricaine encompasses the Central African Republic’s varied communities and contemporary musical life. Aka, Banda, Gbaya, Ngbaka and other repertoires coexist with urban song and popular music.
items.description: A solo vocal line offers one intimate branch, with melodic elaboration shaped by inherited patterns and phrasing. Other practices use interlocking voices, instruments or rhythmic ensembles, reflecting different social settings and traditions.

items.name: Musique mahoraise
items.lineage: Musique mahoraise connects Mayotte’s music and Shimaoré-language song with its wider Comorian and diaspora relationships. Traditional repertoire and contemporary songwriting meet influences such as reggae and other popular styles.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices can combine with guitar, bass, keyboards and hand percussion in an acoustic ensemble. Alternating melodic colors and repeated phrases support songs, while other performers use different local instrumental and vocal textures.

items.name: Musique militaire
items.lineage: Musique militaire encompasses music maintained and performed by military institutions, including signals, ceremonial ensembles, singing and public concerts. Repertoire ranges from functional calls and marches to choral works and wider popular or concert music.
items.description: A choir with piano offers one concert branch, using coordinated phrasing and changing vocal density. Wind bands, percussion and signaling instruments serve other ceremonial and public roles within the broader institutional field.

items.name: Musique tchadienne
items.lineage: Musique tchadienne connects Chad’s varied song traditions and contemporary performers. Local languages and French circulate through national touring and cultural networks, with heritage-rooted material meeting popular influences.
items.description: Voices, guitar and percussion can create a direct song texture with melodic responses and rhythmic support. Duets and small groups offer intimate settings, while other ensembles develop fuller arrangements.

items.name: Musique traditionnelle comorienne
items.lineage: Musique traditionnelle comorienne encompasses inherited practices across domestic, ceremonial, dance and devotional life in the Comorian islands. Songs and instrumental traditions take distinct forms according to community and occasion.
items.description: Voice with firimbi flute can shape an intimate domestic-song texture. Sustained flute phrases and melodic singing provide one setting, alongside larger vocal and percussion practices elsewhere in the repertoire.

items.name: Musique urbaine Kinshasa
items.lineage: Musique urbaine Kinshasa connects contemporary Congolese urban song, rap and electronic dance networks. Artists and DJs circulate between local scenes and wider African club influences, with the named field extending beyond a single city’s residents.
items.description: Layered rhythmic material and electronic percussion support melodies, vocal references and changing club textures. Repetition and edits can connect different styles within a production, while live bands and singers shape other branches of the urban repertoire.

items.name: Muzică bisericească
items.lineage: Muzica bisericească connects Romanian church-music repertoires, including psaltic chant and harmonic choral practice. Regional transmission and institutional publications sustain liturgical material across different vocal approaches.
items.description: Unaccompanied voices shape sacred text through connected phrases and melodic elaboration. Solo, group and choral textures vary by repertoire, with different relationships between sustained lines, rhythm and harmony.

items.name: Muzică creștină
items.lineage: Muzica creștină connects Romanian Christian recording, worship and outreach communities. Contemporary bands, soloists and choirs circulate devotional repertoire through churches, public events and recordings.
items.description: Singing with keyboards can carry familiar praise melodies, while saxophone and other instruments offer responses or instrumental interpretations. Repeated phrases and clear melodic lines support communal and reflective listening.

items.name: Muzica moldoveneasca
items.lineage: Muzica moldovenească connects Moldavian regional song and dance heritage with contemporary circulation. Folk collections, community performance and popular reinterpretations span a field broader than any one ensemble or national pop style.
items.description: Unaccompanied singing can bring melodic phrases and text into focus. Dance-oriented ensembles and other accompanied settings provide contrasting rhythmic and harmonic textures across the repertoire.

items.name: Muzika l’yeladim
items.lineage: Muzika l’yeladim encompasses Hebrew and Israeli children’s musical repertoire, including educational songs, festival material, lullabies and concert arrangements. Songs circulate between family, school, broadcast and performance settings.
items.description: A choir and flute can exchange clear melodic phrases in a composed arrangement. Repetition and expressive word-setting support the text, while other versions use solo singing, instrumental accompaniment or group participation.

items.name: Nederlandse hardstyle
items.lineage: Nederlandse hardstyle connects Dutch-language popular songs, carnival repertoire and communal celebration with hardstyle production. Remixers and event networks bring familiar vocal material into hard-dance contexts.
items.description: Sung hooks and group refrains meet forceful electronic kicks and sharply defined synthesizer figures. Repetition, breaks and changes in intensity connect recognizable songs with an energetic dance pulse.

items.name: Nederreggae
items.lineage: Nederreggae connects reggae performers and audiences in the Netherlands and neighboring Low Countries. Dutch-language songs and multilingual circulation link local bands with the wider reggae tradition.
items.description: Rhythmic guitar chords, bass and drums support voices and keyboards, with horns adding responses and accents. Ensemble phrasing balances repeated accompaniment with melodic and vocal movement.

items.name: NepHop
items.lineage: NepHop connects Nepali-language hip-hop communities in Nepal and the diaspora, including recorded songs, live performance and battle rap. MCs, producers and organizers sustain local networks and exchanges with wider hip-hop practice.
items.description: Rhythmic spoken delivery, wordplay and contrasting flows shape verses over beats. Unaccompanied battles and call-and-response performance provide another branch, emphasizing verbal timing and direct interaction.

items.name: Normal indie
items.lineage: Normal indie connects independent musicians associated with Normal, Illinois, including The Normals and Andrew Osenga. Local roots and collaborations link the community with wider American indie and singer-songwriter networks.
items.description: Acoustic strumming and layered human voices support melodic songs. Intimate solo passages and communal refrains offer contrasting textures within the broader regional scene.

items.name: Norsk lovsang
items.lineage: Norsk lovsang connects Norwegian church songwriters, worship bands and congregations through local ministries and national networks. Contemporary songs circulate alongside hymn and gospel traditions across denominations.
items.description: Lead singing and congregational refrains rise over keyboards, guitar, bass and drums. Repeated melodic phrases and harmonic support encourage shared participation, with quieter devotional passages providing contrast.

items.name: North Alabama indie
items.lineage: North Alabama indie connects independent musicians around Huntsville, the Tennessee Valley and neighboring northern Alabama communities. Local radio, venues and collaborations support varied rock and song-oriented projects.

items.name: Northeast Indian indie
items.lineage: Northeast Indian indie connects independent artists and performance networks across India’s northeastern states. Festivals, venues and collaborations support diverse songwriting and musical identities within a shared regional field.

items.name: Northern Irish indie
items.lineage: Northern Irish indie connects independent artists, venues, recordings and music institutions across Northern Ireland. Belfast is one important center within a wider regional network that overlaps Irish and British independent music.
items.description: Voices, electric guitar, bass and drums carry melodic songs, with piano adding harmonic weight and contrast. Arrangements move between intimate phrases and fuller ensemble passages across indie-pop and rock approaches.

items.name: Northwest China indie
items.lineage: Northwest China indie connects independent musicians and audiences across the region, including Xi’an’s post-punk and psychedelic networks. Local scenes and labels link contrasting regional backgrounds with wider Chinese independent music.

items.name: Norwegian experimental
items.lineage: Norwegian experimental connects artist-run composition and improvisation networks, including the SOFA label and exploratory concert practice. The field overlaps jazz, contemporary composition and other experimental traditions.
