items.lineage: Colombian folklore brings together regional song, dance and instrumental traditions transmitted through communities, performance and teaching. Andean and coastal repertoires retain distinct rhythmic identities while circulating through national anthologies and new arrangements.
items.description: Regional melodies and dance rhythms recur in contrasting instrumental and vocal forms. The traditional Andean string trio sets the bright bandola against ringing tiple and guitar accompaniment, one established ensemble within the country’s much wider folk heritage.

items.name: CZSK Emo Rap
items.lineage: Czech and Slovak emo rap connects confessional writing with the region’s independent rap and alternative-music networks. Local-language releases and cross-border radio sessions bring emotionally direct rap into contact with punk, electronic music and melodic pop.
items.description: Intimate or urgent verses address relationships, anxiety and personal uncertainty over producer-built beats. Rapping can alternate with melodic hooks; dark electronic textures and rock influences vary between artists. A direct rhythmic vocal and produced accompaniment represent the rapped branch.

items.name: Musik Anak-Anak
items.lineage: Indonesian children’s music joins composed songs, classroom participation and family entertainment. Educators and songwriters including Ibu Sud and Pak Kasur helped establish a familiar repertoire, extended through television, recordings and newer independent projects.
items.description: Clear sung melodies, memorable repetition and accessible accompaniment support play, learning and shared family listening. Indonesian-language songs about everyday life and imagination circulate alongside regional children’s repertoires, with piano-led singing offering one enduring format.

items.name: Tibetan Folk Pop
items.lineage: Tibetan folk pop carries familiar Tibetan song traditions into contemporary recordings, concerts and diaspora songwriting. Performers such as Techung connect inherited melodies and Tibetan-language poetry with new compositions and collaborations, sustaining links between cultural memory and present-day popular listening.
items.description: Expressive singing and memorable melodic phrases foreground Tibetan words and folk-derived contours. Acoustic instruments and modern accompaniment coexist; intimate voice-and-piano settings emphasize the song text, while other arrangements retain plucked lutes or use larger contemporary ensembles.

items.name: Telugu Devotional
items.lineage: Telugu devotional music brings sacred poetry and praise into temple worship, community singing, concerts and recordings. Annamacharya and later saint-poets remain important sources, with classical settings, folk-derived songs and newer arrangements circulating through religious institutions and popular devotional media.
items.description: Devotional words and singable melodic contours support praise, contemplation and shared religious life. Raga-shaped ornament and a steady drone enrich the classical vocal branch, with violin responses and hand-drum accompaniment; folk and popular arrangements give the wider repertoire other textures.

items.name: Pop Boliviano
items.lineage: Pop boliviano connects Bolivian popular-song performers with local, regional and diaspora audiences. Songwriters work across intimate acoustic settings, bands and contemporary studio production.
items.description: Lead melodies and recurring refrains can sit over supportive keyboard harmony. A voice-and-piano setting brings the song and its phrasing forward, while other performers use broader instrumental arrangements.

items.name: Cantautor Català
items.lineage: Catalan singer-songwriter music draws on the chanson-linked Nova Cançó and the folk revival, with later authors extending its poetic, personal and social concerns into acoustic song, pop and experimental arrangements.
items.description: Words and melodic phrasing lead this varied author-song tradition. Guitar or piano can frame an intimate performance, while fuller bands and electronic textures support other branches. This profile uses expressive singing with restrained piano accompaniment.

items.name: Lagu Bugis
items.lineage: Bugis-language song carries poetic expression, advice and community memory in South Sulawesi. Traditional melodies continue in domestic singing, contemporary popular arrangements and choral presentations of regional repertoire.
items.description: Melody and Bugis-language phrasing carry the song, with personal feeling and shared cultural values held in the lyric. This profile represents the vocal-ensemble branch: connected group singing lets the text and melodic line remain prominent without making a particular choir size or harmonization universal.

items.name: Finnish Trap
items.lineage: Finnish trap localizes the bass-heavy, electronically produced rap style within Finland’s hip-hop networks. Performers combine locally inflected slang and spontaneous vocal cadences with contemporary trap production, alongside melodic and pop-facing branches.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal phrases sit over deep electronic kick-bass, crisp programmed percussion and synthesizer melodic phrases. Sparse spaces between phrases heighten the low end and vocal cadence; melodic hooks and denser production appear in other branches.

items.name: Greek Drill
items.lineage: Greek drill connects contemporary drill production with Greek-language rap and local urban scenes. Collaborating MCs and producers adapt its dark rhythmic spaces to neighborhood narratives, social observation and personal expression, while crossing into other rap styles.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal phrases press against sparse, weighty beats, with pauses and changes of cadence sharpening their impact. Greek slang and local references sit alongside varied lyrical subjects; melodic hooks and other production approaches remain part of the wider scene.

items.name: Iowa Hip Hop
items.lineage: Iowa hip-hop connects local rappers, producers, studios and independent performance spaces across cities including Davenport, Des Moines and Cedar Rapids. Artists develop regional voices within wider American rap networks, with boom-bap, contemporary trap and experimental production all circulating through the scene.
items.description: Foreground rap verses meet producer-built rhythms and recurring hooks. Beat textures and vocal approaches vary across the scene, from direct sample-oriented storytelling to more electronic and melodic approaches. This straightforward MC-and-beat branch leaves room for the words and rhythmic delivery.

items.name: Irish drill
items.lineage: Irish drill developed through local rappers and producer networks adapting the Chicago- and UK-derived style. Artists including Offica and A92 connect Irish experience with African diasporic influences, while distinct accents, rhythmic choices and online collaboration shape the scene.
items.description: Rhythmic rap rides a forceful produced beat with prominent low end and sharply placed percussion. Bouncy rhythmic shapes can bring an Afrobeats inflection, while vocal cadence and local references distinguish individual performers.

items.name: Swiss Trap
items.lineage: Swiss trap develops bass-heavy programmed rap within Switzerland’s multilingual music networks. Artists such as Pronto combine locally inflected delivery with international trap influences, while collaborations and pop, dancehall and Afro-oriented branches cross national and language borders.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines move over electronic low end, crisp programmed percussion and short synthesizer melodies. Repetition and open spaces frame the vocal cadence, with melodic hooks and denser production appearing across the wider scene.

items.name: Persian Drill
items.lineage: Persian drill brings drill rap into Persian-language and diasporic networks. Exchanges between Iran and overseas scenes, including London, support forceful rhythmic delivery and local identity alongside bilingual expression and varied personal subjects.
items.description: Clipped or flowing rap phrases ride sparse, hard-edged beats, with vocal emphasis and spaces between lines shaping the momentum. Persian speech rhythms and bilingual passages localize the delivery; melodic inflections and contrasting lyrical subjects vary across artists.

items.name: Indie Curitibano
items.lineage: Curitiba’s independent music scene connects local songwriters, bands and producers through collaborative releases, cultural spaces and festivals. Its author-led repertoire spans alternative rock, intimate Brazilian song, folk-inflected pop and electronic or hip-hop production.
items.description: Personal melodies and distinctive vocal phrasing move between intimate acoustic textures, guitar-band arrangements and electronically shaped pop. This gentle song branch pairs a singing lead with chordal piano, leaving space around the words and melody.

items.name: Classic Ukrainian Pop
items.lineage: Ukraine’s classic pop repertoire grew through estrada singers, songwriters and vocal-instrumental ensembles. Lyrical composed songs and folk-inflected melodies entered radio, television and concert circulation, becoming an enduring shared repertoire alongside later revivals.
items.description: Expansive melodies and memorable refrains connect this enduring Ukrainian song repertoire. Vocal-instrumental bands, orchestral accompaniments and intimate voice-and-piano settings offer different presentations of the same songs. This quieter branch supports connected singing with clear chordal piano.

items.name: Cristiana para niños
items.lineage: Spanish-language Christian children's music links church teaching, family worship and recorded entertainment. Ministries create original songs and Spanish adaptations that make biblical stories and devotional ideas accessible through participation and repetition.
items.description: Clear melodies, repeated words and easily followed refrains encourage children and adults to sing together. Simple chordal accompaniment can support group worship, while action songs and animated recordings extend the repertoire into homes and classrooms.

items.name: Plugg en Español
items.lineage: Plugg en español connects Spanish-language rappers and producers through the spacious, melodic beat tradition of plugg. Online collaborations link scenes in Argentina, Chile and other Spanish-speaking communities, adapting the style to local speech and relationships while retaining its connection to Atlanta production.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines move over sparse programmed drums, deep electronic bass and soft synthesizer melodies. Repeating motifs leave room around the voice, while sung hooks and more R&B-oriented arrangements appear in neighboring branches.

items.name: Brockton Hip Hop
items.lineage: Brockton hip hop grew through a local battle-rap community and later recording collectives such as Van Buren Records. Creative spaces including SoundLab connected the Massachusetts city’s rappers and producers with neighboring Boston scenes.
items.description: Competitive verse, tightly patterned speech and contrasting vocal deliveries link league battles with collaborative recorded rap. Unaccompanied exchanges foreground verbal rhythm; produced songs also draw on soul, R&B and electronic textures.

items.name: Louange
items.lineage: Louange connects Christian praise with Afro-francophone gospel networks linking West and Central Africa, the Caribbean and Europe. Churches, choirs and touring ministries circulate repertoire across these communities.
items.description: Collective singing, devotional texts and repeated phrases shape this praise repertoire. Unaccompanied groups combine sung lines with vocal imitations of instrumental sounds; other settings use instrumental accompaniment. French and African-language songs share a transnational church and concert network.

items.name: Dicsőítés
items.lineage: Dicsőítés is Hungarian Christian praise and worship music practiced in churches, prayer communities and ministry gatherings. Shared songbooks and worship teaching connect congregational participation with contemporary devotional songwriting.
items.description: Clear sung melodies and repeated praise texts invite participation. Guitar-led singing provides an intimate setting, while other worship groups use fuller instrumental ensembles.

items.name: Pop Dance
items.lineage: Pop dance joins vocal hooks and familiar song structures to emphatic dance rhythms and electronic production. Its international recording tradition reaches across disco-derived pop, synthesizer-led dance songs and later club-pop crossovers.
items.description: Melody and vocal hooks remain central while a strong rhythmic backing and electronic colors keep the song danceable. Bright, punctuated delivery and recurring refrains connect the pop-song foreground with club-oriented production.

items.name: Indie Catracho
items.lineage: Indie catracho brings together independent Honduran artists working across alternative rock, pop, folk and electronic music. Local collaborations, self-production and small performance circuits support an overlapping community within the country’s wider musical life.
items.description: Guitar-led songs combine clear vocal melodies with bass and drum grooves. Acoustic, electronic and experimental approaches also circulate through the scene, whose shared identity rests on local creative networks as well as sound.

items.name: Chinese Talent Show
items.lineage: Chinese talent-show music circulates through televised and streamed competitions, contestant performances and programme-linked releases. Shows such as CHUANG and The Coming One connect developing singers with production teams, music platforms and fan communities.
items.description: Vocal presentation and memorable melodies lead arrangements ranging from intimate guitar accompaniment to elaborate ensemble productions. Contrasting verses and refrains support expressive performances, covers and original songs.

items.name: Deep Progressive House
items.lineage: Deep progressive house cultivates the restrained, groove-led side of progressive dance music through specialist labels, remix networks and gradual DJ programming. Pads, rolling bass and detailed percussion build atmosphere without requiring a large festival climax.
items.description: Long transitions let bass movement, percussion and atmospheric layers develop together. Selectors connect tracks through pacing and texture, often placing these sounds in the earlier, deeper portions of extended sets.

items.name: Assamese Hip Hop
items.lineage: Assamese hip-hop connects local language, urban experience and independent production in Assam. Guwahati and other regional communities adapt rap to Assamese expression while maintaining exchanges with English, Hindi and wider Indian hip-hop.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, personal stories and locally inflected language meet producer-made backing. Flows can emphasize direct speech, punchlines and recurring hooks, while electronic beats leave room for the voice.

items.name: Azeri Rap
items.lineage: Azeri rap connects Azerbaijan’s MCs, producers and DJs through recordings, concerts and battle culture. Underground crews and mainstream platforms support a scene where lyric writing, rhythmic delivery and public performance carry distinct local identities.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and pointed lines work against supplied beats. Battle performances emphasize flow and verbal impact; unaccompanied rounds and broader recorded-song approaches extend beyond this beat-backed branch.

items.name: Canadian Drill
items.lineage: Canadian drill brings a drill-oriented rap practice into Canadian scenes and their international connections. Artists can combine local experience with Caribbean language and rhythm, extending the style through migration and exchange rather than one uniform national accent.
items.description: Rhythmic verses meet drill production, leaving room for distinctive cadence and language. Direct rap delivery can coexist with dancehall-inflected or melodic approaches; the backing supplies the rhythmic and tonal bed.

items.name: Gulf Hip Hop
items.lineage: Gulf hip-hop connects rappers, producers and audiences across the Arabian Peninsula and its diasporas. Local and migrant communities develop Arabic, English and bilingual expression through home studios, radio, online circulation and regional collaboration.
items.description: Rhythmic verses sit over producer-shaped beats and bass-led accompaniment. Sparse grooves leave room for language, flow and personal storytelling; other branches incorporate scratching, melodic hooks or regional instrumental colours.

items.name: Indonesian Trap
items.lineage: Indonesian trap develops within the country’s hip-hop networks through locally shaped flows, online production and exchanges with international rap. Performers use Indonesian and English, with playful, confrontational and personal approaches coexisting.
items.description: Staccato rap and memorable hooks move over sparse, bass-led programmed beats. Gaps, rhythmic accents and electronic melodic fragments give the voice room, while producers and performers vary the balance between direct delivery and melodic inflection.

items.name: Kyrgyz Hip Hop
items.lineage: Kyrgyz hip-hop developed through cassette exchange, urban parties, independent studios and battle-rap communities. Russian- and Kyrgyz-language artists connect Bishkek networks with audiences across the country and beyond.
items.description: Rapped verses and hooks ride supplied beats, with flexible flow and local language shaping the delivery. Battles, patriotic songs, personal narratives and club-oriented recordings form different strands of the scene.

items.name: Myanmar Hip Hop
items.lineage: Myanmar hip-hop grew through local rap collectives, home recording and informal circulation before expanding into concerts, studios and online networks. Artists adapt international influences to Burmese-language expression, local experience and changing relationships with audiences and censorship.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines meet assembled beats and bass-led backing. Direct speech, hooks and contrasting flows carry personal and social subjects; sampling, electronic production and popular-song crossover broaden the sound.

items.name: Pinoy Drill
items.lineage: Pinoy drill is a drill-oriented branch of Philippine hip-hop, connecting local MCs and producers with an international rap style. Groups such as O Side Mafia have established a visible place for it within the wider Filipino rap community.
items.description: Measured rap delivery and forceful produced backing give verses their weight. Boasts, punchlines and repeated phrases work through rhythmic space, with tracks moving between street-oriented listening and club circulation.

items.name: Sichuanese Hip Hop
items.lineage: Sichuanese hip-hop links local dialect, neighborhood identity and producer networks in Sichuan, with Chengdu’s rap collectives an important center. Artists bring regional speech rhythms into a wider Chinese and international hip-hop conversation.
items.description: Locally inflected rap flows move over producer-made beats and repeating musical figures. Trap influence, older hip-hop references and melodic crossover coexist, while the cadence and vocabulary of Sichuanese speech remain a distinctive resource.

items.name: Thai Trap
items.lineage: Thai trap developed within Thailand’s rap and beatmaking networks, where online communities connect young producers and vocalists. International trap influences intersect with Thai expression and a scene open to newer electronic and local musical ideas.
items.description: Rap leads move across producer-built backing, with hooks and electronic textures varying by artist. Collaboration between beatmakers and MCs supports both direct verse-led tracks and more melodic crossover approaches.

items.name: UA Trap
items.lineage: UA trap is Ukrainian trap: a network of rappers and beatmakers within the country’s broader hip-hop scene. Local studio collaboration and online release culture connect established trap influences with Ukrainian expression and changing language choices.
items.description: Rap phrases, repeated hooks and beat-led production carry the music. Vocal character and rhythmic space take varied forms, from sparse delivery to more melodic or plugg-influenced approaches.

items.name: Gaddiyali Pop
items.lineage: Gaddiyali pop brings Gaddi-language song into regional recording, music-video and concert networks. In Kangra and Chamba, performers connect inherited lyrics and cultural identity with contemporary popular presentation.
items.description: Sung melodies and recurring refrains meet dance-oriented backing. Folk and devotional material can enter contemporary productions, while live cultural and ritual performances retain other arrangements and functions.

items.name: Pop Romantico
items.lineage: Pop romántico foregrounds intimate relationships and emotive melodic songwriting within Spanish-language pop. Its flexible arrangements span ballads and newer acoustic or produced pop rather than requiring one historical orchestral formula.
items.description: A close melodic vocal and guitar accompaniment can expose the personal address of the lyric. Repeated harmonic patterns support memorable refrains, while changes in phrasing and dynamics give emotional contrast.

items.name: Sepedi Pop
items.lineage: Sepedi pop connects Northern Sotho-language songwriting with Limpopo popular-music networks. Manyalo performers and contemporary Afro-pop producers bring local vocal expression into amplified keyboard and beat-based arrangements.
items.description: Sung phrases and memorable refrains sit above melodic keyboard support and a rhythmic backing. Wedding-oriented Manyalo and contemporary Afro-pop offer overlapping branches with different performance settings and lyrical purposes.

items.name: Thai Viral Pop
items.lineage: Thai viral pop circulates through short-form video, fan participation and streaming discovery. Catchy Thai-language songs cross pop, R&B, soul and hip-hop networks, with successful hooks receiving new arrangements and performance versions.
items.description: A voice-and-piano rendition gives a circulating pop hook a more intimate setting. Melodic phrases remain foregrounded over chordal accompaniment, while contrasting sections make room for changes of mood and emphasis.

items.name: Kurdish Remix
items.lineage: Kurdish remix recasts Kurdish songs and neighboring regional melodies through contemporary electronic production. Online producers connect sung hooks and instrumental phrases with trap, drill, house and other beat styles, circulating their arrangements across Kurdish and Turkish-speaking listening networks.
items.description: Sung phrases and melodic keyboard figures meet a produced rhythmic backing. Flute can answer or color the vocal line, while repeated hooks and electronically arranged beats give familiar melodies a new dance-oriented setting.

items.name: Lo-Fi Latino
items.lineage: Lo-fi latino connects producers across Latin America, Spain and the diaspora through relaxed instrumental beat making. Latin melodies, rhythms and recorded fragments meet the intimate textures of lo-fi hip-hop.
items.description: Layered sample phrases bring melodic fragments, bass and percussion into repeating grooves. Soft-edged recording textures and unhurried pacing leave room for regional musical references, with sampled voices appearing alongside instrumental material.

items.name: Maïmouna
items.lineage: Maïmouna emerged in Abidjan around 2021 as a playful meeting of rap and coupé-décalé. Also called the mouvement des enfants, it links youthful rap delivery with social dancing and the city’s club and maquis culture.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and teasing hooks ride a dance-oriented produced beat. Vocal energy, rhythmic repetition and movement connect the rapper to the gathering; arrangements range from spare instrumentals to layered productions.

items.name: Musique urbaine Brazzaville
items.lineage: Contemporary urban music in the Republic of the Congo connects rap, slam and popular dance-song communities through Brazzaville, recording studios, festivals and online networks.
items.description: Rhythmic speech, melodic hooks and produced beats circulate alongside local dance rhythms and rumba-derived approaches. Artists move between rap, slam, Afro-pop and other popular forms, making this a shared regional scene rather than a single instrumental formula. A rapper over a produced beat represents one active branch.

items.name: Reading
items.lineage: Music for reading is a functional listening field cultivated by composers, publishers and playlist curators. Quiet piano, ambient textures and restrained instrumental arrangements provide a continuous backdrop to books and other sustained reading.
items.description: Connected melodic phrases and unobtrusive harmony leave space around the listener’s attention. Gentle dynamics and slowly unfolding musical continuity favor immersion over abrupt changes or foreground vocal storytelling.

items.name: Minimal Melodic Techno
items.lineage: Minimal melodic techno brings expressive melodic development into the economical patterns of European minimal electronics. The 2000s Traum and Border Community networks and the later Hungry Music collective connect restrained rhythmic frameworks with distinctive melodic voices.
items.description: Repeating rhythmic cells support evolving melodic figures, spacious textures and gradual transitions. Producers and selectors connect understated groove with cinematic, introspective or pop-shaped ideas without requiring one fixed arrangement.

items.name: Drill Dominicano
items.lineage: Dominican drill connects Dominican and diasporic rappers with the international drill vocabulary. Producer collaborations and cross-border releases adapt the style to local speech, experience and multilingual performance.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and concise hooks interact with produced drill backing. Street narratives and personal themes coexist, while individual performers draw on different Dominican and wider Latin rap connections.

items.name: Lithuanian Trap
items.lineage: Lithuanian trap developed through the country’s younger rap scene and its producers, alongside older hip-hop approaches. Local artists adapt an international style through their own collaborations, language and recording networks.
items.description: Rhythmic vocals and recurring hooks interact with produced backing. Electronic texture and beat design shape the delivery, while individual artists range from direct rap to more melodic or experimental approaches.

items.name: NZ Gangsta Rap
items.lineage: New Zealand gangsta rap places local street narratives within the wider national hip-hop scene. South Auckland artists connected international rap influences with neighbourhood experience, including accounts of gang life, its consequences and leaving it behind.
items.description: Direct rhythmic storytelling rides produced beats and low-end backing. Forceful verses can alternate with hooks and guest voices, while local references distinguish the narratives from imported settings.

items.name: Rap Criolo
items.lineage: Rap Criolo connects Cape Verdean Kriolu language with hip-hop communities in the islands and diaspora, notably metropolitan Lisbon. Its lyrics explore neighbourhood life, migration, identity and social experience.
items.description: Rhythmic Kriolu verses work with produced beats and low bass. Vocal phrasing and local language give the music its character; unaccompanied passages and melodic approaches also occur.

items.name: Türkçe Trap Metal
items.lineage: Türkçe trap metal connects Turkish-language rap with the intensity of metal-influenced vocal performance and contemporary beat production. Independent rappers and producers circulate releases and collaborations through a shared online underground, bringing screamed delivery alongside rhythmic verses.
items.description: Forceful rhythmic verses and screamed accents meet programmed drums and distorted 808 low bass. Abrasive textures and sharply delivered phrases characterize this crossover, while individual tracks vary in vocal approach and instrumental color.

items.name: Classic Bulgarian Pop
items.lineage: Bulgarian estrada developed through radio, conservatory training and state-supported popular-song festivals in the second half of the twentieth century. The Golden Orpheus and Melody of the Year circuits connected singers, composers and arrangers, leaving a repertoire that continues to be performed and revisited.
items.description: Expressive lead melodies and lyrical songcraft connect intimate guitar-accompanied songs with larger dance-band and orchestral settings. Romantic, reflective and brighter popular songs share a historical recording and festival culture, with arrangements varying widely across artists.

items.name: Vintage Swedish Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Swedish pop gathers older Swedish-language entertainment songs from revue, radio, film, dance halls and domestic music-making. Schlager melodies, comic couplets and sentimental songs moved between stage performers, records and printed arrangements, forming a repertory that later revivals continue to revisit.
items.description: Clear sung melodies and text-led phrasing sit over a compact piano accompaniment. Sentimental warmth, gentle dance motion and theatrical turns coexist in this older entertainment repertory; intimate singing at the piano is one branch alongside larger radio and ballroom ensembles.

items.name: Fotbollslåtar
items.lineage: Swedish football songs connect club supporters, national-team campaigns and popular songwriting. Commissioned tournament songs and club hymns circulate through records, broadcasts and communal singing, while familiar melodies acquire new supporter texts.
items.description: Memorable refrains, direct lyrics and shared singing give football songs their rallying character. A sung melody with chordal piano accompaniment offers one compact rendition of this repertoire, alongside crowd chants, rock bands and electronic productions.

items.name: Grave Wave
items.lineage: Grave Wave emerged around a late-2000s and early-2010s network of dark independent music, web publications, labels and clubs. Witch house, post-punk, gothic synth music, industrial electronics and neofolk circulated together through compilations, remixes and DJ programmes.
items.description: Nocturnal atmosphere and a shared underground visual culture connect disparate song and electronic styles. DJ programmes move between dark rhythmic tracks, synth textures and guitar-based material rather than relying on one tempo or production method.

items.name: Ho Munda
items.lineage: Ho community music links seasonal songs with collective dance in Singhbhum and adjoining eastern India. Courtship, harvest, weddings and Mage celebrations combine bamboo-flute melodies, communal singing and interlocking drum rhythms.
items.description: Sung phrases and flute melodies guide the dancers while a single-headed kettle drum and a double-headed drum articulate the shared pulse. Formations and song repertories change with the season and occasion; the ensemble supports communal movement rather than a fixed concert arrangement.

items.name: Jain bhajan
items.lineage: Jain bhajan, also called stavan, praises the Jinas and expresses Jain devotional ideals. Regional languages and folk-derived melodies connect temple, domestic and public singing, while modern recordings also draw on art-music and popular arrangements.
items.description: Devotional singing gives the text a clear melodic shape, with repetition and expressive phrasing supporting contemplation. A recorded art-music branch uses tabla and a sustained drone, alongside communal traditions with different accompaniment.

items.name: Lai Hla
items.lineage: Lai hla connects Chin song communities through local-language repertoire, recordings and everyday music-making. Hakha Chin lyric and chord collections bring contemporary songs, patriotic material and Christian repertoire into shared channels of learning and performance.
items.description: A clear sung melody and guitar chords support an intimate, portable song setting. Repeated sections make lyrics easy to learn and share, while the wider repertoire also circulates through gospel groups, popular recordings and electronic arrangements.

items.name: Marathi Balgeet
items.lineage: Marathi balgeet brings Marathi-language children’s songs into family play, classrooms and contemporary educational media. Short rhymes, memorable phrases and coordinated actions help children share language and rhythm.
items.description: Voices repeat compact phrases while hand patterns mark the pulse. Clapping games can alternate song with playful spoken sounds and gestures; arranged recordings offer additional ways of circulating the repertoire.

items.name: Muzică Maramureșeană
items.lineage: Maramureș music brings together village singing, wedding repertories, dance tunes and pastoral music from northern Romania. The cetera fiddle and strummed zongoră form a characteristic instrumental partnership, often joined by a dobă drum. Solo long-song traditions coexist with lively collective performances.
items.description: A decorated fiddle melody moves over insistent strummed chords and a drum pulse. Wedding musicians vary and elaborate the tunes, with shouted strigături adding vocal energy. Other parts of the regional repertoire favor free, sustained solo singing and quieter pastoral sounds.

items.name: Necrotrap
items.lineage: Necrotrap is an online underground rap field connecting dark trap production, abrasive low bass and screamed delivery. Its producers and performers circulate through small internet networks alongside dark trap and trap metal. Distortion and clipped 808 sounds are prominent options rather than a requirement for every release.
items.description: Harsh rhythmic vocals confront forceful produced beats and low bass. Clipping, sparse threatening textures and abrupt vocal accents can intensify the delivery; calmer and more melodic productions also circulate within the field.

items.name: Rave
items.lineage: Rave developed around collective electronic dance events and DJ culture, connecting acid house, techno, breakbeats and subsequent hard-dance scenes. Its late-1980s and 1990s British history sits within wider international club and sound-system exchanges, with later generations continually revisiting and reshaping the repertoire.
items.description: Selectors sustain dance-floor momentum through mixing, overlapping records and manipulating loops or short fragments. Repetition, low-frequency energy and contrasting electronic textures connect otherwise different styles; the surrounding gathering is central to the music’s identity.

items.name: Deep Dubstep
items.lineage: Bass-centered dubstep associated with soundsystem listening, restrained percussion and dark atmospheric space, continuing through international producer labels and DJ circulation.
items.description: Deep dubstep favors low-frequency weight, space around percussion and atmospheric textures. Its producers and DJs connect the early soundsystem tradition with ongoing bass-music releases and mixes. The label overlaps minimal and classic dubstep, and DJ programmes may move between its half-time feel and faster breakbeat material.

items.name: Malayalam Hip Hop
items.lineage: Malayalam hip-hop developed through independent Kerala-based crews, online circulation and experimentation with the rhythms of the Malayalam language. Street Academics links early spoken-word and cassette-loop practices with later influences from jazz, soul, ambient music, glitch and grime.
items.description: Malayalam rap moves between independent crews, film collaborations and online releases. Rhythmic spoken delivery carries regional-language wordplay over repeated beats; early cassette-loop experiments coexist with later soul, jazz, ambient, glitch and grime production.

items.name: Chhattisgarhi pop
items.lineage: Chhattisgarhi pop links regional-language songwriting and modern folk with a local album, film and concert industry. Singers such as Nitin Dubey developed audiences through recordings and stage performances before artist channels and music videos widened circulation. Folk melody, playback singing and studio production remain connected within this regional field.
items.description: Melodic leads and duets carry regional-language lyrics over rhythmic studio arrangements. Electronic rhythm, programmed sounds and effects support contemporary songs, while other arrangements incorporate folk instruments and film-music textures. Repeated hooks and direct vocal phrasing connect recorded songs with stage audiences.

items.name: Dakke Dak
items.lineage: Dakke dak names an exuberant Danish party-music field spanning electronic dance tracks and rap. Club and festival performance, humorous verses and forceful rhythmic hooks connect its performers and listeners.
items.description: Rhythmic Danish punchlines ride a strong electronic backing pulse in the rap-led branch. Direct delivery and repeated rhythmic phrases create an energetic dance-floor address, with singing and other dance formats elsewhere in the broader repertoire.

items.name: Healing Hz
items.lineage: Healing Hz is a frequency-labelled listening field circulated through meditation catalogues and sound-generation apps. Sustained tones, frequency pairs and soft electronic layers organize listening around named frequency settings and relaxation-oriented presentation.
items.description: Long, steady electronic tones provide a minimal branch of this listening practice. Other productions layer tones, pulses or quiet noise; the frequency-labelled presentation and wellness-oriented circulation connect these differing textures.

items.name: Hopebeat
items.lineage: Hopebeat names an optimistic strand of contemporary independent pop, joining bright electronic production with alternative-rock band textures. Nostalgic melodies and approachable hooks connect home-created recordings with an energetic live circuit.
items.description: Clear sung hooks, ringing guitar chords, melodic keyboards and a steady drum pulse create a buoyant band texture. Electronic-pop polish and rock energy coexist, with lyrics and familiar melodic shapes inviting audience participation.

items.name: Modern Downshift
items.lineage: Modern Downshift is a discovery field around independent heavy and melodic rock. Amplified riffs, forceful rhythm sections and memorable sung hooks connect bands working across hard rock, alternative metal and post-grunge.
items.description: Melodic voices rise over electric-guitar hooks, bass and a firm drum backbeat. Rhythmic weight and accessible refrains meet in arrangements that move between tightly locked riffs and more open vocal passages.

items.name: Movie Tunes
items.lineage: Movie tunes circulate film melodies and songs beyond the screen through recordings, sheet music and everyday performance. Musical-film repertoire, animated-film songs and familiar cinema themes meet in this listening and performing tradition.
items.description: Recognizable melodies and song phrases remain central as arrangements move between singers, orchestras, bands and keyboards. A solo-piano branch places the melody above chordal accompaniment, retaining the tunes in an accessible instrumental setting.

items.name: Nova Música Amazonense
items.lineage: Nova música amazonense brings contemporary songwriting from Amazonas into local stages, independent releases and wider Brazilian festival circuits. Rock, MPB, R&B, rap and regional influences coexist within a scene centered on Manaus and connected to other northern cities.
items.description: Original songs combine expressive voices with acoustic accompaniment, amplified bands or electronic production. The intimate voice-and-guitar branch leaves room for clear melodic phrases and chordal movement while the wider scene embraces heavier, dance-oriented and experimental sounds.

items.name: Oeteldonk
items.lineage: Oeteldonk music belongs to the carnival culture of ’s-Hertogenbosch, sustained by local clubs, song competitions and community celebrations. New carnival songs join familiar refrains in the Kwèkfestijn and a shared repertoire associated with the city’s festive identity.
items.description: Projecting voices, memorable refrains and lively wind-band responses invite collective participation. Trumpets, trombones, saxophones and low brass combine with rhythmic percussion, while humorous texts and theatrical presentation animate the songs.

items.name: Swazi Traditional
items.lineage: Swazi traditional music sustains communal song, dance and ceremonial life in Eswatini. Royal-village repertoires, regimental songs and women’s seasonal celebrations connect musical participation with social memory, public honor and the agricultural calendar.
items.description: Shared melodies and coordinated vocal entries accompany public dancing and collective celebration. Songs can affirm community ties, honor royalty and mark seasonal ceremonies; male, female and mixed groups maintain different repertories within the wider tradition.
exemplars: Women and men of the Queen Mother’s Village

items.name: Deep Psytrance
items.lineage: Deep psytrance emphasizes immersive, groove-led psychedelic trance rather than a single label roster. It overlaps dark progressive and Zenonesque practice, combining repetitive dance rhythms with spacious textures, detailed sound design and gradual developments across long DJ journeys.
items.description: Hypnotic bass movement, repeating percussion and subtly changing electronic textures give deep psytrance its immersive flow. Darker progressive passages can meet techno-like restraint and psychedelic sound design; mixing and live rhythmic layers build extended journeys without requiring constant peak-time intensity.

items.name: Chill Breakcore
items.lineage: An online breakcore label used by contemporary producers for atmospheric, melodic and liquid-influenced work, heard in both listening mixes and club DJ practice.
items.description: Chill breakcore links atmospheric drum-and-bass and liquid textures with the fragmented rhythms of online breakcore. It circulates through producer releases, listening mixes and DJ sets, with substantial overlap with jungle, liquid DnB and the wider breakcore field.

items.name: Detroit trap en español
items.lineage: Detroit trap en español connects Spanish-language rappers and producers with contemporary Detroit-derived rap. Artists such as Gloosito and JayDime participate in a wider Spanish-language scene that adapts this vocabulary through collaborations, releases and live performance.
items.description: Conversational rapping and emphatic rhythmic phrasing ride over programmed percussion and a pitched low kick. Chopped or repeating samples supply melodic and harmonic hooks, leaving space for flexible vocal placement, humorous lines and sharp changes of emphasis.

items.name: Pop Reggaeton
items.lineage: Pop reggaeton brings melodic urban-pop hooks into the rhythmic production of reggaeton. Its Spanish-language crossover field connects performers across Latin America, including a strong Venezuelan singer-songwriter network.
items.description: Sung hooks and romantic lyric address sit over a recurring reggaeton beat. Melodic phrasing and a clear rhythmic pulse support the crossover between dance music and pop song.

items.name: Calming Instrumental
items.lineage: Calming instrumental listening brings gentle instrumental compositions into relaxation, focus and quiet domestic settings. Contemporary piano composers draw on older nocturne forms while using compact melodies and restrained textures suited to these listening contexts.
items.description: Gentle piano melodies unfold through connected phrases and lightly weighted accompaniment. Motion may be flowing or relatively quick while the touch remains soft; a calm listening purpose does not require every piece to share one tempo. Solo acoustic piano is one branch of a wider instrumental field.

items.name: Carnaval Limburg
items.lineage: Limburg carnival music grows through local associations, dialect songwriting and seasonal celebrations. Shared refrains connect communities across the province while preserving differences between local traditions.
items.description: Festive singing meets accessible melodies, dance rhythms and ensemble accompaniment. Accordion, brass, keyboards and rhythm sections can support massed refrains, while intimate song settings also preserve the repertoire.

items.name: Chill Lounge
items.lineage: Contemporary chill-lounge listening draws on downtempo electronica, Balearic curation and smooth lounge grooves. Producers, radio programmes and hospitality channels connect spacious electronic textures with relaxed melodic and vocal material.
items.description: Unhurried electronic grooves, soft-edged melodies and spacious production suit relaxed listening. DJ programmes connect instrumental and vocal selections through flowing transitions, with acoustic colors and electronic textures sharing the sound.

items.name: Ghanaian Alternative
items.lineage: Ghanaian alternative music grows through independent musicians, producers and creative communities, especially in Accra. DIY collaboration, festivals and platforms such as ACCRA [dot] ALT and Oroko Radio connect local experimentation with international audiences.
items.description: The field includes experimental beatmaking, electronic dance music, soulful singing and independent rap. Producers reshape sampled phrases and rhythmic fragments into new instrumental textures, while vocal projects explore personal expression and social commentary. Its identity lies in creative communities and varied approaches beyond the dominant radio styles.

items.name: Ghoststep
items.lineage: Ghoststep is an electronic discovery tag connecting club productions and bass music. Its repertoire includes dubstep, house and techno contributors, with DJ selection and microphone-led performance among the documented practices.
items.description: Recorded bass, percussion and electronic textures form a flexible club-music palette. A representative DJ-and-MC branch combines continuous selection with rhythmic spoken delivery; the discovery field overlaps several established electronic styles.

items.name: J-Division
items.lineage: J-Division is a Japanese pop discovery field linking character-song projects, vocal units and real-world pop groups. Its repertoire crosses animated and game franchises, rap battles and dance-pop, with published arrangements extending the songs into instrumental performance.
items.description: Distinctive melodies and rhythmic hooks support solo and ensemble vocal identities. Character performances, rap verses and dance-oriented production coexist with pop songwriting; piano arrangements offer one documented instrumental branch of this wider repertoire.

items.name: Japanese New Wave
items.lineage: Japanese new wave grew through late-1970s and early-1980s art-school, live-house and independent recording networks. Groups including Plastics, Hikashu and P-Model connected angular rock songs with electronic keyboards, rhythm machines and visual experimentation; later revivals continued both band and electronic approaches.
items.description: Angular guitar figures, direct vocals and contrasting keyboard textures carry concise, rhythm-conscious songs. Drum-band arrangements sit alongside machine-driven technopop, experimental electronics and theatrical performance; the repertoire crosses rock and electronic-pop scenes.

items.name: Mezmur
items.lineage: Mezmur connects Ethiopian Christian song with church choirs, solo singers and devotional recordings. Shared hymns and newly composed songs circulate through congregations, recordings and community networks.
items.description: Group singing gives devotional words a shared melodic and rhythmic shape. Unaccompanied choral settings form one branch alongside keyboard, guitar and fuller instrumental arrangements; soloists and choirs carry both inherited hymns and new songs.

items.name: Pygmy music (Central African archival field)
items.lineage: Central African forest music documented in the Ituri recordings of Colin Turnbull and Francis Chapman during the 1950s. The historical archival label encompasses several communities and musical practices: initiation and forest-devotion singing, hunting and gathering songs, social dances, and instrumental music. Mbuti and Efe repertoires sit within this wider field alongside related regional traditions.
items.description: Interlocking vocal entries, circulating short phrases and overlapping group parts are characteristic of the polyphonic singing branch. Other practices feature cane flutes, lamellophones, musical bows, zithers, drums and slit-gong signalling. Sacred, occupational and recreational settings support different ensembles and textures; the Alima singing tradition provides a representative canonic vocal setting.
exemplars: Mbuti singers — Bambuti – Alima Song, complete FW03855_209

items.name: Rominimal
items.lineage: Rominimal names a Romanian minimal electronic-music community associated with extended DJ sets, small labels and club gatherings. Rhadoo, Raresh and Petre Inspirescu helped shape its international circulation, while newer practitioners connect the sound with microhouse, deep tech and psychedelic influences.
items.description: Sparse rhythmic details, repeating bass movement and slowly evolving textures sustain long dance-floor passages. Track selection and gradual blends shape a patient groove, with room for house, techno and more psychedelic colours.

items.name: Russian Hyperpop
items.lineage: Russian hyperpop developed through online youth music communities around the turn of the 2020s, combining pop songwriting with exaggerated electronic production and the circulation of short-form video. Sqwore, 17Seventeen, rizza, treepside and Midix form part of its varied scene.
items.description: Strongly altered voices, synthetic bass, fragmented samples and abrupt shifts in texture give familiar pop gestures an unstable digital character. Singing and rap mingle with pitched vocal effects, glitches and dense electronic beats.
exemplars: Note-Store — Sqwore Пластиковые воспоминания, complete Piano.Easy PEA0334385

items.name: Stomp and Whittle
items.lineage: Stomp and whittle groups intimate and inventive indie songwriting, from small acoustic performances to elaborately arranged folk-pop. Personal lyrics, lightly voiced melodies and distinctive instrumental colors connect artists across this listening community.
items.description: Melodic singing and rhythmic plucked accompaniment support personal, playful and reflective songs. Small acoustic settings sit beside fuller indie-pop arrangements, with attention to lyrics and individual instrumental color.

items.name: Viet Lo-fi
items.lineage: Vietnamese lo-fi developed through online producers and channels including Freak D Music, Orinn and1967. Reworked Vietnamese pop songs circulate alongside instrumental listening music, connecting a local song repertoire with the broader international lo-fi aesthetic.
items.description: Slowed pacing, softened high frequencies and deliberate recording imperfections give familiar songs a hazy, intimate character. Producers manipulate recorded audio and add textural noise or effects; sung melodies and existing instrumental arrangements remain audible within these transformations.

items.name: Voetbal
items.lineage: Voetbal music connects Dutch football supporters with club songs, national-team anthems and familiar popular melodies. Stadium singing, supporter recordings and commercial releases circulate across club communities, adapting words and refrains to express allegiance and shared celebration.
items.description: Club marches, national-team songs and adapted popular choruses give supporters shared words and melodies. Projected rhythmic singing and clear chordal accompaniment support a song-led branch alongside unaccompanied crowd chants and amplified party versions.

items.name: Chill Phonk
items.lineage: Chill phonk names a mellower strand of internet phonk, linking lo-fi and trap-derived beats with sampled melodic material. Contemporary producers and sample libraries use the name across both relaxed, jazzy textures and darker, more forceful arrangements, within the wider circulation of phonk online.
items.description: Repeating sampled phrases, rounded programmed low end and a flexible rhythmic pocket support short vocal fragments. Jazz-colored loops and softened textures can coexist with dark effects and stronger drums; the name describes an adaptable listening mood rather than a fixed tempo or an exclusively instrumental format.

items.name: Deep Progressive Rock
items.lineage: Deep progressive rock is a practitioner-used designation within progressive and art rock. Atmospheric arrangements and shifting dynamics connect melodic songwriting with intricate rhythm, extended instrumental colours and contrasts between delicacy and weight.
items.description: Clear singing and reverberant guitar arpeggios move across a dynamic bass-and-drum foundation. Electric piano, tonewheel organ and tape-replay keyboard colours fill the harmonic space, while changing textures and interlocking rhythms give the music an expansive, sometimes melancholy character.

items.name: Classic Turkish Pop
items.lineage: Classic Turkish pop revisits familiar popular songs through nostalgic concerts, reissues and new arrangements. Its repertoire crosses the aranjman era, Anatolian melodic influences and later Turkish songwriting, keeping older songs active in contemporary listening and performance.
items.description: Expressive melodies and clearly shaped song sections carry a repertoire that moves between reflective ballads and brighter rhythmic pop. Piano adaptations foreground the melodic line and supporting harmony, while band and orchestral renditions provide other colours within the same broad historical field.

items.name: Vintage Spanish Pop
items.lineage: Older Spanish popular-song culture connects stage entertainment, printed songs and commercial recordings. Cuplé, sentimental song and imported dance-song forms circulated through singers and publishers, while later revivals revisit that repertory in intimate and larger ensemble settings.
items.description: Text-led singing carries romantic and theatrical expression over a clear chordal accompaniment. Voice and piano provide one compact setting; historical recordings also employ dance bands and orchestras, with varied rhythms and dramatic character.

items.name: Christmas Product
items.lineage: Christmas Product is a seasonal recording field gathering familiar holiday songs, carols and purpose-made festive listening. Commercial catalogues circulate vocal and instrumental versions across styles, from family singalongs to piano arrangements.
items.description: Recognizable seasonal melodies receive clear harmonic accompaniment and approachable phrasing. Piano versions form one branch of a varied catalogue that also includes singers, ensembles and dance-oriented holiday records.

items.name: Electrofox
items.lineage: Electrofox gathers an indie-electronic listening community around songcraft, club-oriented production and new-wave affinities. Its artists connect independent bands, remix culture and electronic pop across French and international networks.
items.description: Sung hooks and layered voices meet guitar figures and electronically constructed rhythms and textures. A clear studio sound can retain the character of an indie song while inviting dance-floor remixes.

items.name: Indie Triste
items.lineage: Indie triste gathers Spanish-language independent songs of longing, loss and intimate reflection. Home-grown singer-songwriter practices and online circulation connect acoustic folk-rooted performers with a wider range of restrained pop and alternative productions.
items.description: A close singing voice and spare guitar figures can carry vulnerable words and recurring melodic ideas. Unhurried phrasing, space between attacks and a restrained texture give the acoustic branch its inward quality.

items.name: Lo-Fi Chill
items.lineage: Lo-fi chill connects intimate internet songwriting with mellow hip-hop and pop production. Singers and producers exchange emotionally direct songs through online collaborations, with acoustic writing, soft beats and sampled voices forming overlapping strands.
items.description: Quietly delivered melodies and personal lyrics sit over simple guitar figures or softly layered beats. The acoustic songwriting branch keeps words and recurring melodic phrases close, while fuller productions add sampled material, electronic rhythms and collaborators.

items.name: Lo-Fi Product
items.lineage: Lo-fi product is a discovery grouping around commercially circulated lo-fi listening catalogues, producer aliases and playlist brands. Independent beat makers and collaborative labels supply relaxed tracks for everyday listening, with original pieces, reinterpretations and purpose-led releases sharing the field.
items.description: Produced beats and repeating textures support unobtrusive listening. Some catalogues emphasize mellow instrumental remakes, while others connect lo-fi hip-hop with sleep, study and other daily activities; no single production device or instrument lineup defines the whole grouping.

items.name: Lo-Fi Sleep
items.lineage: Lo-fi sleep gathers gentle beat producers and listening communities around rest and quiet background listening. Short, restrained productions extend the relaxed side of lo-fi culture, with soft rhythmic repetition and uncluttered texture rather than a single compulsory instrument lineup.
items.description: Calm produced beats provide an understated pulse and space for repeated textures. Low intensity and a close listening scale support a restful atmosphere; melodic sources and production methods vary between makers.

items.name: Modern Bhajan
items.lineage: Modern bhajan brings Hindu devotional song into contemporary independent releases, music videos and streaming communities. Traditional praise texts and recurring invocations meet acoustic songwriting, amplified arrangements, electronic production and devotional rap.
items.description: Devotional singing carries repeated names, refrains and melodic ornament through intimate acoustic settings and contemporary produced tracks. Guitar figures and flute responses support one gentle song-led branch, while the wider listening community also includes beats, rock textures and rap.

items.name: Modern Darkwave
items.lineage: A contemporary continuation and revival of darkwave, connecting post-punk songwriting with electronic dance pulses and gothic atmosphere. International club, festival and independent-label networks carry newer groups alongside the older darkwave repertoire.
items.description: Melancholic melodic vocals, articulated low-string lines and contrasting synthesizer textures sit above programmed dance pulses. Song-led band arrangements coexist with sparse electronic productions, noisier textures and club remixes.

items.name: Modern Goth
items.lineage: Contemporary goth develops the post-punk and gothic-rock repertoire through active bands, independent releases, club audiences and international touring. Younger groups draw on earlier atmospheric rock and synth-pop while bringing new songwriting, social perspectives and production approaches.
items.description: Melodic vocals, prominent bass and rhythmic guitars combine with drums and electronic colour. Danceable momentum can sit beside melancholy, theatrical or politically engaged lyrics; guitar-led bands and more electronic arrangements share the contemporary goth circuit.

items.name: Nova Música Maranhense
items.lineage: Nova música maranhense connects contemporary songwriters, bands and producers from Maranhão through festivals, recordings and local performance networks. Their work draws on regional song and dance traditions while engaging with wider Brazilian popular music.
items.description: An acoustic song branch places expressive melodic singing over a repeating guitar accompaniment. Other artists expand the regional repertoire through bands, electronic production and collaborations, bringing local imagery and rhythms into varied contemporary settings.

items.name: Pixel
items.lineage: Online fan-song creators build original songs, parodies and arrangements around games, internet characters and shared fictional worlds. The Pixel discovery field connects catchy pop writing, playful storytelling and digitally circulated reinterpretations across these communities.
items.description: Memorable melodic hooks and clear chordal support carry songs associated with games and online fandom. Piano arrangements bring those melodies into an acoustic setting, alongside the field’s sung and electronically produced versions.

items.name: Previa
items.lineage: Previa connects pre-party listening with a circulating repertoire of Latin dance edits, remixes and DJ sets. Familiar pop and urban hooks are recombined with cumbia, reggaeton and other club rhythms, moving between home gatherings, online releases and dancing.
items.description: Short recognisable hooks, rhythmic transitions and contrasting remixes keep the programme moving. DJs may connect cumbia, RKT, reggaeton and pop versions within one set, while recorded vocals and changing backing textures remain part of the mixed selections.

items.name: Psychokore
items.lineage: Psychokore is a German horror-rap branch associated with Blokkmonsta, Hirntot and related underground artists. Its deliberately theatrical narratives connect horrorcore with a stripped electronic sound drawing on Dirty South and EBM.
items.description: Minimal electronic percussion and low synthesizer figures leave space for forceful narrative rap. Beats range from fast propulsion to slow menace, while fictional characters and exaggerated violence shape the storytelling. Collaborations connect the scene with wider German underground rap.

items.name: Relaxative
items.lineage: Relaxative groups gentle listening repertoire across contemporary piano, instrumental covers, lounge and atmospheric electronic music. Streaming discovery brings these different traditions together around relaxed listening rather than a single historical ensemble or technique.
items.description: Clear melodic lines, softened dynamics and unhurried textures provide a calm listening character. Acoustic piano and guitar sit alongside jazz-derived arrangements and electronic mixes; this profile represents the composed solo-piano branch.

items.name: Romántico
items.lineage: Romántico gathers instrumental interpretations of romantic songs and familiar melodies, especially Latin American boleros and popular standards. Piano, guitar, harp, saxophone and light-orchestra recordings share this listening field, carrying recognizable song melodies across different instrumental colours.
items.description: Familiar melodies sing through measured piano phrases and warm chordal support. Boleros, sentimental songs and international standards appear in intimate instrumental versions alongside fuller ensemble arrangements.
exemplars: John Pazos and His Bolero Orchestra

items.name: Viet Remix
items.lineage: Viet remix circulates Vietnamese songs in remixed dance versions, nonstop DJ programmes and online listening communities. Pop ballads and older sentimental repertoire can acquire energetic electronic arrangements, while Vinahouse club practice forms a prominent overlapping branch.
items.description: Recognizable Vietnamese melodies and recorded vocals ride driving electronic rhythms and repeating dance hooks. Continuous mixes connect remade songs through transitions, while individual remixes range from club-oriented arrangements to faster social-media edits.

items.name: Hard Minimal Techno
items.lineage: Hard minimal techno connects minimal club producers around economical percussion, prominent bass figures and cut-up vocal material. DJ programmes develop these elements through repeated grooves and transitions between records.
items.description: Clicking percussion and compact bass grooves give the music a direct club pulse. Brief vocal cuts and small changes in texture punctuate extended mixed passages.

items.name: Focus Trance
items.lineage: Focus trance is a discovery label connecting melodic progressive producers and DJs. Its repertoire links trance-inflected melodies with progressive-house sequencing and gradually evolving electronic textures.
items.description: Layered melodic selections unfold over steady dance rhythms, with long transitions and changing atmospheric textures. A continuous DJ programme can include both vocal and instrumental passages.

items.name: Glitter Trance
items.lineage: Glitter trance is a discovery label linking melodic electronic producers and DJs across progressive house, trance and chill-out. Its mixed programmes connect flowing melodies and vocal passages with sustained electronic dance grooves.
items.description: Melodic selections move through quiet introductions, steady dance passages and gently evolving transitions. Vocal and instrumental textures alternate over a continuous mixed programme.

items.name: Pop Cristiano
items.lineage: Pop cristiano connects Spanish-language popular songwriting with Christian faith and testimony. Artists and bands circulate melodic songs through churches, independent labels, radio and digital platforms, joining devotional themes to contemporary pop and regional musical influences.
items.description: Memorable sung melodies and recurring refrains carry reflection, hope and personal devotion. Acappella editions foreground the vocal lines, while acoustic bands and electronic production give other songs fuller rhythmic and harmonic support.

items.name: Pop EDM
items.lineage: Pop EDM connects melody-led popular songwriting with electronic dance production. Radio hooks, remixes and club versions circulate between streaming releases, DJ sets and festival stages, bringing recognizable songs into dance-floor arrangements.
items.description: Songful melodies and recurring hooks sit over electronic dance pulses, with transitions and extended arrangements shaping the DJ branch. Performers balance approachable pop phrasing with club momentum; different tracks and live arrangements retain a wide range of vocal and instrumental colours.

items.name: Thai Folk Pop
items.lineage: Thai folk pop brings intimate songwriting and acoustic textures into popular-song settings. Singer-songwriters, small bands and mixed listening programmes connect local lyrics and folk influences with contemporary melodic pop, alongside the wider Thai indie and rural-song fields.
items.description: Clear vocal melodies and recurring song sections often sit against strummed accompaniment and modest band textures. DJ listening programmes also carry this repertoire, connecting whole songs while preserving their recorded vocal and instrumental layers.

items.name: Vintage Cantonese Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Cantonese pop brings older Cantonese popular songs into present-day listening and performance. Film and stage repertories, dance-song arrangements and later television themes connect Hong Kong with audiences across southern China and Southeast Asia, while revivals keep familiar melodies in circulation.
items.description: Memorable melodies and expressive song phrasing link early screen songs with later popular standards. Western dance rhythms and regional melodic traditions meet in varied arrangements; instrumental adaptations carry the tunes into intimate plucked-string performance.

items.name: Vintage Italian Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Italian pop connects older canzone, radio entertainment and popular dance-song repertories with later revivals. Singers and instrumentalists brought regional melodies, swing and other international dance rhythms into records, variety shows and television, leaving a repertoire still performed in new arrangements.
items.description: Tuneful phrasing and memorable refrains range from lyrical songs to witty, rhythmically animated numbers. Swing-inflected harmony and dance accents are prominent in one branch, with piano adaptations retaining the melody while reworking the accompaniment.

items.name: Abstract IDM
items.lineage: Abstract IDM develops the experimental side of electronic listening music through unstable rhythms, resampling and evolving textures. Independent producers and labels connect detailed digital editing with ambience and melodic fragments, treating irregularity and transformation as compositional material.
items.description: Fractured beats and bass patterns interact with granular textures, drifting pads and uncertain melodic phrases. Repetition gives way to small mutations, irregular attacks and changing layers, with studio processing shaping both the rhythm and the surrounding space.

items.name: Deep Chill-Out
items.lineage: Deep chill-out is a listening-oriented discovery field within ambient and downtempo culture. Its producers and selectors connect spacious electronic production with choral, acoustic and cinematic material in reflective programmes.
items.description: Slow-moving textures and gently joined selections create a spacious listening flow. A curated DJ programme can pass between choral voices, piano, classical music and electronica without reducing them to one fixed studio ensemble.

items.name: Game Mood
items.lineage: Game Mood gathers music circulated through online role-playing communities, especially the NoPixel scene. Performers and producers create songs for fictional identities and venues while releasing them to real listeners beyond the game.
items.description: A rap-led branch places rhythmic verses over produced beats. Recorded songs circulate through streamed in-game performances, while the broader community also includes sung pop and other electronic styles.

items.name: Música Prehispánica
items.lineage: Música prehispánica is a discovery field around the sound heritage of pre-colonial Mesoamerica and its modern reinterpretation. Archaeological instruments, replicas, Indigenous musical continuities and newly composed or improvised works inform a varied repertoire; surviving objects do not establish the original melodies or a single universal tuning system.
items.description: An experimental flute branch explores simultaneous pitches, breath-shaped attacks and changing fingerings on a three-tube ceramic aerophone. Other interpretations combine whistles, shells, percussion, voices or electronic sound, connecting historical inquiry with contemporary performance.

items.name: No Beat
items.lineage: No Beat is a Brazilian producer-and-MC discovery label spanning digitally circulated funk, arrochadeira remixes and trap-funk collaborations. Producer signatures and recurring vocal partnerships connect the releases; the name does not signify music without a beat.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines ride producer-built beats, with short hooks and dance-driven repetitions. This profile represents a rap-and-funk production branch within a wider catalogue of remixes and regional dance styles.

items.name: Salsa International
items.lineage: Salsa International is a discovery label connecting singers, orchestras and dance repertoires across the international salsa circuit. Classic son-derived arrangements, harder orchestral grooves and romantic songs circulate together through recordings, touring bands and social dancing.
items.description: Interlocking piano and percussion support sung lines, answering voices and instrumental phrases. Larger horn bands are prominent, while intimate café ensembles preserve the dance pulse with a smaller acoustic palette; the default represents a flute, piano and hand-percussion branch.

items.name: Scottish Hush
items.lineage: Scottish Hush is a discovery label connecting Scottish independent songwriters and bands, from intimate acoustic performances to fuller arrangements. Personal storytelling and collaborations link its folk, pop and independent-rock strands.
items.description: An acoustic branch sets a single singing voice against intricate nylon-string guitar. Percussive fingerwork and flowing melodic figures support reflective words, while the wider field also includes amplified bands and collaborative ensembles.

items.name: Śląskie Piosenki
items.lineage: Śląskie piosenki connects popular songs circulating through Silesian performers, regional entertainment and domestic music-making. Romantic schlager, family songs and dance-oriented refrains appear alongside adaptations and local-language repertoire.
items.description: Recognizable song melodies and clear chord progressions make the repertoire accessible for singing and instrumental play. A domestic piano rendition carries the tune above chordal support, alongside the vocal duos, bands and electronic arrangements heard across the wider field.

items.name: Tallava
items.lineage: Tallava developed among Roma and Ashkali communities in Kosovo and neighboring Balkan regions, spreading through weddings, celebrations and diaspora networks. Extended improvisation and responsive singing link older voice-and-frame-drum practices with electronic keyboard ensembles.
items.description: A singer stretches words into melismatic phrases over sustained keyboard support and a recurring dance pulse. Clarinet motifs and keyboard leads answer and elaborate the line, while the performance expands around guests, dedications and dancers rather than a fixed short-song form.

items.name: Vintage Radio Show
items.lineage: Vintage Radio Show gathers archival broadcast entertainment, including serial drama, comedy, literary readings and spoken storytelling. Network transmission, syndication and later record reissues carried these programmes beyond their original local audiences.
items.description: In the solo storytelling branch, a narrator shapes pacing, diction and character through speech, leaving the story unobscured by accompaniment. The broader archive also contains ensemble acting, comic dialogue, musical interludes and sound effects.

items.name: Deep Soul House
items.lineage: Deep soul house gathers a contemporary house discovery community drawing on deep-house, soul and disco traditions. Producers and DJs connect harmonic warmth and repeated rhythmic patterns with underground dance-floor circulation.
items.description: Continuous house selections develop through track transitions and changing rhythmic or harmonic textures. The DJ branch retains the recorded layers inside its mixed programme.

items.name: Deep Tropical House
items.lineage: Deep tropical house connects melodic, vocal-centered house with the softer textures of the 2010s tropical-house crossover. Producers and DJs link radio-friendly songs with club and festival sets.
items.description: Light rhythmic motion, clear melodic hooks and vocal warmth connect deep-house pacing with tropical-pop arrangements. Plucked synth colors, sampled or recorded instrumental layers and accessible song structures appear across the repertoire. DJ sets may lift the energy beyond the gentler radio versions.

items.name: Deep German Hip Hop
items.lineage: Deep German hip hop gathers German-language underground and independent rap artists whose careers connect recorded releases, online video battles and live competitive circuits. Performers such as Cashisclay, Twizzy and Punch Arogunz move between these overlapping spaces. Written a cappella events provide one performance branch alongside their wider recorded repertoire.
items.description: Prepared rhymes, rhythmic speech and emphatic phrasing foreground verbal delivery. In the unaccompanied battle branch, two MCs take alternating turns, allowing cadence, pauses and changes of emphasis to shape the performance without an instrumental backing.

items.name: Drill brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian drill localizes Chicago and British drill influences within Brazil’s rap scenes, developing through performers such as Vandal, LEALL, VND and L7nnon. MCs and producers connect its heavy beats with Portuguese flows, local street narratives, football culture and exchanges with Brazilian funk.
items.description: Sliding electronic bass, distinctive hi-hat and snare placements, and forceful rhythmic verses form a recognizable production vocabulary. Brazilian artists adapt these patterns to local language and experience, with collaboration and overlap across grime, trap and funk communities.

items.name: Norwegian pop rap
items.lineage: Norwegian pop rap connects rhythmic verses with melodic hooks and popular-song production. Artists such as Karpe, Madcon and Paperboys helped bring Norwegian rap into radio and mainstream pop, while multilingual and diasporic influences widened its lyrical and melodic vocabulary.
items.description: Rap verses and sung refrains share space over programmed drums, sampled phrases and polished melodic backing. Songs move between personal stories, social observation and broadly accessible hooks. The field overlaps national hip-hop and contemporary Norwegian pop, with artists working across both audiences.

items.name: Outer Hip Hop
items.lineage: Outer hip hop gathers independent rap and producer networks including Canadian prairie musicians and their collaborators. Personal narratives, social observation and inventive wordplay meet producer-built beats through self-released recordings and small-label circulation.
items.description: Rhythmic lead verses sit over a produced beat in a compact studio arrangement. Verbal phrasing and changes of accent remain foregrounded, while the backing texture can vary between productions.

items.name: Deep Happy Hardcore
items.lineage: Deep happy hardcore gathers a contemporary hardcore producer and DJ cohort around fast dance beats, buoyant melodic hooks and energetic vocal refrains. Label mixes and club performances connect established UK hardcore practices with internationally circulating releases.
items.description: An energetic DJ presentation joins melodic hardcore selections through continuous playback and transitions. The whole mixed programme retains its embedded voices and instrumental layers rather than treating them as a new live ensemble.

items.name: Deep Hardcore
items.lineage: Deep hardcore gathers an electronic hardcore discovery cohort with early rave, gabber and experimental club connections. Distorted rhythms, sampled phrases and changes of electronic texture circulate through records and DJ programmes; the field is distinct from hardcore punk instrumentation.
items.description: A continuous DJ programme connects older hardcore selections with contrasting rhythmic weight and atmosphere. This listening-oriented branch keeps the complete mixed repertoire and its embedded sound layers.

items.name: Rebel Blues
items.lineage: Rebel blues is a discovery field connecting forceful rock songs, blues-inflected voices and cinematic pop. Its repertoire includes artists whose work circulates through film, television and promotional soundtracks, alongside quieter arrangements of the same songwriters.
