items.description: Memorable melodic hooks and dramatic contrasts link the repertoire across band, electronic and acoustic treatments. Piano arrangements bring out the song melody and chordal support without reproducing the original vocal or production layers.

items.name: Boom Bap Español
items.lineage: Boom bap español gathers Spanish-language rap shaped by beatmaking traditions and a foregrounded MC. Producers and rappers sustain an underground network through collaborations, releases and performance, with recurring rhythmic backings supporting narrative, wordplay and confrontational delivery.
items.description: A single rhythmic rap lead works against a produced beat. The representative arrangement emphasizes sharply articulated phrases and a steady rhythmic foundation, leaving the backing’s specific sampled or synthesized architecture open.

items.name: Covertrance
items.lineage: Covertrance gathers dance-oriented cover versions and reinterpretations of familiar songs and themes. Trance and club producers recast recognizable melodies through electronic arrangements, vocal versions and instrumental mixes, with lounge adaptations also circulating in the wider catalogue.
items.description: Recognizable hooks meet repeating electronic bass, synthesizer figures and a steady programmed club pulse. Sung versions and extended instrumental treatments can reshape the same material for different listening and dancing settings.

items.name: Covertronica
items.lineage: Covertronica gathers electronic dance reinterpretations of familiar songs, connecting vocal remakes and remix production with club and streaming circulation. Producers rebuild recognizable hooks for contemporary dance arrangements, while DJs bring those records into continuous programmes.
items.description: In the club-programming branch, a DJ blends electronic cover records into a continuous dance sequence. Recorded voices and instrumental layers remain embedded in the tracks, with transitions shaping momentum between familiar songs.

items.name: Deep Chill
items.lineage: Deep chill connects relaxed electronic listening with lounge, Balearic and chill-house repertoire. Producers and selectors circulate melodic recordings through albums, compilations and continuous radio mixes, balancing gentle rhythmic movement with spacious textures.
items.description: Unhurried transitions and contrasting recorded selections sustain a relaxed listening flow. Instrumental colors and occasional vocals share the programme, while restrained grooves support rather than dominate the atmosphere.

items.name: Deep Comedy
items.lineage: Deep Comedy gathers recorded stand-up and comic monologues circulated through comedy clubs, specialist labels and streaming discovery. Personal stories, social observation and topical jokes depend on speech rhythm, pauses and audience address rather than a sung melody.
items.description: A solo comic shapes a spoken monologue through conversational emphasis, pauses, character and punchline timing. Dark social observation and everyday storytelling coexist within this recorded-comedy discovery field.

items.name: Deep Talent Show
items.lineage: Deep talent show gathers a deeper discovery cohort of televised singing-competition performers and their later recordings. Acoustic pop, close vocal harmonies and familiar song interpretations sit alongside fuller studio productions, connecting televised performances with independent releases and concert careers.
items.description: Blended lead and harmony voices carry a popular-song melody above acoustic-guitar chords and melodic fills. The compact acoustic branch highlights ensemble phrasing and song structure, while the broader discovery field also includes amplified bands and electronic production.

items.name: Downtempo Fusion
items.lineage: Downtempo fusion gathers artists combining relaxed electronic rhythms with song, jazz, soul and atmospheric production. Its discovery repertoire ranges from vocal-led groups to instrumental producers, with DJ programmes connecting these materials across listening and dance settings.
items.description: Layered selections unfold with relaxed pacing and gradual transitions. This DJ branch preserves recorded vocal and instrumental textures inside a continuous programme, alongside the field’s separately documented live-band and studio-production approaches.

items.name: Electropowerpop
items.lineage: Electropowerpop connects catchy pop-rock songwriting with electronic production, tuned vocal textures and dance-oriented rhythms. Its online discovery cohort includes bands and bedroom projects from the late-2000s alternative-pop scene, spanning electronic arrangements and expanded live guitar bands.
items.description: A tuned sung lead moves through compact pop hooks above electronic textures and a guitar, bass and drum foundation. Clean guitar figures and a locked bass pulse leave space for the electronic layers, while the live rhythm section gives the arrangement physical drive.

items.name: Emoplugg
items.lineage: Emoplugg is an online melodic rap label linking emotional vocal expression with plugg-related electronic beat production. Its discovery community overlaps emo rap and melodic internet rap, with processed sung phrases and intimate lyrics carried by producer-built rhythms.
items.description: A melodic lead rides a produced beat, with vocal treatment shaping the intimate sung phrases. The arrangement leaves the beat mechanism open while keeping the singer and rhythmic production separately controllable.

items.name: Flick Hop
items.lineage: Flick hop is a discovery label connecting underground rap producers and MCs across North American and European networks. Its artist corpus includes Snowgoons, Sicknature, Virtuoso, Chief Kamachi and related independent collaborators, with sample-based production and MC-led songs forming a prominent branch.
items.description: Rhythmic verses ride recurring sampled phrases and programmed drum patterns. Producers build a groove around the character of a chosen loop, adjusting drum weight and layering to its mood; other artists and releases extend the palette with keyboards, scratches and different vocal arrangements.

items.name: Groove Room
items.lineage: Groove Room brings together a contemporary network of melodic house producers and remixers. Labels and online DJ programmes connect rounded dance rhythms, tuneful electronic textures and vocal material with both club and relaxed listening.
items.description: Steady house pulses support smooth melodic phrases and recurring vocal or instrumental hooks. Mixed programmes extend the groove across tracks, balancing dance momentum with spacious transitions and polished electronic sound.

items.name: Muzică copii
items.lineage: Romanian music for children encompasses play songs, educational singing and purpose-composed instrumental repertoire. Composers and educators draw on folk idioms and contemporary popular material alongside graded pieces for young listeners and learners.
items.description: Clear melodic figures, compact forms and accessible contrasts support listening, singing and early musical learning. In the composed piano branch, connected lines and modest harmonic textures develop from simple ideas toward richer interplay.

items.name: Novos Talentos Brasileiros
items.lineage: Novos talentos brasileiros is a discovery label centered on emerging Brazilian singers, including a substantial cohort associated with televised youth singing competitions. Their repertoire crosses MPB, pop and regional song, and extends into independent releases and local concert appearances.
items.description: A small vocal ensemble shares popular-song melodies over acoustic-guitar figures and percussion. This intimate stage branch gives familiar repertoire a flexible group presentation, alongside the broader field’s larger television and studio arrangements.

items.name: Polka Norteña
items.lineage: Polka norteña is the northern Mexican adaptation of the European polka, developed through local dance, instrumental ensembles and commercial recordings. Its lively melodies and duple dance pulse circulate through accordion conjuntos, wind and string groups, and piano interpretations.
items.description: Clear melodic strains and a buoyant duple pulse shape this dance repertoire. A composed solo-piano interpretation carries melody and accompaniment within one instrument, alongside the more widely heard accordion and ensemble branches.

items.name: Proto-hyperpop
items.lineage: Proto-hyperpop gathers electronic-pop experimenters in an online discovery cohort spanning PC Music associates, digital pop producers and newer internet artists. Its repertoire connects exaggerated pop textures, electronic sound design and club mixing, with substantial overlap with hyperpop.
items.description: In the DJ branch, contrasting pop fragments and club tracks are joined through quick transitions, edits and playful changes of direction. Recorded voices and instrumental layers remain within the mixed programme.

items.name: Punjabi Lo-fi
items.lineage: Punjabi lo-fi connects Punjabi popular-song repertoire with online remix and bedroom-production communities. Producers such as MixSingh and Swattrex circulate new songs alongside softened, slowed and reverberant versions of existing recordings. The discovery field also overlaps bilingual South Asian pop and international lo-fi remix culture.
items.description: Sung melodies and existing instrumental layers can be retained within complete recorded-song reworkings. Slower pacing, extended reverberation and softened bandwidth reshape the listening texture, while the broader field also includes newly produced bedroom songs.

items.name: Remix Product
items.lineage: Remix product is a discovery label gathering commercial dance remixes, cover versions and edited club tracks. Its documented repertoire connects familiar vocal hooks with hands-up, hard-dance and other electronic club treatments, circulating through releases and mixed compilations.
items.description: An energetic DJ mix connects edited dance selections, contrasting melodic hooks and rhythmic drops. The playback-and-mixing branch retains recorded vocal and instrumental layers without pretending to identify every original production instrument.

items.name: Slow Game
items.lineage: Slow game is an online discovery label connecting contemporary R&B singers, melodic rap collaborations and club-oriented DJ productions. Its cohort includes West Coast radio and mixtape networks alongside artists from other regions, with romantic hooks, rhythmic vocal exchanges and polished electronic backing.
items.description: The DJ branch presents sung hooks and rap passages within mixed recorded tracks, connecting R&B intimacy with club energy. The broader field also includes original songs and producer-led collaborations; the label does not prescribe a single tempo or a uniformly slow performance.

items.name: Speed Up Brasileiro
items.lineage: Speed Up Brasileiro gathers accelerated versions of Brazilian popular recordings circulating through streaming and short-video platforms. Singers and producers rework their own songs alongside remixers, shortening their temporal scale while retaining recognizable vocal hooks and backing tracks.
items.description: Accelerated sung phrases and a produced beat compress a familiar song into a brisk remix. Melody and accompaniment move together through continuous phrases, with pitch treatment varying between versions.

items.name: Twin Cities indie
items.lineage: Twin Cities indie encompasses independent music rooted in Minneapolis and Saint Paul. Its regional networks bring together guitar rock, pop songwriting and folk-influenced approaches, with electronic production also entering contemporary bands.
items.description: A vocal-led electric band combines strummed guitar, bass and acoustic drums with synthesizer layers and programmed percussion. This electronic indie-pop branch sits within a wider metropolitan community of contrasting sounds.

items.name: Voidgrind
items.lineage: Voidgrind groups underground extreme-metal discoveries, including death-metal bands with dense riffs and forceful rhythmic interplay. The listening cohort overlaps cavernous, technical and grinding metal practices rather than requiring a single playing technique.
items.description: Electric guitars move between accented riffs and lead phrases above picked bass and a forceful drum kit. A foreground voice joins the amplified band, with changes of density and articulation shaping its momentum.

items.name: Westcoast Flow
items.lineage: Westcoast flow gathers contemporary West Coast rap and melodic vocal production. The named discovery cohort includes Los Angeles artists who combine conversational rhythmic delivery, sung hooks and producer-led beats, with connections to local R&B and club music.
items.description: An alternating rap-and-sung foreground sits over layered sampled rhythmic and melodic phrases. This representative studio branch leaves vocal register and the balance of speech and melody open, while supporting a clear groove and compact hooks.

items.name: Carnaval de Cádiz
items.lineage: Cádiz Carnival sustains a civic tradition of topical songs, parody and costumed street performance. Neighborhood associations, rehearsals and the official competition connect coros, comparsas, chirigotas and cuartetos, each with its own vocal organization and repertoire. The tango, pasodoble, cuplé and comic sketch give these groups distinct ways to comment on public life.
items.description: Comic dialogue, topical verses and sung cuplés share the stage in the cuarteto branch, with buzzing carnival pitos providing pitch cues. Cádiz also sustains harmonized comparsas, guitar-and-percussion chirigotas and plucked-string coros, each with its own repertoire and ensemble practice.

items.name: Pop Electrónico
items.lineage: Pop electrónico connects Spanish-language songwriting with synthesized textures, programmed accompaniment and electronic performance. Its Latin American and diaspora scenes span intimate trip-hop-influenced songs, dance-oriented pop and more expansive live arrangements.
items.description: A melodic vocal line moves through synthesized layers and programmed accompaniment. Textured electronic layers connect intimate singing with the movement of dance-oriented pop.

items.name: Dark minimal techno
items.lineage: Dark minimal techno develops sparse, ominous club music through independent production and label communities. Plazma Records and related artists combine restrained rhythmic repetition with unusual recorded sounds, dissonant details and carefully spaced electronic figures.
items.description: Small loops, sampled transients and synthesizer patterns leave pronounced spaces between events. Gradual changes in filtering, repetition and placement sustain an uneasy atmosphere without requiring a dense wall of distortion.

items.name: Dutch Drill
items.lineage: Dutch drill developed through local rap networks and exchanges with British and American drill. Amsterdam and Rotterdam performers use neighborhood references, Dutch speech and varied personal subjects, with direct street rap and more melodic crossover approaches coexisting.
items.description: Rhythmic verses ride ominous produced beats, with sharply placed drum attacks and spaces that emphasize the rapper’s cadence. Local slang and neighborhood references shape the delivery; some artists favor melodic hooks or dance-oriented crossover arrangements.

items.name: Polish Trap
items.lineage: Polish trap connects local MCs and producers with international trap production and contemporary Polish rap. Online circulation and collaborations support a broad field, from direct verse-led delivery to melodic hooks and crossover songs.
items.description: Rap cadence and repeated phrases move against produced rhythmic and tonal backing. Direct verses coexist with melodic delivery and electronic textures; producers vary the density, mood and placement of the beat around the voice.

items.name: Deep Pop EDM
items.lineage: Deep Pop EDM is a melodic dance-pop discovery field connecting electronic producers, songwriters and featured singers. Catchy melodies and relaxed house-inflected movement coexist with acoustic instrumental colors and radio-oriented arrangements.
items.description: A clear vocal melody sits among gentle piano figures, lyrical saxophone lines and electronic accompaniment. The balance favors memorable melodic phrases and an approachable dance pulse, while other artists emphasize different acoustic and electronic colors.

items.name: czsk electropop
items.lineage: CZSK Electropop connects Czech and Slovak electronic-pop artists, from independent synthesizer projects to singer-led productions. Local radio, clubs and cross-border collaborations bring together Czech, Slovak and English-language songs.
items.description: A sung melody moves against synthesizer hooks and programmed rhythm. Retro electronic colors coexist with contemporary production, visual presentation and varied song forms; acoustic and more experimental approaches also appear within the field.

items.name: Melanesian Pop
items.lineage: Melanesian pop connects popular-song communities across Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and neighboring Pacific networks. Touring singers and bands combine local languages and melodies with reggae, R&B and other contemporary song styles.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices meet guitar, bass, keyboards and percussion in a dance-oriented band setting. Repeating song phrases and relaxed or lively grooves carry local language and identity across an active regional touring circuit.

items.name: Marathi hip hop
items.lineage: Marathi hip hop gives Maharashtra’s regional language and local experiences a place within Indian rap. Artists such as Sambata build on international hip-hop influences while using Marathi vernaculars to express neighborhood identity, personal ambition and social criticism.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and emphatic phrasing move over producer-built beats. Repeated drum patterns, edited samples and contrasting backing textures support rhyme, flow and narrative, while collaborations connect local voices to wider Indian hip-hop production.

items.name: Study Beats
items.lineage: Study beats developed within online instrumental hip-hop listening, where beatmakers, labels and streaming channels connect relaxed grooves with studying and everyday concentration. Chillhop and its collaborators helped circulate this listening culture through curated streams, compilations and producer exchanges.
items.description: Repeating sampled phrases and carefully spaced drum patterns create a steady instrumental backdrop. Jazz and soul colours, soft melodic fragments and restrained changes are common, while producers also develop original compositions. The music can reward attentive listening as well as accompany study.

items.name: Greek Fem Rap
items.lineage: Greek fem rap brings women-led rap and feminist organizing into Greece’s wider hip-hop communities. Independent recordings, collective performances and local networks connect personal testimony, social criticism and changing approaches to beat-making.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, punchlines and repeated vocal phrases move over produced beats. Direct speech-like delivery can open into melodic hooks, while arrangements range from sparse rap backing to more elaborate electronic and traditional influences.

items.name: Deep Discofox
items.lineage: Deep discofox is a discovery label within German-language party and Schlager music. Familiar vocal hooks, recurring dance rhythms and festive refrains connect its performers to discofox dancing, party releases and club DJ programmes.
items.description: Direct melodies and steady dance patterns keep the repertoire accessible for communal celebration and partner dancing. DJs connect songs through mixed sets, while party-oriented recordings share space with Schlager and popular dance music.

items.name: Dutch Indie
items.lineage: Dutch indie connects independent musicians, small labels and live venues across the Netherlands. DIY collaboration links guitar bands with folk, electronic pop and more experimental songwriting; labels such as Snowstar and international showcases help these overlapping local networks reach listeners abroad.
items.description: Interlocking guitars, bass and drums can support conversational vocals, melodic refrains and deliberately rough edges. Other branches favor intimate folk or electronic textures. Collaboration and independent circulation connect the field without imposing one language, ensemble or production style.

items.name: Hjemmesnekk
items.lineage: Hjemmesnekk is the participatory song-making strand of Norwegian russetid. Graduation groups write and record their own identities into songs, sometimes making the backing themselves and often collaborating with professional producers. The finished recordings circulate at celebrations and through streaming platforms.
items.description: Catchy sung refrains, personal group lyrics and a produced rhythmic backing connect collective participation with studio songcraft. Singers record repeated takes and producers shape the vocal balance, pitch and arrangement; the music can borrow from dance, pop and rap rather than requiring a single beat style.

items.name: Belarusian Hip Hop
items.lineage: Belarusian hip hop connects local and diaspora rap communities through Belarusian- and Russian-language writing. International hip-hop influences meet neighborhood experience, personal reflection and changing social contexts, with artists moving between underground releases and wider popular circulation.
items.description: Rhythmic spoken verses ride producer-built beats, leaving space for rhyme, accent and personal narrative. Some artists emphasize Belarusian vernacular expression, while melodic collaborations and live-band experiments widen the field.

items.name: Rap Regio
items.lineage: Rap regio connects Monterrey and its surrounding communities through local MCs, studios, producers and independent releases. Neighborhood networks and collaborations have sustained both lyrical rap and changing electronic production practices.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, personal narratives and local expressions move over producer-built beats. Repetition and contrasting backing textures support rhyme and flow, while the regional scene embraces multiple production approaches.

items.name: gothic alternative
items.lineage: Gothic Alternative brings together alternative-rock and metal artists whose songs combine emotive singing with heavier guitar textures. The discovery field overlaps gothic rock and gothic metal while also including melodic hard-rock, acoustic and electronically produced branches.
items.description: A melodic lead voice contrasts with overdriven guitar lines, a grounded bass pulse and a firm drum backbeat. Piano chords can support quieter passages or reinforce the harmony as the band builds in intensity.

items.name: Aesthetic Rap
items.lineage: Aesthetic rap developed through online rap communities, SoundCloud releases and collaborative Discord networks. Its artists connect internet imagery and short, memorable tracks with varied approaches to sample-based production.
items.description: Restrained rhythmic voices contrast with bright sampled melodies and hard drum patterns. Other branches favor hazy production and reverberant vocals; internet circulation links these approaches without making every recording sound alike.

items.name: Libyan Hip Hop
items.lineage: Libyan hip hop joins local MCs and producers with diaspora collaborators. Rhythmic Arabic writing has carried personal experience, public criticism and changing hopes, while studio networks connect artists in Libya with the wider North African scene.
items.description: Direct rap phrasing rides producer-built beats and repeating rhythmic foundations. Language, flow and lyrical viewpoint shape the delivery; some projects also bring local instruments into the production, widening the field without prescribing one ensemble.

items.name: Russian Trap Metal
items.lineage: Russian trap metal connects aggressive rap delivery and metal-influenced vocal intensity with producer-built beats. Artists in Russia and the diaspora use online releases and collaborations to move between trap, heavy electronic music and metal aesthetics.
items.description: Forceful bars and screams sit above hard rhythmic production. Vocal distortion and abrupt changes can heighten the tension, while beatmakers shape the backing through varied electronic methods; individual tracks may add guitars or other layers.

items.name: Glitch Beats
items.lineage: Glitch beats brings finely edited rhythms and synthetic sound design into experimental electronic production. Its discovery community spans intimate studio composition, beat-oriented pieces and manipulated digital textures.
items.description: Short synthesized tones and intricately placed rhythmic events create patterns that shift between groove and interruption. Detailed software editing lets small attacks, pauses and timbral changes shape the arrangement.

items.name: Flamenco Fusion
items.lineage: Flamenco fusion extends flamenco singing, guitar and dance through contemporary composition and cross-cultural collaboration. Acoustic companies and larger amplified ensembles coexist, connecting Andalusian musical vocabulary with new theatrical and popular-music settings.
items.description: Ornamented singing and sharply articulated guitar interweave with percussion and the dancer’s rhythmic footwork. Contrasting vocal passages and instrumental responses create a theatrical dialogue, while contemporary arrangements can draw on a wider palette.

items.name: Antilliaanse Rap
items.lineage: Antilliaanse rap connects Dutch Caribbean artists and diasporic communities through local releases, studios and collaborations. Papiamento and Dutch-language practices coexist with wider international hip-hop influences.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and vocal hooks move over producer-built beats. Direct delivery, repeated phrases and changes of flow support personal stories and dance-oriented tracks across varied production styles.

items.name: Thai teen pop
items.lineage: Thai teen pop develops around youth-oriented performers, labels and fan communities within the wider Thai popular-music industry. Kamikaze became a prominent centre through acts such as Four-Mod, Faye Fang Kaew and K-OTIC, linking melodic songs, choreography and a shared youth style.
items.description: Catchy sung hooks, dance rhythms and polished arrangements connect romantic songs with energetic group performances. Electronic pop textures and rhythmic backing support soloists and vocal groups, while concerts and later reunions sustain the repertoire across generations.

items.name: Regional Mexicano Femenil
items.lineage: Women performers have shaped Mexican regional song through ranchera, mariachi, banda, norteño and grupera traditions. Recorded repertoire, touring bills and broadcast programmes connect established interpreters with newer singers across Mexico and its diaspora.
items.description: Expressive lead singing connects romantic songs, narrative repertoire and regional dance forms. Accompaniment ranges from intimate guitar settings to full mariachi, banda and amplified groups; the women-centered discovery field crosses those established styles.

items.name: Deep Euro House
items.lineage: Deep euro house is a discovery label connecting European-oriented melodic house, vocal crossover records and club producers. Its artist network spans radio-friendly songs, deep-house grooves and longer underground mixes, circulating through streaming playlists, labels and DJ programmes.
items.description: Melodic phrases and vocal hooks ride steady electronic grooves, with warm or spacious textures alongside more driving club tracks. The DJ branch mixes complete recordings; the wider repertoire includes original songs and varied producer collaborations.

items.name: Música Tropical Guatemalteca
items.lineage: Guatemalan tropical music connects the national marimba tradition with popular dance repertoires including cumbia, salsa and merengue. Marimba ensembles and larger marimba orchestras circulate through community celebrations, public concerts and migrant audiences.
items.description: Wooden marimba melodies and chordal patterns meet repeating tropical dance grooves. Ensembles range from marimba-led instrumental groups with bass, drums and keyboard to larger vocal orchestras with wind instruments and additional percussion.

items.name: Indonesian Viral Pop
items.lineage: Indonesian viral pop connects popular songs and cover performances through social-video circulation. Home recordings, repeatable hooks and online audiences can lead singers into label releases and television appearances.
items.description: Memorable vocal melodies are central, with arrangements ranging from singer-and-guitar covers to fuller produced pop. The acoustic branch foregrounds a clear sung line and steady chordal accompaniment.

items.name: Fußball
items.lineage: Fußball song culture in German-speaking communities includes club anthems, supporter chants, comic songs and recordings for tournaments and celebrations. Familiar refrains connect football identity with participatory popular music.
items.description: Collective singing and memorable refrains range from short crowd chants to fully arranged popular songs. A cappella groups can carry both melody and rhythmic backing through voices alone.

items.name: Malaysian Tamil Pop
items.lineage: Malaysian Tamil pop connects locally produced Tamil songs, independent singles and film music. Singers and producers combine melodic hooks with contemporary production and folk-derived expression, circulating through Malaysian studios, screen productions and online releases.
items.description: Memorable sung melodies and answering harmonies meet varied rhythmic settings, from studio beats to vocal percussion. Romantic songs, energetic hooks and semi-folk phrasing share a multilingual Malaysian popular-music setting. A cappella arrangements foreground the contrast between melodic voices and mouth-made rhythm.

items.name: Pop Teen Brasileiro
items.lineage: Brazilian teen pop links youth-oriented singers and vocal groups with television, online audiences and live pop events. Romantic and coming-of-age songs draw on contemporary pop, dance production and ballad singing, with successive generations moving between solo careers and group projects.
items.description: Direct melodic hooks and personal lyrics foreground first relationships, friendship and growing up. Sustained chorus notes and expressive vocal peaks sit over varied pop backing, including electronic beats. The field embraces solo ballads, vocal groups and dance-oriented tracks rather than one fixed production style.

items.name: Dalarna Indie
items.lineage: Dalarna indie gathers independent popular-music artists around Falun, Borlänge and neighboring communities. Regional venues, studios and development initiatives connect guitar bands, electronic acts and singer-songwriters, helping local songs circulate beyond the region.
items.description: Melodic songwriting links varied local pop and rock practices. Intimate piano-led songs emphasize vocal phrasing and harmonic movement, while guitar bands and electronic projects bring contrasting textures to the same regional scene. Independent releases, concerts and artist-development networks sustain this breadth.

items.name: Modern Bollywood
items.lineage: Modern Bollywood foregrounds recent Hindi-film songs and their circulation beyond the cinema through streaming, concerts and instrumental arrangements. Romantic melody, dance-oriented production and contrasting playback voices coexist in a repertoire associated with composers and singers including Mithoon, Pritam, Arijit Singh and Amit Trivedi.
items.description: Memorable melodic refrains and chordal support carry both intimate ballads and more energetic songs. In the published solo-piano branch, the keyboard carries melody and accompaniment together; the wider film and recording repertoire also uses singers, bands, orchestras and electronic production.

items.name: Shush
items.lineage: Shush gathers softly continuous environmental recordings, noise and quiet instrumental music used for unobtrusive listening. Rain, waves and stream recordings feature prominently in its creator selection, alongside piano and other gentle textures.
items.description: A rain-field-recording branch preserves changing water noise and its surrounding atmosphere without adding a sung lead or instrumental accompaniment. The wider listening field also includes sea, river and noise recordings and subdued music; its name does not restrict it to a person making a shushing sound.

items.name: Pop LGBTQ+ Brasileira
items.lineage: Brazilian LGBTQ+ pop is a cross-style discovery community shaped by collaborating artists, releases and festivals. Liniker and related songwriters connect contemporary popular song with soul, samba and other Brazilian traditions.
items.description: Melodic hooks, recurring song sections and expressive harmonic motion connect a varied popular-song repertoire. Acoustic interpretations bring the melody forward over sustained chordal support.

items.name: Shib
items.lineage: Shib is an internet discovery grouping that brings together independent rap, pop-facing songs and instrumental beat music. Its creator selection includes Steven Cooper, whose direct lyrical delivery and pop–hip-hop production sit alongside gentler instrumental recordings elsewhere in the field.
items.description: The rapped branch places a clearly articulated lead over produced accompaniment, using rhythmic verses and memorable phrases to carry personal or motivational writing. Other recordings favor melodic singing or instrumental textures, so the grouping does not prescribe one tempo, vocal style or production method.

items.name: Russian Pixel
items.lineage: Russian Pixel connects Russian-language game-video creators and their song audiences. Minecraft references, online characters and playful personal stories circulate through rap, pop songs and collaborative releases by creators including Фиксай, Топовский, Yellow Fire and Компот.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal phrases and recognizable hooks meet produced beats in one common branch. Lyrics and animated clips draw on games and shared online references, while arrangements range from rap-led tracks to melodic singing and remixes.

items.name: Música Mexiquense
items.lineage: Música mexiquense brings together traditional ensembles and contemporary songwriters associated with Estado de México. Local studios and concert networks connect regional repertoire with Mexican popular song.
items.description: Melodic vocal phrases unfold over piano harmony in an intimate popular-song setting. Traditional repertoire and contemporary songwriting circulate through varied regional arrangements.

items.name: Rap Salvadoreño
items.lineage: Rap salvadoreño connects MCs, beatmakers and independent labels across El Salvador and its diaspora. Personal narrative and social commentary meet varied production approaches, from boom-bap grooves to contemporary urban styles.
items.description: Rhythmic verses sit over producer-built accompaniment, with changes of flow and phrasing shaping the pulse. A direct MC lead and a repeating beat provide one established branch of a wider Salvadoran rap field.

items.name: Irish Trap
items.lineage: Irish trap connects rappers, singers and producers working across Ireland and its diasporic communities. Trap production intersects with R&B, pop and other hip-hop approaches through independent releases, collaborations and live performances.
items.description: A direct rhythmic vocal rides over DJ-led recorded accompaniment. Repeated hooks, changes of flow and shifts in the backing connect hard-edged rap with more melodic material across the wider field.

items.name: Pakistani Hip Hop
items.lineage: Pakistani hip-hop brings rappers and producers together across urban scenes and diasporic networks. Urdu, Punjabi and other languages carry personal narratives, social commentary and wordplay over varied beat-driven production.
items.description: Rhythmic rap phrases ride a producer-built backing, using changes of flow and emphasis to bring the lyrics forward. Sparse accompaniment and direct vocal delivery form one established branch alongside melodic hooks and larger collaborations.

items.name: Viral Afropop
items.lineage: Contemporary African pop circulated through short-form video, streaming and cross-border collaborations. Memorable vocal passages and producer-led grooves connect Afropop, Afrobeats and R&B songwriting with rapidly expanding online audiences.
items.description: Melodic lead singing and concise hooks move over producer-built rhythmic backing. Personal stories, relaxed vocal phrasing and danceable repetitions travel through clips, covers and social-media participation, while full songs retain varied pop and R&B arrangements.

items.name: Gong
items.lineage: Southeast Asian gong-ensemble discovery field spanning Balinese gong orchestras, Sumatran talempong and Philippine kulintang communities. Tuned gongs and related instruments organize interlocking patterns, repeating melodic cycles and contrasting ensemble textures.
items.description: Layered gong patterns connect slower structural tones with faster melodic elaboration. Balinese kebyar practice adds bright metallophones, bamboo flutes, hand drums and sharply coordinated changes of pace and dynamics; related regional ensembles develop their own tunings, instrument groupings and social uses.
exemplars: Gong Kebyar of the Puri of Peliatan

items.name: ZXC
items.lineage: ZXC is an online discovery field connecting emotional rap, phonk-adjacent production and gaming or anime-associated scenes. Russian-language Dota and dead-inside communities overlap with a wider multilingual internet-rap cohort, circulated through streaming and social platforms.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and emotionally charged hooks sit over produced beats, with metallic cowbell patterns prominent in the phonk-facing branch. The broader field also includes melodic and atmospheric tracks; the shared discovery label does not impose one language, tempo or production device.

items.name: Lounge House
items.lineage: Lounge house connects house music with relaxed listening and social spaces such as beach clubs, hotel lounges and sunset gatherings. DJs, producers and live collaborators draw on melodic club music, chill-out textures and familiar songs.
items.description: Steady dance grooves support flowing melodies and an inviting atmosphere. DJ sets may be joined by live saxophone improvisation, while recorded and instrumental selections move between gentle background listening and more active dancing.

items.name: Chakma Pop
items.lineage: Chakma pop carries contemporary songs in the Chakma language through local studios, online video and cross-border community networks. Romantic writing and cultural identity connect newer compositions with established song traditions, while digital production lets singers collaborate with arrangers beyond their hometowns.
items.description: A foreground sung melody meets arranged recorded accompaniment. Personal lyrics and repeated song sections carry romantic and community themes, with home recording and online circulation supporting exchanges between singers, arrangers and listeners.

items.name: Hyperpop Italiano
items.lineage: Italian hyperpop developed through independent electronic producers, online collaborations and small labels. Digital experimentation meets Italian-language songwriting, with a varied scene connecting pop melodies to distorted and fragmented textures.
items.description: Processed singing, reshaped samples and synthesizer layers build sharply contrasting digital arrangements. Hooks may fragment or change function as timbre and editing become compositional devices, with intimate lyrics set against dense electronic sound.

items.name: Gypsy
items.lineage: Romani musical traditions span distinct communities across Europe and beyond, carried through family teaching, theatre, touring ensembles and recordings. Russian Romani guitar, Balkan ensembles and flamenco-related performance are among the overlapping regional practices gathered under this historical discovery label.
items.description: Russian Romani solo guitar combines resonant open strings, bass movement and elaborated melodic phrases. Fingerstyle variation and contrasts of touch develop familiar musical material, alongside the singing, dancing and larger ensembles found in other Romani traditions.

items.name: Khortha Pop
items.lineage: Khortha pop circulates through regional singers, recording studios and video labels in Jharkhand and neighboring areas. Contemporary romantic and festive songs connect local-language expression with studio arrangement and electronic production.
items.description: Sung local-language melodies sit over arranged electronic accompaniment. Repeated vocal phrases and contrasting song sections give romantic and dance-oriented material an accessible form, while production ranges from restrained textures to lively rhythmic layers.

items.name: Solfeggio Product
items.lineage: Solfeggio product is a frequency-themed listening category circulated through digital meditation and ambient catalogues. Named-frequency releases appear alongside quiet music, noise and environmental sound, with titles and packaging organizing the listening experience. The label describes publishing and discovery practice rather than the historical solfège teaching system.
items.description: Sustained tones and gently interacting overtones provide a minimal listening branch. Long durations and small changes in texture replace verse-based song development; other releases combine frequency-labelled sounds with broader ambient or environmental layers.

items.name: Edinburgh Indie
items.lineage: Edinburgh’s independent music community connects small venues, labels and artist-led networks. Guitar bands, intimate songwriting and electronically produced pop coexist, with local collaborations linking the city to the wider Scottish scene.
items.description: Song-led performances range from close voice-and-piano writing to full guitar bands and layered electronic arrangements. In a piano-led branch, melodic vocal runs unfold over changing chords, while independent production and performance networks connect varied personal styles.

items.name: Deep Vocal House
items.lineage: Deep vocal house connects expressive dance singing with club remixes and DJ circulation. Its discovery repertoire crosses soulful house, dance-pop and extended vocal remixes, bringing distinctive singers into electronic dance settings.
items.description: Prominent sung melodies and short vocal flourishes ride recurring dance rhythms. Radio edits and longer club mixes place the voice in changing electronic textures, while live vocal appearances and DJ sets carry the repertoire into social dance spaces.

items.name: Progressive Trance House
items.lineage: Progressive trance house connects melodic house and trance through labels, producers and extended DJ programmes. The Silk-associated cohort includes Shingo Nakamura, PROFF and Something Good, alongside wider progressive club networks.
items.description: Gradual builds, sustained melodic layers and recurring dance grooves link tracks across long mixes. Lyrical keyboard colours and spacious passages coexist with more driving rhythms, with DJs shaping the sequence and continuity.

items.name: Modern Uplift
items.lineage: Modern uplift gathers melodic contemporary rock and pop-rock through digital discovery. Guitar bands balance reflective verses with expansive, memorable choruses, connecting alternative-rock textures with accessible songcraft.
items.description: Lead singing rides electric guitar, bass, keyboards and a drum backbeat, with additional percussion widening the rhythmic texture. Contrasts between restrained verses and energetic choruses give the songs their rising shape.

items.name: Indie Surf
items.lineage: Indie surf brings surf-derived guitar colors and vocal harmonies into contemporary independent pop and garage-rock scenes. DIY recording, small labels and touring connect artists whose music ranges from hazy melodic songs to brisk, rhythm-led bands.
items.description: Warm guitar figures and harmonized singing ride a bass-and-drum backbeat. Bright melodies, relaxed vocal delivery and garage-rock roughness can coexist, while other branches add keyboards, electronic layers or denser studio arrangements.

items.name: Música Catarinense
items.lineage: Música catarinense encompasses original songs and varied popular-music practices connected with Santa Catarina. Local composers, festivals, universities and independent performers sustain a repertoire shaped by coastal and inland communities, with MPB, folk, samba and rock among its overlapping traditions.
items.description: A voice-and-guitar branch places local songwriting beside MPB, bossa nova and samba. Changing harmonies and rhythmic guitar accompaniment support clear sung texts, while the wider regional field also embraces ensembles, amplified bands and instrumental work.

items.name: Deep Minimal Techno
items.lineage: Deep minimal techno gathers DJs and producers across stripped-back techno and deeper club grooves. Its discovery cohort includes Sam Paganini, Hollen and Luigi Madonna alongside more melodic and house-adjacent producers.
items.description: Repeated rhythmic figures, restrained changes and sustained tension shape extended club listening. DJs connect tracks through pacing, transitions and recurring grooves, with darker textures and melodic passages varying across the field.

items.name: Stomp Pop
items.lineage: Stomp pop brings together rhythm-forward indie and alternative-pop bands whose emphatic beats and compact hooks translate readily to live performance. Electric riffs, forceful drums and memorable vocal exchanges connect guitar-pop melody with the energy of alternative rock.
items.description: Emphatic drum patterns and guitar riffs support melodic leads and answering vocals. Compact duo performances can sound full through amplified rhythm guitar and a forceful kick drum, alongside larger-band and more polished pop arrangements.

items.name: Nuevo tango
items.lineage: Nuevo tango developed through Astor Piazzolla’s expansion of Argentine tango into composed concert music, incorporating jazz, counterpoint and adventurous harmony. It circulates through instrumental ensembles and published solo arrangements as well as recordings.
items.description: Tango phrasing meets extended harmony, contrapuntal lines and dramatic contrasts. Concert works and intimate instrumental arrangements carry this repertoire beyond the conventions of the traditional dance orchestra.

items.name: Speed Plug Brasileiro
items.lineage: Speed Plug Brasileiro circulates accelerated Brazilian plug and trap recordings through streaming releases and online remix culture. Artists issue speed versions beside their original recordings, retaining recognizable vocal phrases and electronic backings within a compressed time scale.
items.description: Rap phrases, melodic inflections and produced beats become brisker through accelerated playback or tempo processing. Recognizable hooks and continuous phrases connect the remixes to their source songs, while producers vary pitch treatment and the degree of acceleration.

items.name: Plena Uruguaya
items.lineage: Plena uruguaya developed within Uruguay’s tropical dance orchestras, adapting Caribbean influences into local rhythms, arrangements and repertoires. Montevideo ensembles, dance venues and later recordings carried the style across generations, alongside related cumbia and other national popular traditions.
items.description: Voices and bright trumpet figures ride a piano-and-bass foundation, with timbales and hand drums shaping the dance pulse. Repeated phrases and clear rhythmic grounding link the orchestral sound to social dancing; later ensembles expand the palette with electronic keyboards and other horns.

items.name: Breaks
items.lineage: Breaks is a broad electronic dance label centered on syncopated broken-beat rhythms, bass movement and sample-led hooks. DJ mixing connects its funk and hip-hop roots with club production, with related breakbeat, big-beat and bass-music practices overlapping in repertoires and performers.
items.description: Broken drum patterns and bass weight support cut-up hooks and rhythmic transitions. Recorded mixing strings these materials into dance programmes, crossing related funk, hip-hop and electronic styles without requiring one fixed tempo or hardware setup.

items.name: Deep CCM
items.lineage: Deep CCM is a contemporary Christian listening field connecting worship songwriters, prayer-room musicians and independent devotional releases. Its network includes Jon Thurlow, Misty Edwards, United Pursuit and related worship communities, linking personal prayer with music shared in congregational gatherings.
items.description: Melodic devotional singing ranges from intimate piano-supported songs to communal band arrangements. Repeated choruses, scripture-shaped texts and room for spontaneous musical development connect reflective listening with worship participation.

items.name: Techno Rave
items.lineage: Techno rave draws together contemporary warehouse and festival techno communities. Its discovery cohort includes CLTX, WNDRLST and Blame the Mono, with hard-techno pressure, trance influences and rave-oriented DJ performance.
items.description: Forceful recurring kicks, insistent bass figures and changing electronic textures drive extended dance sets. Melodic tension and rougher passages can alternate as DJs shape the energy of a room.

items.name: Deep Progressive Trance
items.lineage: Deep progressive trance follows the melodic, atmospheric side of progressive club music. Its discovery cohort includes Global Experience, Basic Perspective and Daniel Wanrooy, connecting trance production with longer-form DJ listening.
items.description: Layered melodies, recurring bass patterns and gradual transitions build an extended arc. Restrained passages can open into brighter rhythmic peaks, while vocal tracks and instrumental textures coexist within DJ programmes.

items.name: Gaming Dubstep
items.lineage: Gaming dubstep is an online discovery field connecting contemporary bass-music listeners with gaming and streaming culture. Its creator cohort includes UBUR, Barely Alive and Chime, spanning heavy dubstep, riddim and more melodic electronic approaches.
items.description: Bass-led drops, recurring electronic riffs and contrasting build-ups support high-energy listening. DJ programmes connect these tracks into longer sets, with recorded voices and effects remaining part of the mix.

items.name: Men Chika
items.lineage: Men chika is a Japanese male-idol discovery field connecting independently circulating groups, recurring live appearances and close fan participation. Bright dance songs and more reflective ballads coexist in its repertoire.
items.description: Melodic refrains and direct sung texts carry songs associated with male idol groups. Their repertoire also circulates through karaoke, where a singer performs over an arranged digital accompaniment. Group staging, vocal exchanges and studio layers vary across artists.

items.name: Zen
items.lineage: Zen-labelled listening music draws on imagery and practices of contemplation across acoustic improvisation, ambient composition and relaxation recordings. Cross-cultural collaborations helped circulate Japanese instrumental colors within this broad recorded-music field.
items.description: Unhurried phrases, spacious pauses and contrasting sustained and plucked sounds create a contemplative setting. An acoustic improvisational branch combines clarinet, shakuhachi and koto; other recordings use electronic textures or environmental sound.

items.name: Anime Drill
items.lineage: Anime drill brings character references and fan storytelling into drill-facing rap production. Online creators connect anime narratives with rapped verses, low bass and programmed beats, overlapping the wider anime-rap and nerdcore communities.
items.description: Rhythmic rap verses interpret anime characters and stories over programmed percussion and low bass. Electronic lead figures and chordal layers support the vocal narrative, with different creators drawing on drill, trap and broader online rap production.

items.name: Koligeet
items.lineage: Koligeet is the song tradition of Maharashtra’s coastal Koli communities. Fishing life, weddings and seasonal celebrations feed an oral repertoire also carried into commercial albums, stage orchestras and dance remixes.
items.description: Melodic verses and repeating calls carry community stories and invitations over a lively hand-drum pulse. Compact street singing sits alongside larger wind-and-percussion ensembles and contemporary recorded song arrangements.

items.name: Soul Flow
items.lineage: Soul flow is a recorded hip-hop discovery field connecting rappers and producers through rhythmic delivery, sample-based construction and crossover listening. It circulates alongside alternative and jazz-influenced rap, with both produced songs and separately issued vocal versions.
items.description: Conversational rap phrasing, repeating cadences and changing verbal accents keep the vocal line prominent. Sampled grooves characterize a production branch, while unaccompanied versions expose the pacing and interaction of the voices.

items.name: Russian Drain
items.lineage: Russian Drain connects Russian-language internet rap and melodic song through collaborating performers and online discovery. Artists such as Sqwore,17 Seventeen and Cupsize move among reflective hooks, emotionally direct verses and electronically produced tracks.
items.description: Vocal introductions, recurring hooks and contrasting verses meet produced rhythmic backing. Collaborations and changes in delivery link melodic pop phrasing with rap, while individual releases vary in vocal processing and electronic texture.

items.name: Japanese Concert Band
items.lineage: Japanese concert-band music links school, university, community and professional wind ensembles through concert programmes, competitions and published arrangements. Original concert works, marches, film themes and popular-song arrangements circulate alongside international wind-band repertoire.
items.description: Woodwinds and brass exchange melodic lines over low-register support and percussion. Contrasting dynamics, blended sustained passages and clearly articulated ensemble figures shape music written for both compact bands and large sections.

items.name: Finnish Drill
items.lineage: Finnish drill connects local rap voices with the transnational circulation of drill. The discovery field includes street-facing verses and crossover performers whose beats also draw on contemporary trap and club music.
items.description: Rhythmic Finnish rap delivery sits over produced beats, with space for the performer’s cadence and local references. Harder street-rap approaches coexist with melodic and club-facing work across the discovery community.

items.name: Rap Anime
items.lineage: Spanish-language fan-rap communities reinterpret anime characters and narratives through songs, fictional battles and collaborations. Online video channels connect this repertoire with wider gaming, animation and popular-culture rap.
items.description: Rhythmic character verses, storytelling and imagined battles connect anime fandom with rap performance. The Spanish-speaking discovery community also includes game and cartoon crossovers; produced songs coexist with separately released vocal-only versions.

items.name: Persian Melodic Rap
items.lineage: Persian melodic rap connects Persian-language rap with sung hooks and song-oriented crossover. Its discovery community includes independent rappers, producers and melodic singers circulating through online releases and collaborations.
items.description: Melody and lyrical expression share space with rhythmic rap delivery across this Persian-language listening field. Produced tracks coexist with intimate song renditions, including voice-and-piano arrangements that foreground melody and text.

items.name: Latin Viral Rap
items.lineage: Latin viral rap is a web-circulating discovery community around Spanish-language fan songs, fictional battles, games and online personalities. Independent video creators connect character narratives with humor and rap performance.
items.description: Rhythmic verses, recognizable characters and direct references to online culture organize these songs. Produced tracks and vocal-only fan-battle editions share a community that crosses gaming, anime and creator tributes.

items.name: Sludgecore
items.lineage: Sludgecore connects heavy, abrasive band music with hardcore urgency, doom-derived weight and noise-rock textures. International bands circulate through independent releases and touring networks, overlapping sludge metal while emphasizing varied forms of distorted riffing and forceful vocal delivery.
items.description: Weighty guitar figures and abrasive bass lock into forceful drum patterns beneath projected vocals. Slow pressure can alternate with more urgent passages, while rough textures and recurring riffs sustain the ensemble’s momentum.

items.name: Electra
items.lineage: Electra is a discovery field joining varied experimental electronic composition, song and club practices. Its repertoire includes Laurel Halo, Sarah Davachi, Lucrecia Dalt and Holly Herndon, spanning detailed sound design, acoustic-electronic combinations and contrasting approaches to rhythm.
items.description: Electronic texture, transformed acoustic material and carefully shaped space connect contrasting pieces. Club-oriented branches combine techno, bass music and layered drum rhythms; other works open toward ambient listening, vocal experimentation and composition.

items.name: Gamecore
items.lineage: Gamecore gathers video-game remixers, composers and instrumental interpreters across online listening and festival communities. Recognisable game melodies meet electronic dance production, chiptune colours, band arrangements and cinematic reinterpretations.
items.description: Game themes and newly composed motifs circulate as records, remixes and DJ programmes. The electronic performance branch connects melodic hooks with dance rhythms while retaining the recorded voices, instruments and effects within each selection.

items.name: Persian Sad Rap
items.lineage: Persian sad rap is an online listening field within Persian-language rap and song crossover. Its artists work across Iranian and diasporic production networks, connecting personal writing with independently produced recordings.
items.description: A close rhythmic rap line and produced accompaniment foreground the words. The wider listening community also includes sung hooks and collaborative songs, with reflective expression and contemporary rap production sharing the same space.

items.name: Fake
items.lineage: Fake is a catalogue discovery label encompassing tribute recordings, karaoke versions and instrumental remakes of familiar popular songs. Its repertoire ranges from dance remixes and sound-alike performances to acoustic and piano adaptations, with song recognition linking otherwise different arrangements.
items.description: Recognizable melodies and harmonic patterns remain central as popular songs move into new vocal, instrumental or backing-track versions. Piano arrangements carry the tune and accompaniment together, while other branches use complete bands, electronic production or karaoke backing.

items.name: Rasiya
items.lineage: Rasiya is a Braj-region song field spanning Krishna-associated seasonal singing, public poetic contests and commercial folk-pop. Hathrasi performers elaborate prosodic and melodic patterns in exchanges between singing clubs, while recorded circulation also carries secular, playful and romantic songs.
items.description: Projected lead phrases receive emphatic choral answers over harmonium and hand- and stick-played drums. Verse invention and recurring melodic patterns shape the exchange; freer solo delivery can alternate with measured refrains. The broader recorded repertoire includes many lighter popular arrangements.

items.name: Glitchbreak
items.lineage: Glitchbreak is an online electronic label connecting breakcore, drum-and-bass, alternative rave and sample-heavy remix production. Producers cut and recombine rhythmic material, while collaborative mashup projects and recorded mixes circulate alongside original tracks.
items.description: Fragmented break rhythms and reworked samples connect the field to breakcore and digital collage. The recorded-mixing branch layers existing material into continuous programmes, retaining sung voices, instrumental fragments and percussion within playback. Other branches compose original tracks and remixes.

items.name: Experimental Big Band
items.lineage: Experimental Big Band extends large-ensemble jazz through collective improvisation, unconventional orchestration and the meeting of composed structures with open forms. Free-jazz orchestras and later creative big bands offer different approaches within this field.
items.description: Contrasting reed registers, low winds and rhythm-section textures can build dense collective passages or open into sparse exchanges. Sectional writing and individual improvisation interact, with some ensembles also drawing on rock or minimalism.

items.name: Plug Brasileiro
items.lineage: Plug brasileiro connects Brazilian rappers and producers through internet releases, melodic experimentation and self-produced beats. The local network adapts the spacious beat vocabulary of plugg to Portuguese-language expression, with some artists also drawing on samba, arrocha and other Brazilian song forms.
items.description: Rapped phrases and melodic inflections sit over spacious produced beats. Online collaboration and independent releases connect a Brazilian network whose music ranges from understated reflection to playful crossovers with local popular styles.

items.name: Dubstep Product
items.lineage: Dubstep product groups bass-heavy electronic releases, remixes and crossover productions circulated through digital catalogues. The field includes producers who combine forceful electronic rhythms, melodic material and contrasting organic or synthetic textures.
items.description: A DJ presentation blends prepared tracks and original loops into a continuous bass-led programme. Recorded vocal and instrumental layers remain inside the mixed material while transitions shape its momentum.

items.name: Filthstep
items.lineage: Filthstep circulates within heavy dubstep and bass-music communities, emphasizing abrasive electronic textures, forceful drops and contrasting rhythmic passages. Producer releases, label compilations and DJ programmes connect the term with brostep, drumstep and related bass styles.
items.description: A back-to-back DJ programme carries heavy bass selections through transitions and changes of rhythmic density. Recorded vocals, samples and instrumental layers remain in the full mixed material.

items.name: Desi Emo Rap
items.lineage: Desi emo rap connects emotionally direct rap with South Asian independent recording networks. Artists including MC Insane, Big Scratch and Tanishq foreground personal distress, relationships and resilience through local-language verses and collaborations with producers.
items.description: Intimate or urgent words meet producer-built accompaniment, with rhythmic verses and melodic hooks offering different ways to express vulnerability. The rapped branch places a direct lead voice over a repeating beat, while arrangements and vocal processing vary between artists.

items.name: Vintage Schlager
items.lineage: Vintage Schlager gathers older German-language popular songs associated with shellac records, sound films, revues and dance cafés. Interwar entertainers and later interpreters connect theatrical delivery, memorable refrains and sentimental melody in a repertoire that continues through recordings, concerts and piano arrangements.
items.description: Tuneful refrains, clear chordal movement and contrasting verse passages carry romantic, comic and nostalgic songs. Piano arrangements bring melody and accompaniment together, while the wider repertoire also includes solo singers, vocal groups and dance orchestras.

items.name: Tape Club
items.lineage: Tape Club gathers independent pop associated with small labels, mail-order discovery, personal mixtapes and intimate band communities. Its international repertoire overlaps twee pop, C86 and later indie pop, linking British guitar-pop traditions with North American and other independent scenes.
items.description: Interwoven clean guitar lines and closely blended singing carry concise, personal songs. The repertoire ranges from brisk jangling pop to quieter reflective writing, with small-scale arrangements that leave melodic details exposed.

items.name: Swedish Trap Pop
items.lineage: Swedish trap pop connects melodic rap, popular-song hooks and trap-oriented production in Sweden. Its listening community includes Dree Low, Dani M, Blizzy and artists who move between rap, drill and sung pop crossover.
items.description: Melodic phrases and recurring hooks sit alongside rhythmic verses and produced beats. The repertoire also circulates through instrumental song arrangements, where a keyboard carries the melody and harmonic support.

items.name: Persian Trap
items.lineage: Persian trap circulates through Persian-language rap collaborations and online producer networks. Its discovery repertoire includes Fxrtem, Cinq5o, Feryoung and related performers, with substantial overlap with melodic rap and the wider Persian hip-hop field.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal phrasing works against produced accompaniment, while tracks vary in their melodic content, vocal treatment and rhythmic density. Collaborations between performers and beat producers connect home and studio production with online releases.

items.name: Futuristic Swag
items.lineage: Futuristic swag connects late-2000s Atlanta club rap, playful self-presentation and buoyant producer-led recordings. Yung L.A., J Money and F.L.Y. are central reference points for a listening community whose influence continues in newer Atlanta rap.
items.description: An agile rapped lead rides a produced beat, with recurring rhythmic phrases and room for spontaneous cadences. The wider repertoire links dance hooks, melodic crossover and colorful electronic production.

items.name: GbVfi
items.lineage: GbVfi is a listening field connecting Guided by Voices, Robert Pollard’s associated projects and neighboring independent guitar-song communities. Its repertoire spans concise melodic rock, handmade recordings and more expansive studio arrangements.
items.description: Melodic lead singing meets ringing guitar chords and a steady bass-and-drum foundation. Short hooks and changes in rhythmic emphasis give the band a direct, lively character while leaving space for stranger song ideas.

items.name: Corrosion
items.lineage: Corrosion connects gothic-rock and darkwave bands carrying the melodic, atmospheric side of post-punk into later independent scenes. Expressive singing, interlocking electric guitars and bass combine with keyboards and programmed rhythms, supporting songs of melancholy, romantic tension and nocturnal imagery.
items.description: Layered vocal and keyboard textures frame recurring guitar figures and a firm bass foundation. Programmed percussion can give the songs a regular pulse, while darker harmonies and spacious arrangements link contemporary recordings to the gothic-rock revival.

items.name: Indie Rockism
items.lineage: Indie rockism gathers contemporary melodic guitar bands whose recordings connect independent pop hooks with energetic rock performance. PUBLIC, Colony House and similar projects circulate between local scenes, touring bills and online listening communities.
items.description: Lead and supporting voices meet ringing electric guitar, bass, drums and synthesizer color. Recurring hooks and a buoyant pulse give the songs a direct, danceable character while a live band supplies dynamic accents.

items.name: Gymcore
items.lineage: Gymcore groups forceful, melodic hard-rock listening around bands such as Silent Season, Message from Sylvia and Fight Like Sin. Its hooks, amplified riffs and emphatic rhythm sections connect contemporary alternative-rock recordings with energetic live performance.
items.description: Projected sung hooks rise over heavy electric-guitar figures, a grounded bass line and driving drums. Melodic refrains and contrasts in weight keep the music direct and energetic.

items.name: Modern Dream Pop
items.lineage: Modern dream pop extends atmospheric independent pop through intimate singing, repeating melodic figures and richly layered guitar, keyboard and electronic textures. Its contemporary bands and solo artists revisit earlier dream-pop and shoegaze approaches while circulating through independent labels, concerts and streaming communities.
items.description: Suspended melodic phrases and recurring harmonies give the songs a hazy, reflective character. Piano interpretations place melody and accompaniment together on one keyboard, while the broader repertoire also uses voices, guitars, organs, synthesizers and programmed or live rhythms.

items.name: Pop R&B
items.lineage: Pop R&B connects rhythm-and-blues vocal expression with concise popular songwriting, melodic hooks and contemporary production. The repertoire crosses ballads, dance-oriented songs and intimate vocal performances, with both electronic recordings and acoustic instrumental interpretations.
items.description: Memorable refrains, expressive melodic turns and repeating harmonic patterns connect pop songcraft with R&B phrasing. Piano arrangements combine the vocal melody and harmonic support on one keyboard; sung versions may add layered voices, bass, keyboards and programmed rhythms.

items.name: Flamenco Urbano
items.lineage: Flamenco urbano connects Spanish rap and flamenco-inflected song with trap and reggaetón production. Artists such as Nyno Vargas, Omar Montes, Daviles de Novelda and Mala Rodríguez participate in a collaborating urban-music community.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and melodic hooks interact with produced dance rhythms. Performers move between rap and song while collaborations and online releases connect local styles to a wider audience.

items.name: Dubsteppe
items.lineage: Dubsteppe is a discovery field connecting Russian-language dance remixes, club-pop and house-oriented producers with adjacent international collaborations. Vocal hooks move between radio edits, extended club versions and DJ programmes, linking popular-song repertoire to electronic dance floors.
items.description: Recognizable vocal refrains and electronic bass-and-drum patterns anchor melodic club arrangements. Remixes recast familiar songs for continuous dance programmes, with pop accessibility and house-derived rhythmic momentum connecting a varied producer network.

items.name: Corridos Adictivos
items.lineage: Corridos Adictivos gathers contemporary regional Mexican corrido groups around narrative singing and compact instrumental accompaniment. Requinto lines, recurring bass patterns and brass or accordion colors carry stories of local identity, personal histories and contested power, alongside romantic repertoire circulating through the same performers.
items.description: Direct narrative vocals alternate with melodic string figures over a steady low pulse. Small ensembles can combine two singers, requinto, tololoche and charcheta, while the wider repertoire also circulates through norteño and banda arrangements.

items.name: Classic Bangla Pop
items.lineage: Bengali popular-song listening connects established singers, band songwriters and later pop voices across Bangladesh and West Bengal. Recordings, radio, concerts and acoustic reinterpretations keep familiar songs in circulation across generations.
items.description: Melodic Bengali singing and recognizable song forms connect ballads, band pop and acoustic interpretations. The classic-pop discovery repertoire spans several generations and includes both Bangladesh and West Bengal; its intimate voice-and-guitar branch sits alongside fuller studio arrangements.

items.name: Classic Thai Pop
items.lineage: Thailand’s familiar pop repertoire circulates through singers, string bands, recorded hits and later reinterpretations. Romantic melody and memorable refrains connect older urban-pop performers with subsequent generations of listeners and musicians.
items.description: Melodic Thai popular songs combine lyrical refrains with ballad and dance-song forms. Piano covers and teaching arrangements give familiar repertoire an instrumental setting, alongside the sung band and studio versions that remain central to the field.
exemplars: เพชร โอสถานุเคราะห์

items.name: Kinnauri Pop
items.lineage: Kinnauri popular song brings regional-language singing into recorded dance songs, contemporary arrangements and local digital releases. Singers and producers from the Kinnaur repertoire circulate alongside wider Himachali and Pahadi popular music.
items.description: Regional melodies and sung refrains meet contemporary programmed accompaniment. The field includes folk-oriented songs, dance releases and electronic crossovers; this representative sung-and-programmed branch retains the voice while leaving the backing generator unspecified.

items.name: Speed Up Türkçe
items.lineage: Speed Up Türkçe gathers accelerated versions of Turkish-language recordings circulated through streaming releases and online remix culture. Rappers, singers and remix producers retain recognizable phrases while changing the temporal scale of the recorded song.
items.description: Recorded vocal phrases and their produced accompaniment move together through a brisker rendition. Continuous hooks connect the transformation to the source song, while the amount of acceleration and treatment of pitch vary between releases.

items.name: Zambian Pop
items.lineage: Zambian pop connects local songwriting, studio producers and radio audiences with wider African popular music. Its broad repertoire includes melodic R&B and dance-oriented songs alongside collaborations with rap, gospel and regional bands.
items.description: Melodic singing and recurring choruses sit over produced beats and prominent low bass. Language, rhythmic feel and studio texture vary among artists, linking local audiences with contemporary African pop and R&B.

items.name: Classic Kollywood
items.lineage: Classic Kollywood gathers familiar Tamil-language film songs and the playback voices and composers who keep them in circulation. Memorable melodic refrains, expressive diction and contrasting verse sections link romantic songs, dance numbers and classical-inflected compositions across film generations.
items.description: Playback singing places the melody and Tamil text at the center, with orchestral, band and electronic arrangements varying across the repertoire. Vocal renditions also carry these songs into lessons and informal performance, where phrasing, breath and small melodic ornaments shape a familiar tune.

items.name: Música Sinaloense
items.lineage: Música Sinaloense gathers popular repertoires associated with Sinaloa, including corridos, romantic song, norteño and guitar-led regional groups alongside the state’s celebrated wind bands. Contemporary artists connect local song traditions with pop-facing melodies and circulated recordings.
items.description: Expressive singing and recurring refrains carry narratives and romantic themes. Guitar rhythm and answering accordion phrases form one small-group setting, while brass bands and other string-led ensembles supply contrasting textures across the wider regional repertoire.

items.name: Nova Música Paulista
items.lineage: Nova música paulista connects contemporary São Paulo songwriting with independent musical networks and a wide range of Brazilian and international influences. Artists move between intimate song, samba-related rhythms, pop, jazz, experimental textures and electronic production, sustaining a varied metropolitan scene.
items.description: Expressive singing and distinctive songwriting link arrangements of many sizes. In the voice-and-guitar branch, ringing chords and melodic accompaniment leave room for lyrical detail, flexible phrasing and contrasts between reflective passages and rhythmic refrains.

items.name: Modern Alternative Pop
items.lineage: Modern alternative pop brings intimate songwriting together with independent acoustic and electronic production. Artists move between fragile piano-led songs and more layered arrangements, drawing on indie rock, ambient electronics and contemporary popular-song forms.
items.description: Soft piano and restrained singing can expose the melody and emotional detail of a song. Other arrangements expand the same intimate writing through synthesizers, bass, programmed beats and layered vocal harmonies.

items.name: Vintage Dutch Pop
items.lineage: Vintage Dutch pop gathers older popular songs, cabaret melodies and light-entertainment repertoire kept alive through records, songbooks and new performances. Dutch-language storytelling and memorable refrains sit alongside international song adaptations and a range of historical band and orchestral sounds.
items.description: Older Dutch popular songs combine clear melodies and narrative lyrics with intimate accompaniment or fuller entertainment-band settings. Piano arrangements preserve their melodic warmth and the phrasing of familiar refrains.

items.name: Korean Hyperpop
items.lineage: Korean hyperpop grows through independent online production, Seoul and Busan artist networks, and cross-border East Asian collaborations. Song and rap voices meet digitally manipulated backing, combining pop immediacy with noisy, playful or dreamlike electronic textures.
items.description: Korean and English hooks, rap delivery and digitally shaped production connect independent Korean artists with international online pop networks. Artist-curated radio programmes place their own recordings beside cloud rap, electronic club music and other influences.

items.name: Khandeshi Pop
items.lineage: Khandeshi pop brings Ahirani and Khandeshi-language songs into contemporary regional recording and video circulation. Singers and producers combine local melodic and lyrical expression with studio programming, duets and dance-oriented refrains.
items.description: Sung regional refrains and duet exchanges meet programmed accompaniment. Repeating melodic hooks support affectionate, celebratory and narrative songs; electronic production connects the repertoire with the wider regional popular-music field.

items.name: Spanish Invasion
