items.lineage: Spanish Invasion gathers Spain’s1960s beat and early pop-rock groups. British and American records helped shape a local guitar-band sound, while Spanish lyrics, vocal harmonies and original songwriting connected the new music to domestic youth audiences.
items.description: Clear guitar chords, melodic bass and a regular drum backbeat frame compact songs and shared vocal harmonies. Bright hooks and concise arrangements connect beat-group influences with Spanish popular-song phrasing.

items.name: Dangdut Remix
items.lineage: Indonesian dance-remix practice reshaping dangdut recordings through digital editing, rhythmic replacement and sampled cross-genre additions. It developed within the cassette and studio-production economy of the 1990s and continues in electronic dance circulation.
items.description: Dangdut melodies and ornamented singing are placed over reworked electronic dance rhythms. Producers cut and layer recorded fragments, replace or reinforce percussion, and add rhythmic calls, rap or other borrowed textures. The remix is a production practice with varied grooves rather than one fixed drum pattern or exclusively live band format.

items.name: Indonesian Hyperpop
items.lineage: Indonesian hyperpop connects online pop production with Jakarta performance networks and Southeast Asian electronic collaborations. Sung hooks, rap, guitar textures and processed club sounds meet playful digital aesthetics and hardcore-rave energy.
items.description: Digitally shaped hooks and elastic electronic rhythms connect Indonesian pop makers with international hyperpop and rave communities. Artist-curated programmes place local recordings alongside international remixes, rap and harder club music.

items.name: Indie Fuzzpop
items.lineage: Indie fuzzpop brings together small-label guitar-pop and home-recording communities, with melodic songwriting that can range from rough-edged bands to soft electronic textures. Its listening cohort overlaps twee pop, indie pop and noise pop, linking acts such as The Just Joans and Tiny Fireflies.
items.description: Sung melodies, electric guitar, bass, drums and keyboard figures support intimate songs with recurring hooks. Light, direct arrangements can sit beside dry humour, wistful stories and more abrasive or electronically coloured recordings.

items.name: Japanese Hyperpop
items.lineage: Japanese hyperpop connects online pop production, underground rap and experimental electronic scenes. Digitally altered melodies, abrupt textures and internet-mediated collaborations circulate through recordings, clubs and curated radio programmes.
items.description: Sung and rapped hooks meet elastic digital production and rapidly changing textures. The field overlaps digicore and underground rap, with curated programmes bringing these recordings into a shared listening setting.

items.name: Kavkaz
items.lineage: Kavkaz brings regional Caucasian popular-song repertoires into recorded releases, concerts and broadcast appearances. Singers combine local languages and Russian-language material, with love songs, homeland themes and duet exchanges alongside changing studio arrangements.
items.description: Melodic solo and duet singing carries regional words and familiar refrains. Unaccompanied appearances expose the paired voices directly, while other releases use varied studio accompaniment.

items.name: Pinoy city pop
items.lineage: Filipino city pop connects the renewed international interest in Japanese city pop with Manila Sound, indie songwriting and local pop audiences. Contemporary bands draw on polished jazz-pop harmony, disco-funk rhythm and the melodic warmth of earlier Filipino popular music.
items.description: Clean guitar figures, rounded bass lines, keyboard chords and a steady kit groove support smooth, tuneful singing. Romantic songwriting and a buoyant retro-modern sound link the Filipino scene to the wider city-pop revival while retaining its own language and musical references.

items.name: Indian Lo-Fi
items.lineage: Indian lo-fi connects independent electronic producers with local melodic traditions and intimate online listening. Film-vocal reworkings coexist with flute-led instrumental experiments and deliberately imperfect rhythmic textures.
items.description: Breathy flute melodies and soft beats share space with electronically shaped environmental textures. This instrumental branch combines sustained melodic phrasing with a relaxed, imperfect production surface; vocal remixes remain another important part of the wider field.

items.name: Balkan drill
items.lineage: Balkan drill adapts drill production to regional rap networks across southeastern Europe. Crni Cerak, Rasta and Banfica helped bring its hard beats and local-language street narratives to clubs, festivals and streaming releases. It overlaps Balkan trap while emphasizing drill-oriented rhythm and delivery.
items.description: Clipped rhythmic verses and emphatic hooks sit over heavy pitched bass, brisk hi-hat figures and sharply placed percussion. Repeating sampled melodic phrases add contrast, drawing on a wide range of piano, string, choir and flute colors.

items.name: Re:techno
items.lineage: Re:techno connects club-oriented producers and DJs working across techno, hardgroove and loop-led dance music. Repeated rhythmic figures and percussion-driven tracks support extended sets and shifting combinations on the dance floor.
items.description: Persistent beats and short repeating figures build momentum through layered transitions and changes of texture. DJ programmes move across harder, groove-focused and more spacious techno material.

items.name: Música Potosina
items.lineage: Música potosina gathers regional popular-music communities associated with San Luis Potosí. Norteño conjuntos and sax-led groups circulate corridos, romantic songs and dance repertoire alongside local cumbia projects, sustained by recordings, community celebrations and audiences across Mexico and the United States.
items.description: Sung verses and refrains move over interlocking bass, strummed chords and dance rhythms. Accordion and saxophone exchange melodic figures in the norteño-sax branch, while other groups explore romantic and tropical sounds. The regional community shares these practices with neighboring Mexican scenes.

items.name: Krajiška muzika
items.lineage: Krajiška muzika develops regional Krajina singing into accompanied popular folk song. Lead and supporting voices retain close harmonic relationships, while accordion and later rhythm sections or local string instruments connect older communal singing to recorded and festive performance.
items.description: A leading melody is answered or supported by other singers in thirds and held tones. Accordion reinforces the tune and its rhythmic cadence; familiar melodic patterns carry renewed texts, with ensemble texture varying across places and generations.

items.name: Rhythm and Boogie
items.lineage: Rhythm and boogie gathers early rock-and-roll and rockabilly songs with driving rhythms and direct vocal hooks. Regional recording scenes and later reissues keep this dance-oriented repertoire in circulation alongside country, blues and rhythm-and-blues influences.
items.description: An accompanied sung lead rides a compact guitar, bass and drum rhythm section. Repeated figures, firm backbeats and concise refrains give the songs their forward motion, while instrumental breaks add contrasting melodic lines.

items.name: Modern Power Pop
items.lineage: Modern power pop sustains hook-led guitar songwriting through independent bands, small labels and contemporary recording communities. Ringing guitars and vocal harmonies connect earlier beat and power-pop influences with college-rock and present-day indie production.
items.description: Bright guitar figures, melodic bass and a firm drum backbeat support compact songs and shared vocal hooks. Clear chord changes and concise refrains anchor the band sound, while individual records may add keyboards, percussion and other studio colours.

items.name: Pop Nacional Antigas
items.lineage: Pop nacional antigas revisits earlier Brazilian popular-song repertories across romantic pop, brega, soul and MPB. Radio hits and remembered refrains circulate through retrospective listening, reissues and contemporary performances that renew familiar songs.
items.description: Direct sung melodies and memorable refrains carry romantic stories and familiar Brazilian pop repertoire. Voice-and-piano recitals offer an intimate branch, alongside the field’s fuller band, orchestral and studio productions.

items.name: Radio symphony
items.lineage: Radio symphony orchestras developed as broadcaster-maintained ensembles, sustaining orchestral concerts, recordings and radio commissions. Their repertoire ranges across historical concert music and contemporary composition.
items.description: Radio symphony joins the full orchestral tradition with the programming and recording work of broadcast institutions. Performances range from large string-and-wind orchestras to chamber and wind ensembles, with repertoire-specific scoring and concert-hall ensemble balance.

items.name: Meenawati
items.lineage: Meenawati song circulates through Meena communities in eastern Rajasthan, linking local storytelling and devotional singing with recorded popular music. Community gatherings and regional digital releases carry these songs into dance and DJ-remix settings.
items.description: Regional sung storytelling and expressive refrains coexist with contemporary recorded dance arrangements. DJ remixes place the songs alongside other Rajasthani repertoire, while community performances also retain live singing and musicians.

items.name: Nu Age
items.lineage: Nu Age is a contemporary ambient discovery field connecting electroacoustic composition, processed instrumental sound and spacious electronic textures. Its artists overlap organic ambient, modern classical and drone networks.
items.description: Quiet piano miniatures and electroacoustic soundscapes share this contemporary ambient listening field. Simple chordal figures, sustained resonance and unhurried melodic lines form one intimate branch, alongside the sampled textures and processed strings of larger arrangements.

items.name: Música Colimense
items.lineage: Música Colimense brings together popular and traditional music circulating in Colima, including regional bands, mariachi, sierreño groups and romantic rondallas. Municipal and university ensembles connect public celebrations, serenades and recorded regional repertoires.
items.description: In its romantic rondalla branch, blended singing rests on strummed guitars and a plucked bass foundation, while requinto lines answer the melody. Boleros, ballads and bolero ranchero connect local serenades with wider Mexican and Latin American song.
exemplars: Rondalla del H. Ayuntamiento de Colima

items.name: Música Morelense
items.lineage: Música Morelense connects regional popular traditions in Morelos, including wind bands, corrido singers, local songwriters, string ensembles and contemporary regional-Mexican groups. Village celebrations, historical narratives and songs of local identity coexist with commercial dance and romantic repertoire.
items.description: Regional narratives and memorable melodies circulate through solo song, small string groups and festive wind bands. The corrido branch pairs a clearly projected sung story with rhythmic guitar accompaniment, while other local practices use larger ensembles and dance rhythms.

items.name: Musique Mariage Algérien
items.lineage: Algerian wedding music brings regional song traditions into celebrations, from Chaâbi and Hawzi to Kabyle, Chaoui and contemporary popular repertories. Performers adapt ensemble size and repertoire to families and different stages of the festivities.
items.description: A singing lead moves through celebratory melodies with piano accompaniment, plucked qanun responses and ringing frame-drum rhythm. The balance of intimate song and lively dance changes with the repertoire, and larger ensembles can add further melodic instruments.

items.name: Indiecoustica
items.lineage: Indiecoustica connects melodic independent singer-songwriters across acoustic pop, piano pop and understated band arrangements. Personal storytelling and approachable melodies circulate through artist-made recordings, intimate performances and listening playlists.
items.description: A prominent singing voice carries personal songs over clear guitar chords, keyboard harmony and a compact bass-and-drum pulse. Solo acoustic renditions and fuller bands coexist within the listening field.

items.name: Plugg Français
items.lineage: French plugg grew through SoundCloud exchanges among rappers and producers drawing on Atlanta plugg and related Southern rap. Bordeaux producers Bricksy & 3G describe a network connecting French collaborators with Montréal and American scenes, joining spacious melodies to individually shaped rhythms.
items.description: Rhythmic vocal lines sit among repeating keyboard figures, spacious chords and sampled rhythmic layers. Melodic color and the placement of small rhythmic details let rappers work around the beat without requiring a single flow or vocal treatment.

items.name: Sirmauri Pop
items.lineage: Sirmauri pop brings the songs and dance repertories of Himachal Pradesh’s Sirmaur region into contemporary recording and digital circulation. Harul and nati material coexist with new popular songs, while studio producers offer regional rhythm loops for modern arrangements.
items.description: Regional-language singing carries memorable melodic lines over a repeating dance pulse. Contemporary studio arrangements can pair a clear lead voice with sampled dholak rhythms, while other performers retain larger folk or amplified ensembles.

items.name: Gospel Antigas
items.lineage: Gospel antigas gathers older Brazilian evangelical songs and hymns that remain in church, family and recorded repertories. Singers and congregations revisit these songs across changing production styles, with acoustic teaching and devotional performance continuing alongside larger arrangements.
items.description: Older Brazilian evangelical songs remain familiar through worship, recordings and domestic music making. Instrumental piano arrangements carry hymn melodies and supportive harmony alongside the field’s many sung and ensemble renditions.

items.name: Philly Drill
items.lineage: Philly drill developed within Philadelphia’s contemporary rap community through local MC networks and producers working both in the city and abroad. Sparse, ominous beats and forceful vocal delivery connect it to drill while choral and cinematic sampling give parts of the scene a distinctive atmosphere.
items.description: Direct rap delivery meets spare programmed percussion, deep 808 bass and ominous sampled textures. Choral, operatic and cinematic fragments can sustain a dark backdrop, while the performers’ local references and cadence keep the music grounded in Philadelphia rap.

items.name: Cumbia
items.lineage: Cumbia grew from Colombia’s Caribbean musical traditions into a transnational Latin American dance repertoire. Recordings, radio, touring orchestras and migrant audiences carried it across borders, where local communities reshaped its rhythms, instrumentation and social meanings.
items.description: Repeating bass and percussion patterns support sung refrains and answering instrumental phrases. Dance-orchestra arrangements combine keyboards and brass, while guitar-led, accordion-led and electronic approaches give the wider repertoire distinct regional textures.

items.name: Japanese Buddhist chant
items.lineage: Japanese Buddhist chant encompasses the vocal practices of Japan’s Buddhist schools and lay communities. Transmitted from continental Asia and developed through distinct temple lineages, it ranges from elaborate shōmyō to syllabic sutra recitation, ceremonial narratives and devotional hymns. Clergy and lay practitioners preserve these traditions through ritual, instruction and communal singing.
items.description: Voices carry sacred texts through sustained melodic phrases or measured syllabic recitation. Some rituals use bells, bowls, gongs and cymbals as signals, while vocal passages place the sound and meaning of the text at the centre of the practice.
exemplars: Shōmyō, sutra recitation, kōshiki and goeika traditions

items.name: Vintage Italian Soundtrack
items.lineage: Vintage Italian soundtrack music draws on the film and studio archives of the 1960s–80s, where jazz, orchestral writing, pop, funk and psychedelic textures served comedy, crime, horror and other screen genres. Reissue and licensing communities around CAM Sugar and Sonor Music Editions have renewed circulation of this repertoire. Alongside orchestral scores, studio groups such as I Marc 4 supplied compact, groove-led themes built from guitar, organ, bass and drums.
items.description: Short thematic cues move between memorable melody, rhythmic accompaniment and contrasting instrumental colours. Electric organ, guitar and a bass-and-drum rhythm section support the jazz-funk studio-combo strand, while the wider archival field also includes orchestral, electronic and vocal film music.

items.name: Samba Moderno
items.lineage: Samba moderno follows the contemporary Rio singer-composer network nurtured by Lapa venues, Clube Renascença, Cacique de Ramos and projects such as Samba Social Clube and Festa da Raça. Artists including João Martins, Inácio Rios and Nego Álvaro carry older samba traditions into new compositions, collaborations and independent careers.
items.description: Melodic singing and shared refrains interlock with compact cavaquinho or banjo accompaniment, guitar and layered hand percussion. New songs about affection, everyday life and social experience circulate between neighborhood rodas, studio releases and concert stages, retaining the rhythmic conversation of samba while developing individual poetic voices.

items.name: Deep Hardtechno
items.lineage: Deep hardtechno is a discovery label connecting hardtechno and schranz producers and their DJ circuits. Forceful percussion, repeated rhythmic material and driving electronic textures link releases, remixes and extended club sets.
items.description: Dense rhythmic pressure and repeated selections give the music a continuous forward motion. DJs combine recordings and transitions into longer performances; melody and vocal material vary across the repertoire.

items.name: Electropop
items.lineage: Electropop brings electronic production into melodic popular songwriting. Its overlapping synthpop and dance-pop networks connect synthesizer-led bands with solo singers, producers and club remixes. Contemporary artists carry these practices through albums, electronic-music festivals and digital discovery playlists.
items.description: Sung melodies and recurring hooks sit over sequenced rhythmic foundations and layered synthesizers. Live keyboard parts can interact with software sequences, while drum machines articulate a regular pulse. Studio production and rearranged live versions connect song-focused listening with dance-floor energy.

items.name: Speedrun
items.lineage: Speedrun is a discovery field linking energetic internet electronic music with independent games and online creator communities. Its repertoire includes Waterflame, Creo and Dimrain47, spanning melodic synthesis, sample-based arrangement and rhythm-led production rather than one fixed tempo or sound chip.
items.description: Programmed sample layers carry rhythmic and pitched figures beneath clear synthetic melodies. Breakbeat motion, contrasting sections and game-oriented melodic hooks coexist with quieter pieces; the label does not imply that every track accompanies a timed run.

items.name: Kashmiri hip hop
items.lineage: Kashmiri hip hop connects rappers, producers and audiences in Kashmir and its diaspora. Artists such as MC Kash, Ahmer, SOS and their collaborators have developed a regional scene using Kashmiri, Urdu and other languages, with local experience and cultural memory shaping the writing.
items.description: Rhythmic verses and changing flows meet sampled beats and repeated melodic fragments. Folk recordings and local poetic references can enter the production, while other songs draw on different instrumental and vocal approaches.

items.name: Sesotho Pop
items.lineage: Sesotho popular music circulates across South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana, bringing Sesotho-language song into soul, township-pop and contemporary studio settings. Melodic singing and accessible recurring song forms coexist with newer rap and dance crossovers.
items.description: A sung lead carries the text and tune over a repeating popular-song accompaniment. Performances range from amplified bands to singers using recorded backing tracks; this arrangement presents the latter branch with clear melodic phrasing and a steady groove.

items.name: Vietnamese Pop
items.lineage: Vietnamese popular song connects domestic and overseas recording, performance and listening communities. Romantic melodies and familiar song repertories circulate through singers, amplified ensembles and instrumental reinterpretations, including piano arrangements of Trịnh Công Sơn’s songs.
items.description: Melody and supportive harmony carry a familiar popular-song repertory through lyrical phrases and recurring sections. A solo-piano rendition brings the tune into the foreground, alongside the field’s sung ballads, band arrangements and studio productions.

items.name: Griot
items.lineage: Griots sustain West African oral-history, praise and musical traditions through inherited professional knowledge. Regional practices include Mandé jali lineages and other singer-historian traditions, combining remembered genealogies and narratives with sung praise and instrumental accompaniment.
items.description: Narrative delivery alternates with sung praise and instrumental interludes. Voice, phrasing and accompaniment vary by regional lineage and occasion; a Mandinka recital branch pairs a single jali narrator-singer with a small calabash-resonated wooden-key balafon.

items.name: Instrumental acoustic guitar
items.lineage: Instrumental acoustic guitar brings melody, harmony and rhythmic movement into guitar-led compositions without sung text. Modern fingerstyle communities connect folk, jazz, popular and classical influences, with labels such as Candyrat supporting an international network of composers and performers.
items.description: Independent bass notes, ringing chords and melodic lines share the instrument. Fingerpicked patterns, changes of register and dynamic accents shape pieces that range from reflective miniatures to rhythmically vigorous concert music.

items.name: Música Neoleonesa
items.lineage: Música neoleonesa encompasses the traditional repertories of Nuevo León, shaped by local social life and musical circulation across northeastern Mexico and Texas. Narrative romances, songs and dances coexist within a regional history whose accordion traditions became widely known through records and migration.
items.description: Narrative singing can be shared by two voices over accordion melody and the resonant strumming of bajo sexto. The wider repertory also includes dance ensembles and other instrumental combinations; this intimate song setting emphasizes clear words, alternating phrases and a steady accompaniment.

items.name: Indie Việt
items.lineage: Indie Việt connects Vietnamese independent songwriters and bands through small venues, self-released recordings and online audiences. Acoustic songwriting and guitar-band arrangements sit alongside electronic and experimental approaches, with artists building their own relationships with listeners.
items.description: Personal melodic lines and direct lyrics can be presented with a single guitar or expanded into layered band arrangements. The intimate songwriting branch pairs a clear sung lead with picked guitar figures, leaving space around the words and harmonic changes.

items.name: Vintage Swoon
items.lineage: Vintage swoon gathers mid-century romantic teen-pop singers and lesser-known records alongside early rock-and-roll performers. Clear melodic leads, vocal harmonies and compact song forms connect intimate ballads with brighter dance-band presentations.
items.description: A melodic lead and backing voices carry short, memorable phrases over guitar, piano and a steady drum pulse. This compact band treatment represents the livelier side of a listening field that also includes gently arranged romantic songs.

items.name: Corridos Cristianos
items.lineage: Christian corrido performers adapt regional Mexican ballad and contemporary tumbado idioms to testimony, prayer and praise. The field includes original devotional songs and religious adaptations, circulating through community performance and popular recording networks.
items.description: Direct sung messages of faith ride the repeated chord patterns and melodic phrasing of regional Mexican song. This intimate branch uses voice and strummed guitar; requinto-led groups, bass support and larger regional ensembles belong to other branches.

items.name: Concurso de Talentos Argentino
items.lineage: Argentine televised singing competitions bring emerging performers together through auditions, coaching, live rounds and recorded releases. Their repertoire crosses popular song, rock and regional traditions, with contestants developing personal versions of familiar material.
items.description: The singer leads a recognizable melody while accompaniment supports a personal interpretation. An intimate voice-and-guitar arrangement is one established audition branch; ensemble-backed songs and duets extend the wider competition repertoire.

items.name: Modern Country Pop
items.lineage: Modern country pop connects narrative country songwriting with accessible pop hooks and contemporary recording. Songwriters move between intimate acoustic performance and fuller studio arrangements, retaining clear vocal stories while drawing on both country and pop influences.
items.description: Conversational sung verses and memorable refrains frame personal stories. Strummed acoustic chords offer a direct solo-performance setting, while the broader field also embraces bands, layered vocals and programmed pop production.

items.name: New Wave Pop
items.lineage: New wave pop gathers hook-led songwriting associated with new wave and its wider pop audience. Distinctive vocal personalities, guitar figures, synthesizers and danceable rhythms connect late-twentieth-century recordings with later live reinterpretations.
items.description: Memorable vocal lines and concise refrains sit alongside sharply characterized guitar or keyboard textures. Acoustic reinterpretations bring ensemble harmonies and rhythmic guitar accompaniment forward, sometimes alternating songs with spoken recollections.

items.name: Kleine Hörspiel
items.lineage: German-language children’s audio-drama adaptations bring film and family-story characters into recorded listening. Publishers circulate edited dialogue, narration, familiar music and sound effects through albums, audio cards and streaming libraries.
items.description: Contrasting character voices and narration lead the story, with pauses and edits shaping dramatic pace. Recorded music and effects establish scenes and connect dialogue. Familiar family-film adaptations form a prominent part of the listening repertoire.

items.name: Malayalam Madh
items.lineage: Malayalam madh is a praise-song field in Kerala Muslim musical life, especially devotional address to the Prophet. Local-language texts circulate through community gatherings, religious institutions, song collections and contemporary recordings, alongside Arabic and other regional-language praise.
items.description: A leading voice and answering group carry devotional phrases over hand-played frame-drum rhythm. Repeated praise and coordinated accents support communal participation; unaccompanied singing and elaborately produced recordings provide other settings for the same devotional field.

items.name: Marċi Brijużi
items.lineage: Maltese festive marches circulate through local band societies and village feasts in Malta and Gozo. Composers shape buoyant tonal melodies into contrasting sections, often culminating in a trio, while clubs teach successive generations of wind and percussion players.
items.description: Bright upper clarinets and rounded lower winds alternate melodic statements over brass harmony and a steady drum-and-cymbal pulse. Contrasting strains and trio sections carry the celebratory motion of local festa processions.

items.name: World
items.lineage: World music became a shared record-industry category in1987, bringing international and roots recordings together for shops, press and audiences. Its repertoire spans regional traditional practices, contemporary popular styles and cross-cultural collaborations.
items.description: The field encompasses many musical languages and ensembles rather than one universal rhythm or instrumentation. Solo kora improvisation is one established strand alongside vocal, dance and ensemble traditions from many regions.

items.name: Manipuri Pop
items.lineage: Manipuri pop connects contemporary songwriting, music videos and regional film playback in Manipur. Singers draw on local melodic traditions while working with guitars, studio arrangements and popular-song forms. Acoustic singing and fuller produced songs coexist within the field.
items.description: A melodic sung line moves over ringing guitar chords in an intimate acoustic branch. Short ornamental note groups and repeated song sections give the voice room to shape the lyric; larger studio arrangements extend the same repertoire into film and popular recordings.

items.name: Deathgrass
items.lineage: Deathgrass is a discovery label for an underground roots-music network crossing punk, old-time string bands and rough-edged country. Its artist corpus includes Urban Pioneers, Filthy Still and Mikey Classic, bringing acoustic picking, fiddle and earthy vocals into the orbit of punk and alternative Americana.
items.description: Clawhammer banjo and fiddle carry quick melodic figures while slapped upright bass adds a percussive pulse. Sung lines and guitar chords connect the string-band texture to contemporary roots songwriting, with energetic performance shared across old-time, country and punk audiences.

items.name: Venda Pop
items.lineage: Venda popular music joins Tshivenda song and dance traditions with contemporary band and recorded-pop arrangements. Malende-derived melodic contours, recurring rhythmic figures and exchanges between a lead singer and responding voices remain important alongside newer folk-pop and electronic directions.
items.description: A lead melody alternates with group responses above interlocking guitar and bass figures. Kick and hi-hat patterns carry a recurring dance pulse, adapting malende rhythmic relationships to a compact popular band.

items.name: Chicago Mexican
items.lineage: Chicago Mexican music grows through regional-Mexican bands, immigrant audiences and local dance venues. Norteño, cumbia, corrido and other Mexican repertories circulate through recordings, collaborations and live celebrations in the city’s musical community.
items.description: Lead and supporting vocals exchange short phrases over accordion melodies and the ringing chord pulse of bajo quinto. Electric bass and drums anchor this compact norteño-facing dance-band branch within a wider Chicago scene that also includes brass bands and other regional-Mexican styles.

items.name: Tavern
items.lineage: Tavern gathers convivial historical-folk listening and performance, bringing Celtic tune arrangements together with medieval and Renaissance-inspired music. Contemporary performers range from intimate solo instrumentalists to theatrical dance ensembles.
items.description: Interwoven melody, bass and inner voices give the solo fingerstyle-guitar branch a lilting dance pulse. Reels, jigs and reflective tunes share the broader field with ensemble dances and historical-folk reinterpretations.

items.name: Pop Catracho
items.lineage: Honduran popular-song performers connect locally rooted songwriting with tropical rhythms and wider Latin pop. Acoustic cantautores share audiences and recording networks with dance-oriented and urban acts.
items.description: Memorable sung phrases and recurring refrains lead the music. This acoustic branch pairs a direct melodic voice with ringing guitar chords, leaving space for the lyric; other branches use fuller bands, tropical percussion or electronic production.

items.name: Çerkes Müzikleri
items.lineage: Çerkes müzikleri in the Turkish diaspora connects North Caucasian song and dance repertories across Adyghe, Abaza and neighboring communities. Oral narratives, exile laments and dance melodies circulate through community performance and new multilingual stage arrangements.
items.description: A sung narrative unfolds against plucked strings and polyphonic responses. Flute and free reeds extend the melodic colour, while percussion can shape a gradually intensifying dance pulse. Contemporary arrangements retain the repertory’s links to migration, memory and community gatherings.

items.name: funktronica
items.lineage: Funktronica brings funk grooves into electronic and independent pop production. Synthesizer bass, programmed rhythm, guitar and processed vocals can interact in compact arrangements, alongside more instrumental and dance-oriented recordings.
items.description: Electronic bass and a repeating drum pulse support syncopated guitar and effected singing. Sparse arrangements can leave the groove exposed, while unusual vocal treatments and handmade electronic sounds connect funk phrasing with experimental pop.

items.name: Spacewave
items.lineage: Spacewave develops the cosmic and science-fiction strand of contemporary synth music. Producers connect retro electronic timbres with imagined voyages, orbital environments and cinematic storytelling, working across rhythmic synthwave and more atmospheric electronic settings.
items.description: Analog and digital synthesizer melodies unfold above electronic pulses, with film samples adding narrative fragments in some productions. A melodic, rhythm-bearing studio branch sits alongside spacious and ambient approaches.

items.name: Dark Black Metal
items.lineage: Dark black metal is a practitioner-used description for black metal that emphasizes bleak atmosphere, dissonant melody and slower, doom-influenced passages. Forgotten Tomb used the related description Depressive Dark Black Metal while developing music that also drew on darkwave and later expanded toward sludge and heavier rock.
items.description: Arpeggiated guitar figures and uneasy melodic intervals alternate with heavier riffing, bass and measured drum patterns. Harsh vocals and sustained dark textures carry a mournful character, with changes of weight and pace rather than uninterrupted blast-beat intensity.

items.name: Indonesian Lo-fi Pop
items.lineage: Indonesian lo-fi pop connects intimate independent pop with acoustic songwriting and online home-recording culture. Soft vocals, small-scale arrangements and personal interpretations circulate alongside more layered studio productions, including work by Indonesian artists abroad.
items.description: A mellow lead melody is supported by softly fingerpicked acoustic guitar. The intimate acoustic branch emphasizes lyrical phrasing and space around the voice; the wider discovery field also includes fuller electronic and band arrangements.

items.name: Classic Sierreño
items.lineage: Classic sierreño gathers established regional Mexican song repertoires and the groups that carry them forward. Compact guitar ensembles and accordion-led variants support corridos, romantic songs and dance repertories, connecting older styles with new performances.
items.description: Sung lines sit over interlocking chordal and melodic figures, with bass defining the recurring pulse. An accordion-led trio provides one longstanding branch; guitar duets and other small ensembles offer contrasting textures within the repertoire.

items.name: Deep Norteño
items.lineage: Deep Norteño gathers a deeper discovery cohort of norteño conjuntos from northern Mexico and cross-border communities. Accordion, bajo sexto and dance-band rhythm sections support songs, corridos, polkas, waltzes and cumbias, with saxophone prominent in the Ojinaga-associated branch.
items.description: Sung melodies meet accordion phrases and saxophone countermelodies above strummed bajo sexto, electric bass and drums. Dance rhythms and familiar romantic or narrative repertoire connect small-band performance with regional venues and cross-border recordings.

items.name: Vintage Western
items.lineage: Vintage Western gathers archival country-and-western recordings across early rural song, hillbilly blues, western swing and related regional styles. Radio and commercial discs circulated vocal duets, dance bands and small acoustic groups whose repertoires crossed ballads, comic songs and blues.
items.description: A small-group song branch places two voices over ringing guitar chords, with harmonica answering the sung line. Other recordings in the field use larger swinging ensembles, steel guitars or regional dance instrumentation; the historical repertoire extends beyond cowboy-themed lyrics alone.

items.name: Forró Manauara
items.lineage: Forró manauara grew through Manaus dance venues and local bands, combining northeastern forró with Amazonian popular-music circuits. From the1990s onward, musicians and DJs reworked electronic-band styles into a regional scene; later forró de galeral and forró-funk brought new audiences, slang and club influences.
items.description: Singing rides a firm dance pulse, with accordion figures, electric guitar and bass, drumkit and zabumba. Keyboard players shape much of the modern band texture, adding effects, sampled accents and cut-up voices. Repertoires move between xote, established forró songs and newer funk-influenced material within the city’s active dance circuit.

items.name: Narodnozabavna
items.lineage: Narodnozabavna is Slovenian popular folk music heard at dances, weddings, family celebrations and festivals at home and across the diaspora. Since the mid-twentieth century, Avsenik-style wind ensembles and the accordion-led Slak tradition have shaped its polkas, waltzes and songs.
items.description: Accordion melody and chordal accompaniment meet guitar rhythm, a moving bass foundation and ensemble singing. Repeating dance strains and alternating verses, refrains and instrumental passages carry a lively communal repertoire.

items.name: Cryptic Black Metal
items.lineage: Cryptic black metal is a practitioner-used description for occult and enigmatic strains of extreme black metal. Sar Isatum combines this vocabulary with ethereal and symphonic ambitions, drawing atmosphere from ominous riffing and an extreme guitar-band foundation.
items.description: Tremolo-picked distorted guitars, driven bass and rapid percussion support harsh vocals and dark, expansive moods. Arrangements may use keyboards and symphonic layers, while a core guitar-band branch preserves the same cryptic atmosphere through riffs and dynamics.

items.name: Bleakgaze
items.lineage: Bleakgaze gathers introspective black-metal and atmospheric guitar music around artists including Thy Light, ColdWorld and Woods of Desolation. Its overlapping repertoire joins anguished vocals and heavy guitar textures with extended melody, melancholy and changes in instrumental density.
items.description: Sustained guitar textures and repeated melodic figures meet bass, drums and harsh, emotionally direct singing. Spacious passages and shifts in weight make room for reflective atmosphere alongside black-metal intensity.

items.name: Pop Minang (Minangkabau-language pop)
items.lineage: Popular song in the Minangkabau language that grew from post-independence Minang orchestras in Jakarta and Padang into a large regional cassette and later VCD industry centred on Padang. Arrangements set Minang verse over a pop band of guitar, bass, drums and keyboard, often adding the colour of talempong kettle gongs (the canang card stands in) and the saluang bamboo flute (the generic bamboo-flute card stands in).
items.description: Sentimental and dance-tempo songs in which an ornamented lead vocal carries Minang verse over guitar, bass, drums and keyboard pads, with bamboo-flute and kettle-gong figures woven into introductions and fills.

items.name: Anime Phonk
items.lineage: Anime phonk connects phonk production with anime imagery, character themes and online montage culture. Producers combine forceful low bass and electronic rhythms with melodic or metallic hooks and edited vocal phrases, overlapping drift phonk, glitch production and Brazilian funk crossovers.
items.description: Heavy low bass and programmed beats drive sharp cowbell patterns, bright synthesizer figures and stuttering vocal cuts. Drops and repeated fragments provide abrupt changes of energy for club playback and anime montage edits.

items.name: Hypnosis
items.lineage: Hypnosis recordings developed alongside self-hypnosis teaching and guided suggestion, circulating through cassettes, downloads and practitioner podcasts. The listening field brings together spoken programmes, affirmations and accompanying relaxation music; voice-only and music-backed editions coexist.
items.description: A calmly paced voice directs attention through repeated phrases, pauses and suggestions. Some recordings use a musical bed, while others keep the spoken delivery unaccompanied. This representative voice-only branch leaves space around the words and avoids a fixed musical pulse.

items.name: Nanyin (Quanzhou southern chamber song)
items.lineage: Minnan chamber song and instrumental suite tradition of Quanzhou and southern Fujian, inscribed by UNESCO in 2009 and carried by amateur music associations across Taiwan and the Southeast Asian Minnan diaspora. A singer keeping time on paiban clappers leads the upper four instruments: horizontally held pipa, end-blown dongxiao, erxian fiddle and sanxian (the xiao card stands in for the dongxiao and the erhu card for the nanyin erxian).
items.description: Slow, ornamented Minnan-dialect song over a soft heterophonic ensemble of horizontal pipa, dongxiao, erxian and sanxian, with the singer marking time on paiban clappers. Instrumental suites alternate with sung pieces.
exemplars: Ocora: Nan-kouan, musique et chant courtois de la Chine du Sud, vols. 1-6 (Tsai Hsiao-yüeh)

items.name: Beiguan (Taiwanese temple ensemble and luantan theatre)
items.lineage: Loud ensemble and theatre music of Taiwan's Hoklo communities, also called luantan, transmitted by amateur clubs attached to temples, notably in Yilan and Changhua, and heard at temple festivals, processions and funerals. Its paizi suites set paired suona over drum, gongs and cymbals, while its theatre arias, sung in stylized guanhua, are accompanied by hard-bowed fiddles led by the coconut-shell kezaixian; clubs are divided between the rival xipi and fulu schools.
items.description: Blaring paired shawms over thundering drum, gongs and clashing cymbals in processional suites, alternating with high, nasal theatre singing carried by sharp hard-bowed fiddles and punctuated by the same percussion.
exemplars: Taiwan Music Institute (National Center for Traditional Arts) beiguan recordings

items.name: Jiangnan sizhu (Shanghai silk-and-bamboo ensemble)
items.lineage: Amateur chamber ensemble music of Shanghai and southern Jiangsu, cultivated since the late nineteenth century by music clubs meeting in teahouses and private rooms, and the subject of J. Lawrence Witzleben's study Silk and Bamboo Music in Shanghai. Its core repertoire, the 'eight great pieces' (ba da qu), is elaborated heterophonically by erhu, dizi or xiao, pipa, sanxian, yangqin and qinqin, with a small drum and clapper marking time.
items.description: Gentle, flowing heterophony in which fiddle, bamboo flute, plucked lutes and hammered dulcimer each ornament the same tune at once, often moving from a slow, spacious statement to faster, denser variations.
exemplars: China Record Corp. Jiangnan sizhu issues
Eight great pieces repertoire: Huanle ge, Yunqing, Xingjie, Sihe ruyi

items.name: Chaozhou xianshi (Teochew string ensemble)
items.lineage: String-ensemble branch of Chaozhou (Teochew) music of eastern Guangdong, played by amateur music clubs at home and in the Teochew diaspora of Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, and written in the local ersi notation. The high, hard-bowed touxian fiddle leads the Chaozhou zheng (here the guzheng card), yangqin, pipa, sanxian and lower fiddles such as the yehu and tihu, in modes such as qing sanliu, zhong sanliu and huowu that inflect particular scale degrees.
items.description: A bright, penetrating lead fiddle over plucked zither, lutes and hammered dulcimer, with bent, in-between scale degrees in some modes and pieces that accelerate from a measured opening to a brisk close.
exemplars: China Record Corp. Chaozhou string-ensemble issues
Hong Kong Chiu Chow music society recordings

items.name: Chaozhou daluogu (Teochew big gong-and-drum)
items.lineage: Large gong-and-drum branch of Chaozhou (Teochew) music, popular in the Chaoshan region of eastern Guangdong and the Teochew communities of Southeast Asia, and played both seated and in parades. The big-drum player leads and conducts the band, the gongs form its core and the suona carries the melody, with fiddles, zheng, yangqin, flute and cymbals in larger formations (the acoustic drum card stands in for the Chaozhou big drum).
items.description: A booming lead drum drives massed deep gongs and clashing cymbals through sudden stops, accelerations and loud-soft contrasts, with a shawm melody riding above the percussion.
exemplars: China Record Corp. Chaozhou gong-and-drum ensemble issues

items.name: Guangdong hanyue (Hakka Han music)
items.lineage: Instrumental ensemble music of the Hakka of Meizhou and Dabu in eastern Guangdong, traditionally said to preserve music brought south by Han migrants from the Central Plains and listed as national intangible heritage; wind-and-percussion bands serve rites and festivals. Its intimate sixian (silk-string) ensemble is led by the high touxian fiddle with the Hakka zheng (here the guzheng card), yangqin, pipa, sanxian and other fiddles, sometimes with the dongxiao (here the xiao card) and small percussion.
items.description: An elegant, measured string-and-flute ensemble: a reedy lead fiddle and end-blown bamboo flute over rippling zither, hammered dulcimer and plucked lutes, with restrained ornament and a steady pulse.
exemplars: China Record Corp. Guangdong hanyue issues

items.name: Xi'an guyue (Xi'an wind-and-percussion music)
items.lineage: Wind-and-percussion ensemble music kept by temple, village and urban music societies in and around Xi'an, inscribed by UNESCO in 2009 as the Xi'an wind and percussion ensemble and preserved in gongche-notated manuscript scores. Seated suites (zuoyue) and processional pieces (xingyue) set dizi, sheng and guanzi melody with yunluo gong-chimes against several drums, gongs and cymbals (the acoustic drum card stands in for its drums).
items.description: Stately wind melody on flute, mouth organ and reedy pipe, chimed by small tuned gongs, set against long passages of layered drumming and cymbals that swell and recede.
exemplars: China Record Corp. and Hugo releases of Xi'an guyue ensembles
Xi'an guyue societies in Stephen Jones's fieldwork

items.name: Zhihua Temple jingyin (Beijing Buddhist wind music)
items.lineage: Buddhist ritual wind-ensemble music of Beijing's Ming-dynasty Zhihua Temple, transmitted by monk-musicians in a lineage traced to the temple's founding and listed as national intangible heritage in 2006. Guanzi lead, with sheng, dizi and yunluo gong-chimes over drum and cymbals, playing suites from gongche-notated scores (the acoustic drum card stands in for the temple drum).
items.description: Slow, solemn suites in which the nasal, wailing double-reed pipe leads sustained mouth-organ chords and flute, with small gong-chimes, drum and cymbals marking sections.
exemplars: Buddhist Music of the Ming Dynasty (Zhihua Temple musicians)
University of Chicago CAEA digital archive: Capital Music of Zhihua Temple

items.name: Hebei yinyue hui (village shengguan ritual associations)
items.lineage: Amateur village ritual associations (yinyue hui) of central Hebei, south of Beijing, play shengguan wind music for funerals, calendrical rituals and temple fairs from gongche scores copied within each association; those of Qujiaying and Gaoluo are the best documented, and the form is listed as national intangible heritage. A guanzi leads, doubled by sheng and dizi with yunluo gong-chimes, over drum, cymbals and gongs (the acoustic drum card stands in for the association drum).
items.description: A wailing double-reed lead over the sustained chords of mouth organs and a flute, with gong-chimes, drum and cymbals; long, slow suites give way to brisker percussion-led sections.
exemplars: Gaoluo village ritual association (Stephen Jones fieldwork recordings)

items.name: Shaanbei chuishou (northern Shaanxi shawm bands)
items.lineage: Occupational shawm bands (chuishou) of northern Shaanxi around Yulin and Suide, hired for weddings, funerals and temple fairs; historically low-status and often family-based musicians, they are documented in Stephen Jones's Ritual and Music of North China, volume 2. A band pairs an upper and a lower suona over drum, cymbals and small gong, and recent bands also take up popular tunes.
items.description: Two blaring shawms, one high and one low, trade and interweave the melody over a driving drum, crashing cymbals and gong, loud and raw enough to carry across a village.
exemplars: Stephen Jones, Ritual and Music of North China, Vol. 2: Shaanbei

items.name: Luxinan guchui (south-west Shandong drum-and-shawm)
items.lineage: Drum-and-shawm music of south-western Shandong, centred on Heze and Jiaxiang, played by family bands for weddings, funerals and festivals and listed as national intangible heritage in 2006. Its suona playing is full of imitation, of birdsong and of the voices of local opera singers (kaqiang), over sheng, drum, gongs and cymbals; Ren Tongxiang of Jiaxiang carried the style to national stages from the 1950s.
items.description: A virtuosic, bright shawm lead full of bird calls, slides and voice-like inflections, backed by mouth-organ chords and a lively drum, gong and cymbal section.
exemplars: Ren Tongxiang — Bainiao chaofeng (China Record Corp.)

items.name: Liaoning guyue (north-east drum-and-shawm music)
items.lineage: Drum-and-shawm music of Liaoning in north-east China, strongest around Liaoyang, where Han-Wei tomb murals depict drum-and-wind players, and listed in 2006 in the first batch of national intangible heritage as Liaoning guyue. Family bands led by suona and guanzi, with drums, gongs and cymbals, play qupai suites and lighter tunes for weddings, funerals and festivals (the acoustic drum card stands in for the band drum).
items.description: Broad, ringing shawm melody over a steady drum, gongs and clashing cymbals, moving between long ceremonial suites and brisk, lighter tunes.
exemplars: Zhang Lianti and the Zhang family guyue band of Liaoyang
China Record Corp. Liaoning guyue issues

items.name: Shifan luogu (Wuxi-Suzhou gong-drum and wind ensemble)
items.lineage: Ensemble music of southern Jiangsu, centred on Wuxi and Suzhou and part of the wider sunan chuida family; pieces alternate and combine passages for winds and strings (dizi, sheng, erhu, pipa, sanxian) with elaborate passages for drums, gongs and cymbals, while the related shifan gu foregrounds the drum without gongs. Long played by Daoist musicians and amateur clubs for rites and festivities, it was transcribed and studied by the Wuxi-born musicologist Yang Yinliu and is listed as national intangible heritage.
items.description: Lyrical flute, mouth-organ and fiddle passages alternate with intricate, metrically patterned gong, drum and cymbal sections, the two textures sometimes joined in a dense tutti.
exemplars: China Record Corp. Shifan luogu issues

items.name: Naxi guyue (Lijiang Dongjing and Baisha xiyue)
items.lineage: Ancient music of the Naxi of Lijiang, Yunnan: Dongjing music, the hymn and scripture singing of lay Dongjing associations with instrumental qupai derived from Han Chinese ritual music, and Baisha xiyue, a suite that local tradition dates to the Yuan dynasty. Since the 1980s the Dayan Naxi Ancient Music Association has performed it for audiences, with voices accompanied by dizi, erhu-family fiddles, pipa, sanxian and yunluo gong-chimes (the generic bamboo-flute card stands in for the dizi).
items.description: Slow, dignified hymn-singing by a group of mostly elderly male voices in unison, wrapped in a gentle heterophony of flute, fiddles, plucked lutes and chiming small gongs.
exemplars: Nimbus Records: Naxi Music from Lijiang (Dayan Ancient Music Association)

items.name: Hakka bayin (Taiwanese Hakka eight-tone ensemble)
items.lineage: Wind-and-string ensemble of Taiwan's Hakka communities, notably in Miaoli and the Liudui area of Pingtung, hired for weddings, temple rites, festivals and funerals. A suona leads silk-and-bamboo instruments such as the erxian and panghu fiddles, sanxian, yangqin and flute over small percussion in qupai suites (the erhu card stands in for the Hakka fiddles); the Miaoli suona master Chen Qingsong led a renowned family troupe.
items.description: A bright, cutting shawm lead doubled by fiddles, plucked lute and hammered dulcimer, over a festive drum, gong and cymbal section.
exemplars: Chen Qingsong and the Chen family bayin troupe (Miaoli)
Taiwan Music Institute Hakka bayin recordings

items.name: Wudang daoyue (Wudang Mountains Daoist ritual music)
items.lineage: Ritual music of the Daoist temples of the Wudang Mountains in north-western Hubei, now chiefly of the Quanzhen order, listed as national intangible heritage in 2006. Priests chant and sing scriptures and hymns (jingyun) solo and in unison, paced by ritual percussion such as wooden fish, drum, cymbals and gong, with wind melody in larger rites.
items.description: Calm, unhurried priestly chanting, a leading priest answered by the assembly, paced by the knock of a wooden fish and punctuated by small cymbals, drum and gong.
exemplars: China Record Corp. recordings of Wudang Daoist music

items.name: Suzhou daojiao yinyue (Suzhou Zhengyi Daoist ritual music)
items.lineage: Ritual music of the Zhengyi Daoist priests of Suzhou, centred on the Xuanmiao Guan temple and listed as national intangible heritage. Sung hymns and recited scripture alternate with a large instrumental repertoire of wind-and-string qupai and gong-and-drum pieces, related to the region's Jiangnan sizhu and shifan luogu and played by the priests themselves.
items.description: Chanted and sung liturgy over the knock of a wooden fish, alternating with refined passages for flute, mouth organ, fiddle and gong-chimes and with crisp drum-led interludes.

items.name: Taiwanese daoshi ritual music (Zhengyi jiao and funeral rites)
items.lineage: Ritual music of Taiwan's Zhengyi (Celestial Master) Daoist priests (daoshi), who perform community jiao offering rites and funeral rites of merit, with the southern lineages of Tainan and the northern lineages of Hsinchu documented in detail by ethnographers. The high priest and his assistants chant and sing scripture in Minnan, keeping time with ritual percussion, while a hired ensemble of suona, drum, gong and cymbal players supplies qupai interludes.
items.description: Steady, insistent priestly chanting over a knocking wooden fish, broken by blasts of shawm with drum, gong and cymbals that mark each stage of the rite.
exemplars: Lu Chui-kuan's recordings and studies of Taiwanese Daoist ritual music

items.name: Hong Kong Quanzhen Daoist ritual music (jingyun chant)
items.lineage: Ritual music of the Quanzhen Daoist temples of Hong Kong, such as Ching Chung Koon in Tuen Mun, Fung Ying Sin Koon and the Yuen Yuen Institute, studied by Tsao Poon-yee (Tsao Pen-yeh) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong from 1984. Scripture tunes (jingyun) are recited, intoned, chanted and sung by the Daoist masters, the second and third masters keeping the rhythm on the muyu woodblock and the qing bowl (the temple-bells card stands in for the qing). Ching Chung Koon and Fung Ying Sin Koon have modified traditional practice by adding a silk-and-bamboo ensemble of yangqin, huqin and pipa (the erhu card stands in for the huqin).
items.description: Measured scripture chanting by the assembled masters, paced by the dry knock of the woodblock and the ring of a struck bowl, with a soft hammered-dulcimer, fiddle and lute ensemble shadowing the melody.
exemplars: Tsao Poon-yee field recordings of Quanzhen ritual, Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hong Kong Intangible Cultural Heritage inventory: Taoist ritual music

items.name: Wutaishan fojiao yinyue (Mount Wutai Buddhist music)
items.lineage: Temple music of the Buddhist monasteries of Mount Wutai in Shanxi, carried in two strands, the Han Chinese 'blue temple' (qingmiao) monasteries and the Tibetan-Mongolian 'yellow temple' (huangmiao) lamaseries, and entered on China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Beside the sung liturgy, monks play a northern wind-and-percussion ensemble led by the guanzi double-reed pipe with sheng mouth organ and dizi flute (the generic bamboo-flute card stands in for it), over the yunluo gong-chime, drum and cymbals, preserving old qupai melodies.
items.description: A reedy double-reed pipe leads slow ornamented melodies over held mouth-organ chords and flute, with the tinkle of a gong-chime and punctuating drum and cymbals; between pieces the monastic assembly chants in unison.
exemplars: China Record Corporation issues of Wutaishan Buddhist music

items.name: Fanbai (Han Chinese Buddhist liturgical chant)
items.lineage: Liturgical chant of Han Chinese Buddhist monasteries, sung by the assembled monks or nuns at the morning and evening services and in larger rites, with temples such as Kaiyuan Temple in Quanzhou documented on record. A precentor sets the pitch and the assembly answers in unison, the recitation paced by the muyu wooden fish and the qing bowl-bell (the temple-bells card stands in for the qing), with small hand cymbals in some rites.
items.description: Steady unison chanting by a monastic assembly over an unbroken wooden-fish pulse, with a struck bowl-bell marking phrase ends and slower melismatic hymns between the recitations.
exemplars: Ocora: Chine - Fanbai, chant liturgique bouddhique, leçon du soir au temple de Quanzhou (recorded by François Picard)

items.name: Jikong yue (Confucian temple ritual music)
items.lineage: Ceremonial music of the sacrifice to Confucius, performed at the Temple of Confucius in Qufu, Shandong, at the Taipei Confucius Temple and elsewhere, descended from the court yayue repertory of hymns sung at the ceremony. Slow hymn lines, one long note per syllable, are sung over ritual instruments of the 'eight sounds', among them bronze bells, stone chimes, qin and se zithers, xiao pipes, xun ocarina, sheng and drums, while dancers perform the ritual dance; the stone chimes and se have no card here.
items.description: Very slow, stately unison hymn in long syllabic notes, framed by struck bronze bells and drum strokes, with zither, end-blown pipe, ocarina and mouth organ doubling the line.
exemplars: Qufu Confucius Temple sacrificial ceremony recordings

items.name: Nuoxi (nuo ritual masked drama)
items.lineage: Music of nuo, the masked exorcistic ritual drama of southwest and central China, including the nuo rites of Guizhou, the dixi masked drama of Anshun and the Nanfeng nuo dances of Jiangxi, several of which entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Masked performers sing and chant in local dialect to gong and drum, with cymbals in many troupes; in Anshun dixi a single gong and drum accompany a lead singer whose line endings the group takes up.
items.description: Loud dialect singing and chant by masked performers over pounding drum and clanging gong, with group voices answering the leader at line ends and cymbal crashes driving the dance sections.
exemplars: Ethnographic field recordings of Anshun dixi and Guizhou nuo rites

items.name: Dongba jing (Naxi Dongba ritual chant)
items.lineage: Ritual recitation of the dongba priests of the Naxi people around Lijiang in Yunnan, who chant scriptures written in the Dongba pictographic script at funerals, sacrifices to heaven and rites of exorcism, and who also perform ritual dances; the Dongba manuscripts are on UNESCO's Memory of the World register. The priest chants solo or with fellow priests, marking the text on a drum and a hand bell (the hand-drum and temple-bells cards stand in for them).
items.description: Solo recitative chant on a narrow band of pitches, unfolding long ritual texts, punctuated by drum strokes and the shake of a bell.
exemplars: Field recordings of dongba scripture chanting in the Lijiang region

items.name: Bimo recitation (Nuosu Yi ritual chant)
items.lineage: Ritual recitation of the bimo, the hereditary priests of the Nuosu Yi in the Liangshan mountains of Sichuan, who chant from scriptures written in the Yi script at funerals, rites sending the dead to the ancestors, and purifications; bimo music as preserved in Meigu county, regarded as the centre of bimo culture, is on China's national intangible heritage list. The bimo recites while shaking a bronze ritual bell (the temple-bells card stands in for it).
items.description: Half-sung recitation by a solo priest, long text phrases on a few repeated pitches, with a shaken bell sounding through the chant.
exemplars: Liangshan Yi ethnographic recordings of bimo recitation

items.name: Ashiq and mazar chant (Uyghur Sufi devotional song)
items.lineage: Devotional singing of Uyghur Sufi practice in southern Xinjiang, documented in field recordings by Rachel Harris and Rahile Dawut. Wandering ashiq mendicants sing hikmet wisdom poems attributed to Ahmad Yasawi, and pilgrims gather for zikr and song at shrine (mazar) festivals such as Ordam near Kashgar; singers accompany themselves on the dap frame drum.
items.description: Impassioned high solo singing of mystical verse over a pounding jingle frame drum, rising into rhythmic group chanting at shrine gatherings.
exemplars: Rachel Harris and Rahile Dawut field recordings of ashiq singing and mazar festivals (SOAS)

items.name: Lisu four-part hymn singing (Nujiang church choirs)
items.lineage: Unaccompanied four-part hymn singing of Lisu Protestant congregations in the Nujiang valley of northwest Yunnan, a practice that grew from the early twentieth-century missions which also introduced the Fraser alphabet for writing Lisu. Village congregations and church choirs sing translated and locally made hymns in soprano, alto, tenor and bass parts.
items.description: A whole congregation singing strophic hymns in full four-part chordal harmony without instruments, open-voiced and unpolished.
exemplars: Field recordings of Nujiang Lisu church choirs

items.name: Gezaixi (Taiwanese opera)
items.lineage: Hokkien-language opera that took shape in the Yilan area of Taiwan in the early twentieth century from gezai song and local folk theatre, spread to southern Fujian and the Minnan diaspora, and is on China's national intangible heritage list (2006); it was recorded on 78s in the 1930s and later on radio and television. Its core accompaniment is the 'four pillars' of kezaixian coconut fiddle, daguangxian, yueqin and bamboo flute (the generic bamboo-flute card stands in for it), with gongs and cymbals for stage action, and its arias rest on the seven-character tune and the weeping tunes.
items.description: Plaintive Hokkien arias, often in weeping tunes, sung over a nasal coconut fiddle, a wood-topped fiddle, moon lute and flute, with gong and cymbal patterns cueing the stage action.
exemplars: 1930s Columbia Taiwan 78 rpm recordings of koa-a-hi

items.name: Budaixi (Hokkien glove-puppet theatre music)
items.lineage: Music of the glove-puppet theatre of southern Fujian and Taiwan, in which one master puppeteer voices every role while a band plays behind the stage; Fujian puppetry was placed on UNESCO's Register of Good Safeguarding Practices in 2012. Troupes used either the soft nanguan music or the loud beiguan music, the latter with suona shawm, drum, gongs and cymbals leading the action and the kezaixian fiddle, and Taiwan's twentieth-century 'golden light' style moved to recorded soundtracks, continued in the Pili productions.
items.description: One narrator switching voices for every character, from falsetto heroines to gruff villains, cut through by blaring shawm and fast gong, drum and cymbal patterns for fights and entrances.

items.name: Chaoju (Teochew opera)
items.lineage: Opera in the Teochew dialect of the Chaozhou-Shantou region of eastern Guangdong, descended from Ming-dynasty southern drama and carried to Hong Kong, Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia by the Teochew diaspora; it is on China's national intangible heritage list (2006). Singers keep the southern-drama practice of an offstage chorus (bangsheng) taking up line endings, over an orchestra led by the high touxian fiddle with coconut fiddle, yangqin and pipa, and a large gong-and-drum section headed by the drummer.
items.description: Bright, high-pitched dialect arias with an offstage chorus echoing line endings, over a shrill lead fiddle, hammered dulcimer and plucked lute, and a deep gong and drum section driving the stage action.
exemplars: China Record Corporation and Hong Kong Chiu Chow opera recordings

items.name: Liyuanxi (Quanzhou Pear Garden opera)
items.lineage: Minnan-language opera of Quanzhou, one of the oldest surviving descendants of Song and Yuan southern drama, with a refined, slow and highly codified movement style; it is on China's national intangible heritage list (2006). It is sung to nanyin music: the nanyin instruments, pipa, sanxian, dongxiao and erxian, with paiban clappers accompany the singers, while the drummer leads on the nangu, pressing a foot on the drumhead to bend its pitch, and the small aizai shawm marks set pieces. The xiao, erhu and suona cards stand for the dongxiao, erxian and aizai.
items.description: Slow, finely ornamented Minnan arias over a soft heterophony of plucked lutes, end-blown flute and fiddle, with clappers keeping time and a pitch-bending drum steering the pace.
exemplars: China Record Corporation recordings of the Quanzhou Liyuan opera troupe

items.name: Gaojiaxi (Gaojia opera of southern Fujian)
items.lineage: Minnan-language opera of Quanzhou, Xiamen and Jinjiang that grew from 'Song Jiang' processional plays of the Ming and Qing into a full theatre famed for its comic chou roles, including clowns who mimic marionettes; it is on China's national intangible heritage list (2006) and is performed in Taiwan and the Minnan communities of Southeast Asia. Its music joins nanyin-derived arias with livelier puppet-theatre and beiguan tunes, accompanied by a shawm, drum, gong and cymbal section alongside pipa and fiddle.
items.description: Lively dialect singing and comic patter over shawm and a busy gong, drum and cymbal section, alternating with gentler lute-and-fiddle accompanied arias.
exemplars: China Record Corporation recordings of Gaojia opera

items.name: Puxianxi (Puxian / Xinghua opera)
items.lineage: Opera of Putian and Xianyou in Fujian, sung in the Puxian (Xinghua) dialect and counted among the oldest living descendants of Song and Yuan southern drama, keeping a large repertory of qupai tunes and gong-and-drum patterns; it is on China's national intangible heritage list (2006). The accompaniment is led by the drum, with double-reed shawms (the suona card stands in for them) and gongs and cymbals.
items.description: Archaic dialect arias set to fixed tunes, framed by shawm melodies and a drum-led gong and cymbal section playing set patterns.

items.name: Minju (Fuzhou opera)
items.lineage: Opera of Fuzhou sung in the Fuzhou dialect, formed in the late Qing and early Republic when the Rulin, Pingjiang and Jianghu troupe traditions merged; it is on China's national intangible heritage list (2006). Its music draws on the jianghu tunes, yangge, douqiang and folk xiaodiao, accompanied by bowed fiddles, flute and suona with a gong-and-drum section; the erhu card stands for its huqin fiddles and the generic bamboo-flute card for its flute.
items.description: Fuzhou-dialect arias, now lyrical and now brisk, over fiddle and flute with shawm for set pieces and gong and drum cueing the action.
exemplars: China Record Corporation recordings of Fuzhou Min opera

items.name: Kuileixi (Quanzhou string-marionette theatre music)
items.lineage: Music of the Quanzhou string-marionette theatre of southern Fujian, kept by the Quanzhou Marionette Troupe; Fujian puppetry was placed on UNESCO's Register of Good Safeguarding Practices in 2012. Its kuilei tunes, a body of melodies distinct from nanyin, are sung in the Quanzhou dialect, accompanied by the nangu drum pressed by the drummer's foot to change pitch, the zhengluo gong peculiar to the genre and the small aizai shawm (the drum, gong and suona cards stand for them).
items.description: Archaic dialect singing over a pitch-bending drum and a bright small gong, with a small shawm piercing through ceremonial passages.

items.name: Jinju (Shanxi Zhonglu bangzi opera)
items.lineage: Bangzi clapper opera of central Shanxi, also called Zhonglu bangzi, which grew out of Puzhou bangzi in the Qing dynasty around Taiyuan and the Jinzhong merchant towns and spread with Shanxi traders and migrants to Inner Mongolia, northern Shaanxi and Hebei; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Its string section is led by the 'four great pieces': the huhu bamboo-tube lead fiddle (the erhu card stands in), the erguxian fiddle (the banhu card stands in), sanxian and the four-string sihu (no card here), while drum, bangzi woodblock clappers (the paiban card stands in), cymbals and gongs mark the beat types and the stage action.
items.description: High, ringing Shanxi-dialect arias in bangzi beat types, carried by a piercing bamboo-tube fiddle doubled by a gutty wood-faced fiddle and sanxian, with the dry crack of woodblock clappers and clanging gongs and cymbals punctuating each phrase.
exemplars: China Record Corporation jinju recordings of Ding Guoxian

items.name: Hebei bangzi (Hebei clapper opera)
items.lineage: Bangzi clapper opera of Hebei, Beijing and Tianjin, which took shape in the nineteenth century when Shanxi and Shaanxi bangzi was taken up in the Zhili region and was earlier called Zhili bangzi or Jing bangzi; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Its arias are sung high and full-voiced over the wood-faced banhu fiddle in its Hebei form, while bangu drum, bangzi woodblock clappers (the paiban card stands in), cymbals and gongs drive the beat types and the stage action.
items.description: Bright, high-pitched, full-throated arias with sharp rising cries over the nasal bite of the wood-faced banhu fiddle, with woodblock clappers, drum, gongs and cymbals marking the beat types.
exemplars: China Record Corporation Hebei bangzi recordings

items.name: Lüju (Shandong opera)
items.lineage: Shandong regional opera that grew in the early twentieth century in the Guangrao and Boxing area of the Yellow River delta, when performers of Shandong qinshu narrative singing began to act out their stories in costume; it later centred on Jinan and entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2008. Its lead instrument is the zhuiqin bowed lute (the zhuihu card in its qinshu setting), joined by yangqin, sanxian, pipa and erhu.
items.description: Gentle, speech-close Shandong-dialect singing in a lilting folk-song style, the zhuiqin's sliding bowed line shadowing the voice over the bright patter of hammered dulcimer and plucked sanxian and pipa.

items.name: Errenzhuan (Northeast duet song-and-dance)
items.lineage: Duet song-and-dance theatre of northeast China (Liaoning, Jilin and Heilongjiang), in which a clown-role man and a dan-role woman sing, talk, joke and dance with fans and handkerchiefs; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006 and reached national audiences through television and commercial theatres. The banhu fiddle leads, with suona, while the performers snap hand-held clappers (yuzi and bamboo boards; the paiban card in its kuaiban form stands in).
items.description: Fast, bantering duet singing in northeastern dialect, the man and woman trading lines, jokes and spoken asides over a bright, nasal banhu and a wailing suona, with hand clappers snapping out the rhythm of the dance.
exemplars: Zhao Benshan's Liu Laogen Grand Stage errenzhuan theatre (Shenyang)

items.name: Errentai (Inner Mongolian and north Shanxi duet song-drama)
items.lineage: Two-person song-drama of the Han communities of western Inner Mongolia, northern Shanxi, northern Shaanxi and the Zhangjiakou area of Hebei, which grew from local folk song and dance and the songs of migrants who went 'beyond the West Pass' to the grasslands; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. A clown and a dan sing and dance to the 'old three pieces' of sihu four-string fiddle, mei bamboo flute (the dizi card) and yangqin, with the performers' bamboo clappers (sikuaiwa; the paiban card in its kuaiban form stands in), and instrumental paiziqu tunes open and link the scenes.
items.description: Lively duet singing in local dialect, man and woman trading verses and dance steps over a buzzing four-string fiddle, a shrill bamboo flute and rippling hammered dulcimer, with clicking bamboo clappers; brisk instrumental tunes open and link the scenes.
exemplars: Zou Xikou (Going Beyond the West Pass), errentai repertoire piece
Inner Mongolia audio-visual publishing errentai recordings

items.name: Huju (Shanghai opera)
items.lineage: Shanghai-dialect opera that grew from the tanhuang folk-song and story-singing of the Shanghai countryside, known in turn as huaguxi, bentan and shenqu, and took the name Huju in 1941; through the twentieth century it specialised in modern-dress plays of city life and entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Its lead fiddle is a bamboo-tube erhu (the erhu card stands in), joined by pipa, yangqin, sanxian and bamboo flute, with clappers for the beat.
items.description: Soft, conversational Shanghai-dialect singing close to speech, the bamboo-tube fiddle tracing the voice over plucked pipa and sanxian and a rippling hammered dulcimer, with clappers keeping a steady, unhurried beat.

items.name: Xiju (Wuxi opera)
items.lineage: Opera of southern Jiangsu sung in the Wu dialects of Wuxi and Changzhou, which grew from the tanhuang story-singing and folk song of the two cities, merged as Changxi wenxi in the early twentieth century and was renamed Xiju in the 1950s; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2008. Its accompaniment centres on the erhu, with bamboo flute, pipa, yangqin and sanxian.
items.description: Sweet, lyrical Wu-dialect singing in flowing tanhuang tunes, the erhu shadowing the voice with bamboo flute, pipa and hammered dulcimer in soft heterophony over a measured beat.

items.name: Huaiju (Huai opera)
items.lineage: Opera of northern Jiangsu sung in the Jianghuai dialect of Yancheng and Huai'an, which grew in the Qing dynasty from local xianghuo ritual drama and mentanci door-to-door songs and was carried to Shanghai by migrants from the region, where much of its twentieth-century development took place; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2008. Its arias rest on the huaidiao, ladiao and ziyoudiao tune families, led by a huqin fiddle (the erhu card stands in) with pipa, yangqin, drum and gong.
items.description: Plaintive, full-voiced Jianghuai-dialect singing, often in long laments, carried by a bright lead fiddle with pipa and hammered dulcimer and punctuated by drum and gong.

items.name: Shaoju (Shaoxing luantan opera)
items.lineage: Shaoxing luantan opera of eastern Zhejiang, sung in Shaoxing dialect, renamed Shaoju in the 1950s and best known for its Monkey King plays, one of which was filmed in 1960; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Its erfan tunes are led by the banhu fiddle with the douzi supporting it, while the sanwuqi, yanglu and xilu tunes are led by bamboo flute; the traditional six-man band of drum-and-clappers, two wind players, sanxian, cymbals and small gong, plus a big gong, was enlarged with sheng, pipa and zhonghu from the mid-1950s.
items.description: Bold, high-pitched Shaoxing-dialect singing with forceful, declamatory delivery over loud gongs, drums and cymbals; some arias ride a wood-faced banhu fiddle, others are carried by bamboo flute.
exemplars: Sun Wukong San Da Baigujing (1960 Shaoju film with Liu Lingtong)

items.name: Hanju (Hubei Han opera)
items.lineage: Pihuang opera of Hubei centred on Wuhan, whose xipi and erhuang tunes (handiao) developed along the Han River; Han troupes joined Anhui troupes in Beijing in the early nineteenth century and contributed to the formation of Beijing opera. It entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. A high huqin fiddle leads (the erhu card stands in), with moon lute and sanxian, while drum, gong and cymbals cue the stage action.
items.description: Declamatory and lyrical Hubei-dialect arias alternating xipi and erhuang modes, led by a sharp, high fiddle over plucked moon lute and sanxian, with drum, gong and cymbals cueing every entrance.

items.name: Xiangju (Changsha Hunan opera)
items.lineage: Opera of Changsha and eastern Hunan sung in Changsha dialect, which combines several tune systems: gaoqiang high tunes, sung over percussion with a helping chorus taking up the line endings, kunqiang, dipaizi qupai tunes, and tanqiang (nanlu and beilu, kin to erhuang and xipi) accompanied by strings; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. A huqin fiddle (the erhu card stands in) leads the tanqiang with moon lute and sanxian, and drum, gong and cymbals carry the high tunes.
items.description: Changsha-dialect arias that move between high tunes sung over pounding gongs and drums with a chorus taking up the line endings, and string-accompanied arias led by a bright fiddle with plucked moon lute.

items.name: Huaguxi (Hunan flower-drum opera)
items.lineage: Folk opera of Hunan that grew from flower-drum song-and-dance by a clown and a dan, the 'two-small' plays, later joined by a young male role in 'three-small' plays, with many local branches of which the Changsha branch is best known; it entered China's national intangible heritage list in 2006. Its music draws on chuandiao, daluoqiang, paizi and xiaodiao folk tunes, led by the datong big-tube fiddle, with suona and a gong-and-drum section.
items.description: Bright, bouncy duet singing in Hunan dialect, a clown and a dan bantering over the nasal, sliding tone of the big-tube fiddle, with gong-and-drum interludes and suona in the dance tunes.
